name: FSMap: monitor-owned map of all file systems
why: Monitor-owned map; the C++ MDS never subscribes to `fsmap` and only shapes it through beacons, so there is nothing to implement; mgr, tools, cephfs-mirror and libcephfs keep reading it from the unmodified mon.
risk: Its content (states, addrs, metadata, compat) is only as correct as the Rust beacons (F-CLU-021, F-CLU-025).

name: MDSMap: per-file-system map and its wire encoding
why: Every Rust daemon must decode the MDSMap the mon sends to drive its own state and its view of peer ranks; clients get the map from the mon, never from the MDS.
subset: Decode the current encoding only (MMDSMap v2, MDSMap struct_v 5 / ev 20, mds_info_t v10, unknown trailing fields skipped by length) and use in/up/failed/stopped/damaged, mds_info (gid, name, rank, inc, state, addrs, laggy_since), flags (REFUSE_CLIENT_SESSION, ALLOW_SNAPS, ALLOW_STANDBY_REPLAY), session_timeout/autoclose, max_xattr_size, required_client_features, pools, compat, fs_name, last_failure_osd_epoch; tolerate balancer and qdb fields. Per-connection re-encoding for old peers is legacy; forwarding maps to peer ranks is free (Rust-only MDS-to-MDS).

name: Epoch model: FSMap, MDSMap and standby epochs, null map
why: Beacons must carry the right epoch (standby_epochs[gid] as a standby, the fs MDSMap epoch once attached) and maps must be applied in order, dropping non-newer ones; every beacon that reaches prepare_beacon bumps the MDSMap epoch pushed to all clients of the fs.
risk: Changing health text or flapping states produce an MDSMap epoch per beacon to every mounted client (map churn).

name: Map subscriptions and the MDS view of mdsmap (null maps)
why: The mon serves the MDS view of `mdsmap` only to an MDS-type session whose address vector equals the recorded mds_info addrs (the beacon source), and signals removal with a null map of epoch UINT32_MAX (beacon-and-monitor 3.17 items 1, 3, 9).
risk: Applying the UINT32_MAX null-map epoch without restarting stalls every later beacon in PaxosService::dispatch; subscribing from another messenger identity yields no MDS view.

name: FSMapUser: file system name directory for clients
why: Mon-to-client name directory used by kclient `mds_namespace=` and libcephfs `client_fs`; the MDS never uses it, so mounts by fs name keep working with nothing to implement.

name: Kernel client partial MDSMap decode
why: Kernel-side decoding of the mon-encoded MDSMap; nothing to implement, but it fixes constraints: every mds_info needs a msgr2 address (F-CLU-109), entries with state <= 0 (creating, starting, standby-replay) are invisible, reconnect is sent at state >= 10 and new requests only at >= ACTIVE.
subset: Kernels mounted without ms_mode select the v1 address, which the MDS publishes (decision 3).
risk: Ranks must stay contiguous (array bounded by size(in)); the mon keeps them so, `mds rmfailed` breaks it.
override: Decision 3 (2026-10-11): a basic msgr1 listener for kernel clients is P0, so kernels mounted without ms_mode (Rook's default requireMsgr2=false for ceph-csi, the old device syntax, ms_mode=legacy) work unchanged.

name: libcephfs map use and mount availability check
why: libcephfs, ceph-fuse and Ganesha decode the mon's map themselves; the Rust MDS's obligations are indirect: keep beacons flowing (ceph-fuse refuses mounts while any up rank is laggy) and honour REFUSE_CLIENT_SESSION and session_autoclose semantics (sessions category).

name: FSMap filtering for file-system-restricted sessions
why: Mon-side filtering of the FSMap for fs-restricted sessions (subscriptions, read-only commands); no MDS involvement.

name: FSMap sanity invariants enforced by the monitor
why: Monitor-internal assertions on committed FSMaps; valid beacons cannot violate them and there is nothing for the Rust MDS to implement.
risk: Operator sequences (fs compat add_incompat with a standby-replay attached, fs reset with a follower) can still abort the mon; Rust runbooks should avoid them.

name: Multiple file systems: enable_multiple and the default file system
why: enable_multiple and the default fscid are mon state used by unqualified client subscriptions and role parsing; no MDS involvement.
subset: Deprecated alias `fs set_default` is legacy.

name: Data pool list of a file system
why: The MDS must validate layout pools (create with layout, setlayout, setdirlayout) against the MDSMap data_pools after waiting for the client's map epoch; clients use the same list for statfs and layout ioctls.
risk: Validating against a stale map gives EINVAL for a pool just added with `fs add_data_pool` (F-CLU-060).

name: max_file_size published in the MDSMap
why: Clients enforce max_file_size from the mon's map (kclient, libcephfs); the C++ MDS only decodes it and performs no size check.
subset: Decode and ignore; no MDS-side check.

name: Mirroring metadata (MirrorInfo) in the FSMap
why: MirrorInfo lives in the FSMap, is edited by mon commands and read by cephfs-mirror; the MDS never reads it, and mirroring itself comes with P1 snapshots (D8).

name: CompatSet encoding and the MDS incompat feature ids
why: Every beacon carries a CompatSet whose incompat mask the unmodified mon uses to freeze the daemon's compat and to decide fs eligibility; it is the only mon-enforced way to keep C++ and Rust daemons out of each other's file systems (constraint 3).
subset: Encode CompatSet exactly (three u64 masks, bit 0 cleared on the wire, a name for every set bit, ids 1..63). Advertise one constant Rust set: incompat 7 (forced by the mon, F-CLU-016) plus a private Rust format bit N (13..63, ideally reserved upstream) and none of the C++ format bits 1-6, 8-12. C++ feature semantics (inline data, omap dirfrags, anchor table, ...) are out.
risk: If the Rust set contains bit 1 (or all C++ default bits) a Rust standby is eligible for any upgradeable C++ fs (one rank, no standby-replay) and gets promoted into it, merging N; if the Rust fs compat lacks N, C++ standbys can take Rust ranks.
question: Decide the compat strategy. Recommended: {7, N} without bit 1. Cost: `fs new` (mgr/volumes `fs volume create`, Rook CephFilesystem) copies default_compat (C++ bits), so no Rust daemon is eligible until the new fs compat is edited while no rank is up (`fs compat <fs> rm_incompat` 1-6, 8-12, add N), or default_compat is stripped once with the deprecated `mds compat rm_incompat` (pure-Rust clusters only). Alternatives: also advertise the C++ bits (zero-touch, unsafe in mixed clusters) or ask for a small mon/mgr change.

name: Standby eligibility by compat set
why: Eligibility filters run in the unmodified mon (a standby must hold every incompat bit of the fs; extra bits only while the fs is upgradeable); with the compat of F-CLU-014 they keep C++ daemons out of Rust file systems (no N) and Rust daemons out of C++ ones (no bit 1).
risk: Scoring and mds_join_fs (F-CLU-030, F-CLU-031) only rank candidates; only these filters prevent cross-assignment.

name: Forced INLINE incompat bit and compat bootstrap
why: The mon inserts incompat 7 into every stored daemon compat at boot, so a Rust daemon whose beacons omit bit 7 is evicted (blocklisted if ranked) at its first beacon that needs a proposal.
subset: Always send bit 7 with a name. The empty-compat bootstrap and pre-v10 decode defaults are old-daemons legacy. Advertising bit 7 does not mean inline data support (D12: inline data OUT).
risk: The eviction can fire long after boot, e.g. when a promoted daemon first reports leaving up:replay.

name: Compat set must not change after boot
why: The mon compares the compat masks of each state-changing beacon with the boot-time compat and fails the daemon on any difference (beacon-and-monitor 3.17 item 7).
risk: A Rust upgrade that adds a format bit must restart the process (new gid), never change compat inside one identity.

name: Upgradeable file systems and compat merge on promotion
why: Mon-side rule: a daemon with extra incompat bits may join only an upgradeable fs and then merges its bits permanently; with F-CLU-014 this is how N enters a fresh Rust fs and how later Rust format bits roll out through cephadm/Rook's max_mds=1, standby-replay-off upgrade choreography.
subset: The C++ cross-release merge path is old-daemons legacy; for Rust it is the future format-upgrade path.
question: Plan Rust on-disk format evolution as new private incompat bits merged this way (needs the fs upgradeable: one rank in, standby-replay off).

name: fs compat and mds compat commands
why: Mon commands only; with the recommended compat strategy `fs compat <fs> rm_incompat/add_incompat` is the operator step that makes a new fs Rust-only while no rank is up.
subset: Deprecated `mds compat show/rm_compat/rm_incompat` (default_compat) are legacy; at most a one-time default_compat strip in a pure-Rust cluster (F-CLU-014 question).
risk: `fs compat add_*` with id >= 64 aborts the monitor; adding an incompat bit while a standby-replay daemon is attached trips FSMap::sanity.

name: mds_features in the boot beacon and get_up_features
why: The boot beacon must carry a u64 mds_features; the mon stores and dumps it (`features` in fs dump) but nothing interprets it.
subset: Send a constant mask (e.g. the msgr feature bits the Rust messenger supports). Choosing encodings by the AND over ranks (get_up_features) is C++ mixed-version legacy and out.
question: Rust-to-Rust rolling upgrades with mixed versions across ranks need their own version gating (P1 design item).

name: MMDSBeacon message and the beacon sender thread
why: The beacon is the MDS's only control channel to the unmodified mon (liveness, wanted state, last epoch, compat, health, affinity); it must be MMDSBeacon v8 with the full field order, sent about every 4 s from a context that metadata work cannot block.
subset: Vestigial standby_for_* and standby_replay fields are sent as constants; v6/v7 decoding is mon-side legacy.
risk: A health metric of type 0 (MDS_HEALTH_NULL) asserts in the mon's decoder and aborts the monitor.

name: Monitor beacon admission rules
why: The Rust daemon must satisfy every admission rule (mon cap `mds x`, correct fsid, nonzero source port, strictly increasing seq, `version` equal to its effective epoch) or its state requests and health are silently ignored.
risk: A `version` above the committed epoch stalls the beacon in PaxosService::dispatch; an old seq or a repeated up:boot is not counted as liveness and leads to removal.

name: Beacon acks and MDS-side lagginess (self-fencing deferral)
why: Partly inherent safety rule: a daemon with no beacon ack for mds_beacon_grace may already be replaced, so it must stop answering clients and peers (it could otherwise keep renewing caps and serving stale reads) until the mon answers; messages are delayed, not dropped.
subset: Keep: defer all client/peer work while acks are missing, do not serve before the first ack, suppress session staleness right after. Process acks on a path independent of metadata work (the C++ false-laggy coupling to mds_lock disappears).
risk: Blocklisting fences only writes; without self-fencing a partitioned old holder can still answer reads and renewals from cache.

name: Heartbeat-gated beacons (internal watchdog)
why: The mon fails over only daemons that stop beaconing, so a wedged-but-alive Rust daemon must stop beaconing; the liveness signal must reflect real progress of the metadata engine (workers, journal commits), not just the beacon thread.
risk: Long recovery scans without progress signals cause false failovers that restart recovery (resolve-and-rejoin 3.20).

name: Boot registration as a standby with daemon metadata
why: The up:boot beacon registers the daemon in the shared standby pool and its sys_info becomes `mds metadata`/`ceph versions`, which mgr (list_servers, prometheus), cephadm (upgrade version check, stray detection) and Rook (upgrade detection) parse; want_state stays up:boot until the map shows up:standby.
risk: Rook compares each MDS `ceph_version` (`ceph version X.Y.Z`, build, commit id) with the image's `ceph --version`: a lower version or another commit id makes every reconcile rerun the MDS upgrade sequence (max_mds 1, pods scaled down), and an unparsable or missing string makes every reconcile fail.
question: Which version string does the Rust MDS report? It must equal the bundled Ceph CLI's `ceph --version` exactly to satisfy Rook and cephadm.

name: Unique daemon names
why: On boot the mon fails (and blocklists, if ranked) any existing daemon with the same name, so a restarted Rust daemon must reuse its configured name to fence its predecessor at once (Rook node loss, respawn) and refuse empty or digit-leading ids that mon commands parse as ranks or gids.

name: DNE beacon on clean shutdown
why: cephadm and Rook stop MDS daemons with SIGTERM and their waits only watch the FSMap; the DNE beacon (sent, ack awaited about 1 s) makes the mon fail the rank immediately instead of after mds_beacon_grace (15-20 s outage per restart).
risk: Each clean exit of a rank holder blocklists its addresses for a day (harmless: new nonce per process).

name: Health metrics carried in beacons
why: Beacons carry the daemon's health metrics, which the mon turns into health checks (F-ADM-073) and uses to gate `mds fail`, `fs fail` and `fs set max_mds` (F-ADM-083).
subset: MDSHealth v1 with known metric ids 1..17 only, never 0; standbys send none; keep message texts stable (a changing text costs an MDSMap epoch per beacon to all clients). Which metrics are P0 is decided in F-ADM-073.
risk: Metric type 0 aborts the monitor's decoder.

name: Monitor-side laggy detection and its protections
why: Laggy marking and replacement are done by the unmodified mon from beacon timestamps; the Rust part is F-CLU-021/024 (beacons within the mon's mds_beacon_grace from every state, including long replay and stopping).
risk: A laggy holder without an eligible standby is never replaced and ceph-fuse refuses new mounts meanwhile; the mon uses its own mds_beacon_grace, so read the option from the same config.

name: Standby selection scoring
why: Standby scoring runs in the mon; the Rust daemon only supplies its join_fs (F-CLU-031) and addresses.
risk: Ranking is not prevention: a lower-scored eligible standby is still used, so only compat (F-CLU-014, F-CLU-015) separates C++ and Rust daemons.

name: mds_join_fs file system affinity
why: cephadm sets mds_join_fs=<service_id> and Rook sets mds_join_fs=<fs> for every MDS, and the mon uses the beacon `fs` field for scoring and affinity swaps; the daemon must read the option (mon config DB) on every beacon.

name: Per-file-system selection flags: refuse_standby_for_another_fs and host anti-affinity
why: refuse_standby_for_another_fs and host anti-affinity (default on) are mon-side selection policies; nothing to implement in the MDS.
question: Recommend setting refuse_standby_for_another_fs on every fs of a mixed C++/Rust cluster as defence in depth next to compat (cephadm and Rook always set mds_join_fs).

name: Affinity-driven swaps of healthy daemons
why: The mon may fail over a healthy active or standby-replay daemon whose affinity is worse than an available standby's; the Rust MDS only handles an ordinary failover (F-CLU-035, F-CLU-036, F-CLU-080).
risk: Causes failovers of healthy actives in default cephadm/Rook deployments, so cold takeover must be routine and fast.

name: Failed-rank and laggy-holder replacement
why: Failed-rank promotion and laggy-holder replacement are mon policy; the Rust part is entering up:replay (F-CLU-035, F-CLU-037, F-CLU-066).
risk: With defaults, detection to promotion takes 15-20 s plus a Paxos commit, and only an available standby enables replacement.

name: Promotion into a rank and the initial rank state
why: The mon alone assigns ranks and the entry state and the daemon cannot refuse: the Rust MDS must implement up:creating, up:starting, up:replay (also from standby-replay), up:standby-replay (tolerated, F-CLU-039) and up:stopping (beacon-and-monitor 3.17 item 8).
risk: The promotion epoch becomes the rank's inc, which must be adopted (F-CLU-038).

name: Fencing failed rank holders with OSD blocklists
why: Fencing a failed rank holder is the mon's OSD blocklist of every address in the beaconed address vector (exact nonce); D9 makes fencing P0 and the Rust daemon must treat -EBLOCKLISTED as loss of identity (stop serving, restart with a new nonce).
risk: Every RADOS operation must leave through the messenger whose addresses are beaconed; separate librados/Objecter instances with other nonces (tempting for per-core parallelism) are not fenced and break single-writer safety.
question: Confirm the RADOS client design keeps one fenced identity (optionally adding per-shard ownership epochs checked OSD-side).

name: Wait for last_failure_osd_epoch before touching rank objects
why: A daemon taking over a failed rank must not read or write any rank or shard object before its OSDMap epoch reaches last_failure_osd_epoch, so that the old holder is already fenced at the OSDs (F-STORE-042).
risk: The unmodified mon can overwrite last_failure_osd_epoch with 0 (standby-replay removal, `fs fail` in gid order), and the C++ MDS does not wait in up:creating/up:starting (README observation 12).
question: Defence in depth: wait for the latest OSDMap in every entry state and guard journal/shard writes with an ownership epoch checked on the OSD side?

name: Rank incarnation
why: inc distinguishes successive holders of a rank: it must be the OSD client incarnation so OSD duplicate detection never confuses two holders' requests; libcephfs treats an inc change as a restart and peer ranks use it to detect restarted ranks.

name: Standby-replay assignment
why: D9 defers standby-replay to P1, but Rook runs `fs set <fs> allow_standby_replay true` for every CephFilesystem with activeStandby (the mgr rook module creates them with activeStandby=True), and the mon then attaches standbys as followers that cannot refuse.
subset: Accept up:standby-replay: beacon that state and request nothing else, keep no warm state if desired (cold follower), and on promotion run a normal cold replay (F-CLU-069). Warm following is F-CLU-068 (P1).
risk: Never report down:damaged from a follower: the mon then blocklists the healthy active and marks the rank damaged, and if the followed rank is not up it terminates the leader monitor.
question: D9 vs the Rook default: confirm that P0 tolerates the assignment (a follower still counts for ok-to-stop and Rook's liveness probe).

name: Growing the number of active ranks (max_mds)
why: Growth towards max_mds is mon-driven, one rank at a time; the Rust parts are up:creating/up:starting (F-CLU-064, F-CLU-065) and placing shards on the new rank (D6).

name: Shrinking: monitor-driven up:stopping and FSMap::stop
why: The mon sets the highest active rank to up:stopping when in > max_mds and removes it on down:stopped; cephadm and Rook upgrades rely on it (max_mds 1); the Rust part is the drain of F-CLU-102.
risk: Only rank in-1 is stopped and only when up:active; after STOPPED the mon answers with a null map and the daemon must leave (F-CLU-057).

name: fs new
why: `fs new` runs unmodified from mgr/volumes, cephadm and Rook and promotes standbys to up:creating for ranks 0..max_mds-1; the Rust part is up:creating (F-CLU-064).
subset: `--recover` (rank 0 replays existing metadata) only matters for disaster recovery.
question: With the recommended compat (F-CLU-014) the new fs gets default_compat and no Rust daemon is eligible until its compat is edited: choose an operator/automation step, a one-time default_compat strip, or an upstream `fs new` change.

name: fs rm
why: Mon command used by mgr/volumes and Rook to delete a fs once no rank is up; no MDS involvement.

name: fs fail and the joinable flag
why: `fs fail` and joinable are mon state changes used by cephadm (fail_fs upgrades) and Rook; Rust daemons only see removal (F-CLU-057) or fencing (F-CLU-036).
subset: Deprecated `cluster_down` alias is legacy.
risk: `fs fail` erases daemons in gid order, so a follower can reset last_failure_osd_epoch to 0 (F-CLU-037).

name: fs reset
why: Disaster-recovery command, normally used after C++ offline tools (out by D2): it resets the fs compat to default_compat and makes rank 0 replay with every other rank stopped.
subset: If supported: define rank-0 adoption of all shards and re-apply the Rust compat.
risk: After `fs reset` no Rust daemon is eligible until the compat is edited again (F-CLU-014).

name: fs set down
why: `fs set down` is mon state (max_mds 0, later restored); the Rust parts are stopping (F-CLU-102, where the last rank evicts and blocklists all clients) and up:starting on `down false` (F-CLU-065).

name: fs rename and fs swap
why: Rename and swap of offline file systems are mon state changes made while no Rust daemon is attached.
risk: Never persist fs_name or fscid in the Rust on-disk format; take them from the MDSMap (auth caps fsname=, metrics labels).

name: mds fail
why: `mds fail` is used by operators, cephadm and Rook (standby-replay cleanup); the mon blocklists and replaces a holder, and the Rust daemon just leaves (F-CLU-057, F-CLU-105).

name: Damaged ranks and mds repaired
why: The mon handles a down:damaged report (blocklist the holder, rank to damaged, MDS_DAMAGE) and `mds repaired`; the Rust part is deciding when to report it (F-CLU-104).
risk: A damaged rank is out of service until an operator acts; D10 prefers per-shard containment.

name: Hidden and debug rank commands: mds rm, rmfailed, freeze, set_state
why: Hidden debug and repair commands (mds rm, rmfailed, freeze, set_state) edit mon records without MDS involvement.
risk: `mds set_state` can push an invalid state: the Rust daemon must validate assigned states and restart rather than misbehave (F-CLU-054).

name: Read-only fs and mds commands and the fs dump layout
why: fs dump, fs get and mds stat are produced by the mon from beacon data and parsed by cephadm (`up:active`), Rook (fs get, liveness probe on fs dump names), prometheus and dashboard; the Rust part is correct names, states and addrs.
subset: Deprecated `mds compat show` is legacy.

name: Orchestration helpers: mds ok-to-stop, last-seen, metadata, versions
why: ok-to-stop, last-seen, metadata and versions are answered by the mon from the FSMap and boot metadata and used by cephadm and Rook; nothing to implement beyond accurate states and sys_info (F-CLU-025).

group: Rank state machine and map handling
name: Daemon and rank states: numeric values and names
why: Beacons, the mon, both clients and every tool use the numeric state values and their `up:*`/`down:*` names; the kernel ignores entries with state <= 0.
subset: Value -9 (replayonce) is dead code.

group: Rank state machine and map handling
name: State transition validation on both sides
why: The mon evicts (blocklisting rank holders) a daemon that requests an invalid transition, so the Rust MDS requests only legal successors and validates states it is assigned; REPLAY->RECONNECT is legal for any rank count, REJOIN cannot be skipped, CLIENTREPLAY can.
risk: A standby must never request a state and a follower only its own state (DAMAGED is legal but dangerous, F-CLU-039).

group: Rank state machine and map handling
name: Requesting the next state through beacons
why: State changes are requested by repeated beacons and become real only when the map shows them: epoch and wanted state must be updated atomically, and messages arriving before the daemon sees its new state (early reconnects, retried requests, cap flushes) must be parked by comparing with the wanted state.
risk: A beacon with the new epoch but the pre-assignment state is an invalid transition (eviction with blocklist); each step costs a beacon round trip plus a Paxos commit (3-4 epochs per single-rank failover).

group: Rank state machine and map handling
name: Rank sets and derived predicates
why: A Rust rank needs the rank sets to route to peers (shard owners, LOOKUPINO forwarding), detect failures and know when it is the last rank in; the mon and libcephfs compute their own predicates.
subset: Decode in/up/failed/stopped/damaged and use up/active for routing and failure detection; the C++ is_resolving/is_rejoining/recovery-set predicates go with F-CLU-070.

group: Rank state machine and map handling
name: Daemon-level map handling
why: beacon-and-monitor 3.17 items 3 and 9: apply maps in epoch order, leave and return with a new identity when removed (or on the UINT32_MAX null map), keep up:boot until the standby map, start the MgrClient when first in a map, never change rank inside one identity.
subset: Like the C++ self-check, exit when the map's fs compat is not writeable by the Rust compat (defence in depth for F-CLU-014).
risk: A daemon that keeps serving after the map removed it undermines fencing until its writes fail.

group: Rank state machine and map handling
name: Rank-level map handling and peer change detection
why: A per-rank driver must start each phase when the map (not the request) shows the state and detect peer failures or restarts by incarnation; several of its side effects are client-visible.
subset: Keep: messenger entity name mds.<rank> while holding a rank (libcephfs takes the rank from the message source), inc handed to the RADOS client, OSD epoch barrier refresh while active, eviction of sessions lacking required_client_features. Drop: C++ resolve/rejoin triggers and journal fadvise hints.
risk: With msgr2 the kernel checks that the server ident address and nonce equal the map entry.

group: Rank state machine and map handling
name: MDSMap epoch waits for client requests
why: Requests carry the client's MDSMap epoch; a layout naming a pool just added with `fs add_data_pool` must wait until the MDS has that epoch instead of failing with EINVAL.
subset: Epoch waits for layout pool validation (create with layout, setlayout, setdirlayout); the mksnap/ALLOW_SNAPS path is P1 (D8: P0 mksnap returns EPERM).

group: Rank state machine and map handling
name: File-system health checks derived from the map
why: FS_DEGRADED, MDS_ALL_DOWN, MDS_INSUFFICIENT_STANDBY and related checks are computed by the mon from rank states, and Rook and cephadm gate on them; the Rust part is accurate states.

name: Boot stages for up:starting, up:replay and up:standby-replay
why: Before replaying or serving, a rank must load its persistent rank- and shard-level state with a defined error mapping (damaged, restart or read-only); the C++ objects (InoTable, SessionMap, JournalPointer, PurgeQueue, SnapServer, OpenFileTable) are out by D2.
subset: Load shards in parallel (multi-tenant replay); a validate_sessions-like check (session ino reservations vs the allocator) should damage only the affected shard (D10).

name: Creating a new rank (up:creating)
why: `fs new` and growth assign up:creating: the Rust daemon creates its rank-level state and, for rank 0, the root shard with root inode 1 (mode 0755, mds_root_ino_uid/gid, default layout on the first data pool), then requests up:active.
subset: A new non-zero rank creates only rank-level state and receives shards by placement (D6).
risk: If the creating holder dies the mon forgets the rank and the next holder creates it again: creation must be idempotent and should also wait for fencing (F-CLU-037).

name: Restarting a stopped rank (up:starting)
why: When the fs regrows into a previously stopped rank (`fs set down false`, max_mds raised after a shrink) the mon assigns up:starting; the Rust daemon must reopen the cleanly stopped rank state without replay and request up:active.
risk: A dead up:starting holder returns the rank to stopped and its successor does not wait for fencing (rank-lifecycle gotchas 19, 26).

name: up:replay: journal replay of a failed rank
why: D9: cold takeover replays the failed rank's durable state; with per-shard WALs shards replay in parallel (multi-tenant replay goal), rebuilding sessions, completed request ids, completed cap flushes and in-progress truncates (F-STORE-037).
subset: No leader/peer updates, ambiguous imports or fragment operations to rebuild (D4, D5). Report MDS_ESTIMATED_REPLAY_TIME after 30 s (F-ADM-081).

name: End of replay: journal reformat, writeable journal and the single-rank shortcut
why: At the end of replay the rank makes its journals writeable and requests the next state; the mon accepts up:replay -> up:reconnect for any rank count.
subset: Request up:reconnect directly (or up:resolve if kept, F-CLU-073). Journal reformat and snap-table format upgrade are old-data legacy.

name: Standby-replay follower loop
why: Warm standby-replay (tailing the active's journals for fast takeover) is P1 by D9; with per-shard WALs it means tailing many journal streams.
subset: P0 only tolerates the assignment (F-CLU-039).

name: Standby-replay takeover
why: When a followed rank fails the mon promotes its follower in place to up:replay (preferred replacement), so the Rust daemon must handle STANDBY_REPLAY -> REPLAY even without warm state.
subset: P0: wait for last_failure_osd_epoch, then a full cold replay; warm takeover from the follower's cache is P1 with F-CLU-068.

name: Recovery set and cluster-wide resolve/rejoin barriers
why: Cluster-wide resolve/rejoin barriers exist because C++ ranks share caches, locks and 2PC state; with whole-shard ownership (D3, D5) and no cross-rank 2PC (D4) each rank recovers independently (the multi-tenant recovery goal), and neither clients nor the mon see the barrier.
risk: Shard-ownership agreement after failures is still needed (F-CLU-074, F-CLU-075).
question: Confirm that per-rank recovery needs no cross-rank barrier.

name: Survivor reactions to a peer failing and recovering
why: With multi-rank P0 (D6), surviving ranks keep serving their own shards while a peer recovers and park or retry the cross-rank work aimed at it (LOOKUPINO forwards, shard migrations, rstat/quota propagation), detecting restarts by incarnation.
subset: Invalidate shard-boundary copies held from the failed rank instead of a rejoin exchange (F-CLU-085).

name: Deferring messages to bootstrapping peers and dropping stale peer messages
why: The new MDS-to-MDS protocol must hold messages for peers that are still booting and reject messages from an old incarnation of a rank (a fenced holder may still be connected).

name: up:resolve entry and exit
why: The mon accepts up:replay -> up:reconnect for any rank count, and what C++ settles in up:resolve (2PC outcomes, ambiguous imports, root dirfrag authority, snap-table resync, fragment rollback) disappears with D4/D5; shard-ownership settlement is F-CLU-074/075.
question: Settle shard ownership inside up:replay, or keep up:resolve as a visible (degraded) label for it? Either costs clients nothing.

name: Subtree authority resolution (subtree resolves)
why: After any failure all ranks must agree which rank owns each shard (D3: one owner at a time; D6: per-rank failover); C++ claims subtrees with MMDSResolve, Rust needs a durable, epoch-versioned shard map.

name: Ambiguous subtree import disambiguation
why: Live shard migration is P0 (D6), so a migration interrupted by the failure of either side must resolve deterministically: exactly one owner, with client caps and sessions ending at that owner.

name: Cross-rank two-phase update outcomes (peer resolves and ECommitted)
why: D4: no cross-rank 2PC; with whole-shard placement and EXDEV across shards no link, unlink, rmdir or rename spans ranks, so there are no peer resolves or ECommitted to settle.
risk: Any D4 dedicated cross-shard operation that spans ranks (shard-root create, rename into /volumes/_deleting, removal) needs its own crash-atomic design.
question: If cross-shard rename without EXDEV is ever wanted (README phase 4), a new 2PC with in-doubt resolution is required.

name: Rename-specific resolve handling
why: Ambiguous rename witnesses and peer_inode_cap re-export exist only for C++ cross-rank renames, which D4 removes (EXDEV across shards).

name: Snap table recovery and the SERVER_READY gate
why: P0 has no snap table (D8: mksnap returns EPERM), so the SERVER_READY gate and the rank-0 dependency vanish; P1 snapshots need a file-system-wide snapid allocator whose recovery must not hold other ranks in up:reconnect.

name: Post-resolve cache cleanup and authority bits
why: Orphan trimming and auth-bit recomputation after resolve are C++ cache mechanics for shared subtrees; nothing is client-visible.

name: up:reconnect: the client reconnect window and its timeout
why: Clients act when the map shows the rank in up:reconnect and reconnect sessions, caps, realms and file locks; the rank waits for missing sessions at least mds_reconnect_timeout (45 s, extended while reconnect activity continues, ended early when all reconnected), then evicts them with blocklisting, including `timeout`-key sessions (decision 6).
subset: Kill sessions whose address is already blocklisted at window start; deny late reconnects with CLOSE, unknown sessions with REJECT (F-PROTO-057).
risk: libcephfs drops its session and caps if it never observes up:reconnect, a late kclient reconnect gets CLOSE (-EIO on dirty data); the window is per rank by protocol, so one silent client delays every tenant of the rank.
override: Decision 6 (2026-10-11): no recovery hold. A session that misses reconnect is evicted whether or not it carries `timeout`; every shard goes active at once.

name: Recording caps and snaprealms from reconnect messages
why: Reconnected caps keep the client's cap_id and wanted bits, are issued without revoke with seq reset, and dirty cap flushes received during reconnect must be remembered; kclient and libcephfs match later cap messages by cap_id.
subset: Record realms {ino, seq, parent} for reconciliation (F-CLU-092); the parent ino + name hint may be used to find the inode.

name: Admission of replayed and retried requests during reconnect
why: During reconnect clients resend requests that never got a reply (retry > 0) before CLIENT_RECONNECT; a retried request already committed (in the session's completed requests) must be answered, with its created ino, before new requests can change its target.
subset: P0: accept and queue retried requests and answer completed ones first; renewals in any state, other session ops wait, requests from sessions that are not open are dropped silently. REPLAY and ASYNC replays arise only with P1 early replies and async dirops (D7).
risk: Answering a completed retry after another client unlinked its dentry trips libcephfs verify_reply_trace (ceph_abort).

name: Rejoin message exchange: weak rejoin, strong rejoin and acks
why: Weak/strong rejoin rebuilds replica nonces, lock states and remote auth pins between ranks; with no replicas beyond shard-boundary copies (D5) and no cross-rank locks (D4, D16), survivors just invalidate boundary copies (F-CLU-071); MDS-to-MDS only.
question: Confirm boundary copies (shard-root inodes in the parent shard) are dropped and refetched on peer restart rather than reconciled.

name: Recreating survivors' in-flight lock state on the recovering rank
why: Survivors' in-flight remote locks and auth pins on a recovering rank exist only with cross-rank operations and C++ lock machinery (D4, D16).

name: Matching reconnected caps to inodes: OpenFileTable prefetch and open by number
why: After failover the new holder's cache is cold, yet every cap a client reports must be attached to its inode, so open inodes must be loadable by number quickly; the OpenFileTable format is out (D2) but the purpose is P0.
subset: Per-shard open-file index plus the D4 ino-lookup mechanism; the reconnect's parent ino + single-name hint may be used.

name: Moving reconnected caps between ranks (IMPORT/EXPORT during rejoin)
why: With live shard migration and per-rank failover a client can report a cap to a rank that no longer owns the inode; the cap must reach the owner and the client be told with CEPH_CAP_OP_IMPORT/EXPORT matched by cap_id (F-CAPS-036).
risk: Forwarded caps that are never answered leave clients holding caps no rank tracks (C++ gotcha).

name: Forced session open during rejoin
why: Whenever caps are attached on a rank where the client has no open session (F-CLU-088, migration), the rank must open and persist a session and send CEPH_SESSION_OPEN (F-PROTO-041); reconnected sessions are persisted before serving.
subset: Legacy v1 SESSION_OPEN for pre-Mimic clients is out.

name: Choosing lock states from reconnected caps
why: After reconnect the Rust lock/cap engine must start from the caps clients actually hold (exclusive or buffered write caps mean an exclusive writer) so caps and metadata state agree before serving; C++ SimpleLock state choice is out (D16).

name: Scatterlock recovery and NEED_RECOVER
why: Scatterlocks and NEED_RECOVER are C++ cross-rank lock machinery (D16); inside a shard dirstat/rstat are transactional.
risk: Cross-shard rstat/quota deltas pending for ancestors must be durable in the new aggregation mechanism (D4), or ancestor rstats drift after a failover.

name: Snaprealm reconciliation and snapflush rebuild at the end of rejoin
why: P0 keeps snap realms for quota and subvolume roots (D8); clients report their realms in reconnect and must get MClientSnap UPDATE/SPLIT when their view is stale, or client-side quota enforcement uses the wrong realm.
subset: Realm reconciliation (UPDATE/SPLIT and the end-of-rejoin update) for quota/subvolume realms; snapflush rebuild (LOCK_SNAP_SYNC) comes with P1 snapshots.
risk: A malformed snap trace makes the kernel blocklist itself; a SPLIT needs split_inos/split_realms.

name: Rejoin cache repair: invented objects, stale fragmentation, missed link/unlink
why: Invented placeholder objects, stale fragtree mapping and missed link/unlink repair exist only for C++ replicas and dirfrags (D5).

name: Rejoin on a single-rank file system
why: up:rejoin cannot be skipped (the mon only allows RECONNECT -> REJOIN), so every recovering rank passes through it; it is where the rank attaches reconnected caps, seeds lock state, identifies files needing size recovery and reconciles realms before serving.
subset: Per-shard parallel work instead of full-cache scans; no messages to other ranks.

name: up:clientreplay: ordered re-execution of replayed requests
why: D7: early (unsafe) replies and clientreplay are P1; without unsafe replies no client holds a request to replay, but the state machine and ino reservations must leave room for it.
subset: When added: same results and same ino (head.ino), no unsafe reply for replays, before any new request; per-shard parallel replay instead of one-at-a-time is free.

name: Reclaim gating of the clientreplay to active transition
why: Decision 6: the rank-wide hold in up:clientreplay for `timeout` sessions that missed reconnect is not reproduced. Those sessions are evicted at the end of reconnect like any other, and their successor's reset-reclaim gets ENOENT, which FSAL_CEPH ignores.
risk: Accepted gap: when the MDS and a Ganesha fail together, native CephFS clients can take locks that NFS clients will try to reclaim through the new Ganesha. libcephfs reclaim.cc (reclaim after an MDS respawn) expects the C++ behaviour.
override: Decision 6 (2026-10-11): no recovery hold. A session that misses reconnect is evicted whether or not it carries `timeout`; every shard goes active at once.

name: Activation (recovery_done and active_start)
why: On becoming active the rank must start post-recovery work (truncates, size recovery, stray/purge processing), reissue caps and release every request that waited; the C++ populate_mydir and stray-directory layout are out.
subset: The dead-code branch of populate_mydir is legacy.

name: Leftover reconnect caps and cap reissue at activation
why: At activation caps are re-evaluated and may be granted or revoked with the current OSD epoch barrier (libcephfs 7.1, rank-lifecycle 7), and caps whose inode was never found must be answered.
subset: Reissue/revoke all reconnected caps with the OSD epoch barrier; for caps whose inode cannot be found, log a cluster warning and send an EXPORT.
question: C++ sends an EXPORT with cap_id 0 that both clients ignore; send one with the client's cap_id and peer.mds = -1 so clients really drop the cap?

name: File size and mtime recovery for writers that did not come back
why: Data written by a client that never came back must be preserved up to its granted max_size: size and mtime recovered by probing data objects (never shrinking), stat/read/write of the file blocked until done, which needs client_ranges persisted (F-CAPS-022).

name: Re-executing interrupted truncates after recovery
why: A shrinking truncate whose metadata is durable must finish trimming the data objects after a failover (idempotent via truncate_seq), otherwise stale data reappears beyond EOF (F-STORE-065).

name: Purging orphaned preallocated and delegated inodes
why: Orphaned objects of lost creates exist only when clients write before the create is durable (async creates with delegated inos, or unsafe replies), both P1 (D7).
subset: With P1 async dirops: purge unused delegated/preallocated inos of sessions that did not come back (all objects, not only object 0 as in C++).

name: Stopping a rank (up:stopping to down:stopped)
why: D6: a rank stopped by a max_mds decrease (cephadm and Rook upgrades use max_mds 1) must hand off all its shards with their client caps, strays and per-shard purge queues (F-BG-022/023), keep processing requests meanwhile, close remaining sessions (the last rank evicts and blocklists all clients), and only then request down:stopped.
subset: Export whole shards (no stray export to rank 0, no C++ journal capping); ignore new session opens while stopping; keep rank-level state for a later up:starting.
risk: Report STOPPED only when the rank owns no shard and no session: the mon then removes the rank and kernels force-close sessions to ranks >= size(in).
override: Reconciles CLU ('drain purge work') with BG (per-shard purge queues travel with their shard; no full drain).

name: Reporting a rank as DAMAGED
why: When rank-level state cannot be loaded or replayed the daemon must report down:damaged (beacon, wait for the ack) so no daemon is reassigned until `mds repaired`; D10 wants shard-level damage contained instead.
subset: Report DAMAGED only for rank-wide failures (unreadable rank-level state, broken fencing invariant); a damaged shard returns EIO or goes offline while the rank keeps serving.
risk: Wait for the ack without blocking the ack path (C++ can miss it while holding mds_lock).
question: Which failures still take the whole rank down:damaged in the Rust design?

name: Respawn: re-exec as a fresh standby
why: Whenever the daemon may no longer act for its rank (removed from the map, rank change, invalid transition, -EBLOCKLISTED) it must drop all state and return as a new standby with a new gid and nonce (beacon-and-monitor 3.17 item 9).
subset: Mechanism is free: exec, in-process re-init with a fresh messenger and MonClient, or exit (Rook and systemd restart with backoff, so frequent exits are costly).

name: Suicide and orderly shutdown
why: SIGTERM/SIGINT from cephadm, Rook and systemd must end in a DNE beacon and a clean exit; fatal boot errors (auth, rotating keys) and an unwritable map compat must exit instead of serving.
subset: Asok `exit` and the shutdown order are free; avoid the C++ shutdown deadlocks.

name: Write error policy
why: RADOS write errors need defined outcomes: -EBLOCKLISTED means fenced (restart, F-CLU-105); other metadata or journal write errors go read-only or damaged, preferably per shard (D10).
subset: Keep -EBLOCKLISTED -> restart; mds_action_on_write_error semantics may be redesigned per shard.

name: Process bootstrap (ceph-mds -i <id>)
why: cephadm and Rook start `ceph-mds` from the Ceph image with fixed command lines (--id/-n, --fsid, --keyring, --mon-host, --setuser/--setgroup, --foreground, --default-* options, --public-addr) and expect ceph.conf plus the mon config DB to apply (F-ADM-113).
subset: Accept that command line and those config sources, authenticate with cephx, wait for rotating keys, subscribe mdsmap and start beaconing in up:boot; `--hot-standby` and msgr1 protocol 36 are legacy.
risk: Rook resolves `ceph-mds` through PATH and its liveness probe needs the `ceph` CLI, bash and jq in the same image.

name: Single public messenger with per-peer-type policies
why: One msgr2 messenger whose address vector is what the mon records from beacons, what clients connect to and OSD fencing blocklists, and what the kernel checks in the server ident (address and nonce); client connections are lossless stateful-server.
subset: Peer-MDS policies are free (Rust only). The msgr1 accept side serves CLIENT peers with protocol 32 (decision 3); protocol 36 between MDS daemons stays out.
override: Decision 3 (2026-10-11): a basic msgr1 listener for kernel clients is P0, so kernels mounted without ms_mode (Rook's default requireMsgr2=false for ceph-csi, the old device syntax, ms_mode=legacy) work unchanged.

name: MonClient session, keys and subscriptions
why: The daemon needs a MonClient with cephx service keys for MON, OSD, MDS and MGR, subscriptions to monmap, config, mdsmap, mgrmap and osdmap, and the `profile mds` caps (beacons, blocklist commands, cluster log); Rook and cephadm set mds_join_fs and mds_cache_memory_limit only in the mon config DB.
subset: Dropping MMonCommand from pre-Luminous monitors is legacy.

name: Global mds_lock (FIFO fair mutex)
why: The global mds_lock is the C++ serialization the project removes (constraint 5, D16).

name: Completion contexts and the rank finisher
why: MDSContext completions and the rank finisher are C++ re-entry mechanics (D16); their visible effects (restart on -EBLOCKLISTED, ordered journal completions) are covered by F-CLU-105 and the WAL design.

name: Progress thread and rank waiter queues
why: The progress thread and waiter queues are C++ internals (D16); the waits they implement (map epoch, active state, recovery) are kept as behaviours in their own entries.

name: Dispatcher chain, message priorities and ordering
why: Clients rely on their messages being handled in send order where it matters (cap messages per inode in seq order, flushes and releases before later requests, requests sent before CLIENT_RECONNECT); fine-grained concurrency must keep that.
subset: Per-connection ordering for causally related messages, metrics out of band; the C++ priority queue, dispatcher chain and single dispatch thread are internal.
question: Define the per-session ordering contract the transaction engine must honour.

name: Rank message validation and routing
why: The rank must accept exactly the client message types (session, reconnect, reclaim, request, caps, cap release, lease, metrics) from clients, MDSMap and OSDMap from mons, and MCommand (tell) from admin clients and mgr, dropping anything from an unexpected peer type (F-ADM-004).
subset: MDS-to-MDS whitelist is free; MRemoveSnaps comes with P1 snapshots; MMonCommand from legacy mons is out. Never abort on an unexpected message (C++ asserts on a non-MMDSOp from an MDS).

name: Outbound messaging helpers and local delivery
why: Client-visible send rules: forwards are MClientRequestForward with strictly increasing num_fwd and must_resend, and counted pushes (CAPS, LEASE, SNAP, QUOTA) advance the session push_seq that REQUEST_CLOSE must match.
subset: Queue counted pushes for a session without a connection; MDS-to-MDS send helpers (bootstrap deferral, map piggyback) and local delivery are free.
risk: Kernel BUG_ON on a forward for a tid that already got a reply; -EMULTIHOP when num_fwd does not increase.

name: Tick and the shared timer
why: A single 5 s tick under mds_lock is a C++ mechanism; each periodic duty (session liveness, reconnect timeout, health refresh, stopping progress) is classified in its own entry.
risk: Those duties must not stall when the metadata engine is busy.

name: Thread inventory of the daemon and its subsystems
why: Thread inventory of the C++ process; the Rust threading model is free.

name: MDS-originated client requests (MDSMetaRequest)
why: MDS-to-MDS client requests serve cross-rank stray reintegration and quota-realm creation; with per-shard strays and realms created by the owning shard (D3) nothing crosses ranks.

group: Transport: msgr2 (and legacy msgr1) as clients see them
name: msgr1 (legacy protocol) server side for client connections
why: Kernel clients mounted without ms_mode speak msgr1: ceph-csi under Rook's CRD default requireMsgr2=false, the old mon:/path device syntax and ms_mode=legacy. Supporting them is simpler than changing every deployment and test setup (decision 3).
subset: Accept side only, for CLIENT peers, following the transport page 7.3 checklist: banner with the v1 address equal to the MDSMap entry (nonce included); connect with protocol 32; cephx authorizer with one challenge round; READY/SEQ with MSG_AUTH in the features; header, front, middle and data crcs; signed 21-byte footer; strict in_seq + 1; ACK; KEEPALIVE2_ACK; RESETSESSION for unknown sessions; never WAIT; front and middle at most 16 MiB, data at most 64 MiB. Outbound connections to mons, mgr, OSDs and peer MDS daemons stay msgr2. The beacon address vector lists v2 first and v1 second with the same nonce, so C++ clients keep dialling msgr2.
risk: msgr1 has no encryption, only per-message signatures. The kernel treats WAIT, BADPROTOVER, FEATURES and unknown tags as connection errors and retries with backoff.
question: Make requireMsgr2: true (the value in Rook's example cluster.yaml) a documented deployment requirement, or keep a msgr1 listener for ceph-csi kernel mounts?
override: Decision 3 (2026-10-11): a basic msgr1 listener for kernel clients is P0, so kernels mounted without ms_mode (Rook's default requireMsgr2=false for ceph-csi, the old device syntax, ms_mode=legacy) work unchanged.

group: Transport: msgr2 (and legacy msgr1) as clients see them
name: msgr2.1 crc mode for client connections
why: Every current client (7.3 kernel with ms_mode=prefer-crc, libcephfs, ceph-fuse, Ganesha) reaches the MDS over msgr2.1 crc mode (transport 7.2, 7.4).
subset: msgr2.1 framing only; the msgr2.0 (rev0) layout for Ceph 14.2.0-14.2.10 and 15.2.0-15.2.4 peers is out.
risk: The kernel faults the connection on WAIT, a server KEEPALIVE2, SESSION_RESET(full=0), empty or aborted control frames, bad crcs (it ignores nocrc), a first v2 SERVER_IDENT address that differs from the MDSMap entry, or MSG_AUTH missing from the server features.

group: Transport: msgr2 (and legacy msgr1) as clients see them
name: msgr2.1 secure mode (AES-128-GCM)
why: The MDS's own mon and mgr connections select secure mode by default (transport 3.1), and kernel ms_mode=secure or Rook network encryption select it towards the MDS, so AES-128-GCM msgr2.1 is needed anyway.
subset: msgr2.1 64-bit nonce counters only; the msgr2.0 nonce format is out.

group: Transport: msgr2 (and legacy msgr1) as clients see them
name: msgr2 on-wire compression negotiation
why: Not advertising the COMPRESSION banner bit makes C++ peers skip the phase, the kernel never negotiates it, and the C++ MDS selects no compression for client peers anyway.
risk: If the bit is ever advertised, COMPRESSION_REQUEST must be answered with COMPRESSION_DONE; a compressed frame on an uncompressed connection aborts a C++ receiver.

group: Transport: msgr2 (and legacy msgr1) as clients see them
name: Address vector publication and server identity checks
why: Clients learn the MDS address only from the MDSMap and check SERVER_IDENT against it (kernel: first v2 address byte for byte incl. nonce; C++ clients: equality for remote-reset handling); the mon and OSD fencing use the same vector.
subset: Publish the v2 entry first and a v1 (TYPE_LEGACY) entry second with the same nonce (decision 3). The msgr2 SERVER_IDENT and the msgr1 banner both present exactly the published address.
risk: An MDSMap entry that has addresses but no TYPE_MSGR2 address makes the kernel shut the mount down; a restarted daemon must use a new nonce. See F-PROTO-001 for the Rook default.
override: Decision 3 (2026-10-11): a basic msgr1 listener for kernel clients is P0, so kernels mounted without ms_mode (Rook's default requireMsgr2=false for ceph-csi, the old device syntax, ms_mode=legacy) work unchanged.

group: Transport: msgr2 (and legacy msgr1) as clients see them
name: Lossless stateful-server connection policy and replay of unacknowledged messages
why: Client connections are lossless stateful-server: unacknowledged messages must be replayed with their original sequence numbers after SESSION_RECONNECT, which push_seq and cap-sequence correctness depend on.
subset: msgr2 ack_seq/ACK frames and SESSION_RECONNECT(_OK); on kernel msgr1 connections also TAG_ACK and the SEQ exchange on reconnect (decision 3).
risk: The kernel rejects any sequence gap; a C++ client that receives an already-seen sequence number drops it and, by code reading, stops reading the connection; the MDS never initiates TCP to a client.
override: Decision 3 (2026-10-11): a basic msgr1 listener for kernel clients is P0, so kernels mounted without ms_mode (Rook's default requireMsgr2=false for ceph-csi, the old device syntax, ms_mode=legacy) work unchanged.

group: Transport: msgr2 (and legacy msgr1) as clients see them
name: Peer-reset detection and session-reset signalling
why: Clients detect lost server state through SESSION_RESET(full=1) and react (kernel reconnects in up:reconnect, else tears the session down; libcephfs marks it stale); open sessions must survive connection loss, which Ganesha's abort_conn plus reclaim relies on.
subset: msgr2 client-cookie detection and SESSION_RESET(full=1); on kernel msgr1 connections connect_seq detection and the RESETSESSION reply (decision 3).
risk: SESSION_RESET(full=0) is a kernel protocol error; a kernel session torn down while the rank is active silently loses all its caps (dirty state -EIO).
override: Decision 3 (2026-10-11): a basic msgr1 listener for kernel clients is P0, so kernels mounted without ms_mode (Rook's default requireMsgr2=false for ceph-csi, the old device syntax, ms_mode=legacy) work unchanged.

group: Transport: msgr2 (and legacy msgr1) as clients see them
name: MDS entity name and rank identity on the wire
why: libcephfs takes the sending rank from the msgr2 SERVER_IDENT gid and drops messages whose (rank, connection) pair matches no session, so the messenger entity number must be the rank before the daemon is reachable as that rank (failover D9, rank changes D6).
subset: The name number is sent once in the msgr2 SERVER_IDENT and in the src of every msgr1 message header (decision 3). Accept session, reconnect, reclaim, caps, cap-release and lease messages only from CLIENT peers.
risk: A connection accepted while the messenger had another number keeps that number for its lifetime (transport 8 item 32).
override: Decision 3 (2026-10-11): a basic msgr1 listener for kernel clients is P0, so kernels mounted without ms_mode (Rook's default requireMsgr2=false for ceph-csi, the old device syntax, ms_mode=legacy) work unchanged.

group: Transport: msgr2 (and legacy msgr1) as clients see them
name: Keepalives and connection timeouts
why: Clients send KEEPALIVE2 (the kernel at least every 5 s when it does not renew) and expect KEEPALIVE2_ACK echoing the timestamp.
subset: Answer KEEPALIVE2 with KEEPALIVE2_ACK, as a msgr2 frame or as the msgr1 tag on kernel msgr1 connections (decision 3); never send KEEPALIVE2 to clients; a handshake timeout is recommended; the 900 s idle fault is optional.
risk: A server-originated KEEPALIVE2 is a kernel protocol error.
override: Decision 3 (2026-10-11): a basic msgr1 listener for kernel clients is P0, so kernels mounted without ms_mode (Rook's default requireMsgr2=false for ceph-csi, the old device syntax, ms_mode=legacy) work unchanged.

group: Transport: msgr2 (and legacy msgr1) as clients see them
name: Inbound flow control (messenger dispatch throttle)
why: No wire contract (clients only see TCP back-pressure), but an MDS serving thousands of sessions must bound buffered inbound bytes; the C++ messenger-wide 100 MiB budget couples every client and subvolume.
risk: Stopping reads on a shared Ganesha session (F-PROTO-101) because one shard is slow stalls every other subvolume on that session (head-of-line blocking).
question: Choose the bounding unit (connection, session, per-shard queue) so one slow or noisy shard cannot block other tenants that share a session.

name: cephx authorizer verification for service mds
why: Every client connection presents a cephx authorizer for service mds (auth_service_required default cephx); AES and AES256KRB5 keys both occur depending on cluster history.
subset: msgr2 exchange (challenge in AUTH_REPLY_MORE, CephXAuthorizeReply with a 64-byte secret in secure mode, none in crc mode) and, on kernel msgr1 connections, CHALLENGE_AUTHORIZER/BADAUTHORIZER with exactly one challenge round (decision 3).
risk: Ticket expiry is not checked, only that secret_id is among the three held rotating secrets; an empty authorizer must fail.
override: Decision 3 (2026-10-11): a basic msgr1 listener for kernel clients is P0, so kernels mounted without ms_mode (Rook's default requireMsgr2=false for ceph-csi, the old device syntax, ms_mode=legacy) work unchanged.

name: Rotating mds service secrets
why: Without the current rotating mds secrets from the monitors no client authorizer can be verified (transport 7.5).
risk: A MonMap auth_epoch increase wipes secrets and tickets; client authorizers fail until new secrets arrive.

name: msgr1 message signatures
why: The kernel requires MSG_AUTH on msgr1 unless mounted with nocephx_sign_messages, so every message on a kernel msgr1 connection carries a cephx signature in the 21-byte footer and incoming signatures are verified (decision 3).
override: Decision 3 (2026-10-11): a basic msgr1 listener for kernel clients is P0, so kernels mounted without ms_mode (Rook's default requireMsgr2=false for ceph-csi, the old device syntax, ms_mode=legacy) work unchanged.

name: Connection-to-session binding (identity is the cephx global id)
why: Clients keep one session per rank keyed by their cephx global id (a remount is a new session), the session spans every shard on that rank (D4), and messages for a session whose client has not connected yet (force-opened by a shard import, D6) must be queued until it connects.
risk: C++ flushes only the bootstrap queue when it re-points a connection to an imported session (sessions 8); the new design must not lose an import's OPEN or cap messages.

name: Encoding primitives and versioned-struct rules
why: Kernel and libcephfs decode with ENCODE_START rules: struct_compat must be 1 on InodeStat, DirStat, LeaseStat and quota_info_t, unknown trailing bytes are skipped by struct_len, and the raw heads are packed memcpy layouts.
risk: The kernel parses MDSCapAuth/MDSCapMatch positionally without struct_len: never append fields to them (F-ADM-021).

name: Client message catalog and peer-type filtering
why: Current clients exchange message types 22-29 and 0x310-0x314; taking client-type messages only from client peers keeps a client from injecting MDS-internal traffic.
subset: Implement 22 MClientSession, 23 MClientReconnect, 24 MClientRequest, 25 MClientRequestForward (send), 26 MClientReply (send), 27/28 MClientReclaim/ReclaimReply, 29 MClientMetrics, 0x310-0x314; 0x315 MQuarantineDisable only with quarantine (P2). Inter-rank traffic uses the new MDS-to-MDS protocol, so MClientRequest/MClientReply between ranks are not needed and an MClientReply from a client is dropped.
risk: The C++ MDS asserts on an unsafe MClientReply sent by a client; drop it instead.

name: Decode failures and client-triggerable aborts
why: No peer depends on the C++ aborts, but one malformed message must not take down a rank that serves many tenants (robustness goal, multi-tenant isolation).
risk: Decode fallibly: fault the connection or fail the request (-EINVAL/-EBADMSG) on a caps xattr_len/middle mismatch, trailing bytes, unknown lease actions, bad initial-xattr, fscrypt or flock blobs and owner -1; never abort.

name: Golden encodings and encoding test data
why: No runtime contract, but clients fail or assert on any byte deviation, so the Rust codecs need golden-data conformance tests: ceph-dencoder round trips, ceph-object-corpus, the test_frames_v2 frame tables and the RFC 8009 crypto vectors.
subset: Test-time only; nothing is registered with ceph-dencoder at run time.

name: CephFS feature bitmap exchange at session open
why: Clients pick decoders and request formats from the MDS bitmap in every OPEN (the kernel keeps the first 64 bits), and the MDS keeps the client bitmap for its own per-bit behaviour.
subset: Advertise bits 0-14 and 16-21 (not 15, 22, 23, 24 while fscrypt, charmap/subvolume metrics, blockdiff and quarantine are deferred; see the summary table), always send OPEN as v7 with supported_features and metric_spec, same bitmap on every rank. OPEN v1 for sessions without bit 8 is out.
risk: Both clients overwrite their copy of the MDS bits on every OPEN from any rank and the kernel's subvolume-metrics switch is mount-wide, so ranks must never advertise different sets.

name: Per-bit gated behaviour and feature names
why: Current clients set bits 8, 9, 11, 13, 16 and 21 (libcephfs also 19), so only the current-client side of each MDS branch is needed; clients test MDS bits 9, 10, 12-15, 17-20, 22 and 23.
subset: MDS behaviour: v7 session messages with error_string (8), versioned reply encodings (9), notable-caps-only re-issue on stale resume (11), openc_response_t (13), duplicate open answered with OPEN (16), snap-trace format by client bit 19, no charmap gate on bit 22, quarantine (24) P2. Out: branches for sessions lacking 8, 9, 11, 13, 16 or 21, and the broken-root_squash flag.
question: Enforce a built-in client floor (REJECT a REQUEST_OPEN that lacks bits 8, 9, 13, 18, 20, 21) instead of MDSMap required_client_features, which v6.0+ kernels mis-skip (F-PROTO-023)?

name: Feature inference for clients that send no feature bits
why: Legacy: inference serves only clients that send no bitmap (kernels up to v4.18, Ceph up to 13.2.1); a REQUEST_OPEN without a bitmap is rejected instead.

name: required_client_features enforcement and min_compat_client
why: No mgr module, cephadm or Rook flow sets required_client_features (they use only the OSDMap require_min_compat_client), and a non-empty bitmap makes v6.0+ kernels misparse the MDSMap extension and lose max_xattr_size.
subset: If built: REJECT at open, CLOSE at reconnect and evict on change for missing bits; the deprecated min_compat_client and inference before the test are out.
risk: Ignoring the bitmap silently skips an operator's requirement.
question: Rely on the built-in client floor of F-PROTO-021 instead?

name: Connection-level feature bits consulted by the client protocol
why: The 7.3 kernel picks the request head from the MDS connection's FS_BTIME (59) and the reconnect format from MDSENC (29), sends FLUSH_MDLOG only with SERVER_LUMINOUS (21), as libcephfs does, and requires MSG_AUTH in the server features.
subset: Advertise the full CEPH_FEATURES_ALL of the baseline (MSG_AUTH, SERVER_LUMINOUS, MDSENC, EXPORT_PEER, FLOCK, REPLY_CREATE_INODE, MDS_QUOTA, FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2, FS_BTIME/MSG_ADDR2 ...). Assume FLOCK, EXPORT_PEER, MDS_QUOTA, FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2 and FS_BTIME on client connections (no fallback encoders); honour args.open.pool only from CREATEPOOLID connections (libcephfs); never create inline inodes (D12).
risk: A messenger feature set missing FS_BTIME, MDSENC or SERVER_LUMINOUS silently moves the kernel to the legacy request head, reconnect v2 or no FLUSH_MDLOG.

name: Feature bit 22 numbering conflict (Ceph CHARMAP vs kernel SUBVOLUME_METRICS)
why: D15 requires an explicit decision: the 7.3 kernel reads MDS bit 22 as SUBVOLUME_METRICS (enables 1 Hz type-16 metric items) and sets its own bit 22 with that meaning, while libcephfs sets bit 22 meaning CHARMAP and ignores the MDS's bit 22.
subset: P0: do not advertise bit 22 (charmap P2, subvolume metrics P1) and never read a client's bit 22 as charmap capability. With P1 subvolume metrics: advertise it on every rank, fill InodeStat v9 subvolume_id and decode the kernel's type-16 items. A future charmap must be gated on another signal.
risk: Advertising it without a type-16 decoder or inconsistently across ranks toggles kernel metrics per OPEN; reading client bit 22 as charmap capability lets 7.1+ kernels create unfolded names in case-insensitive directories (kclient 7.1.4).
question: Confirm: bit 22 off in P0, on with P1 subvolume metrics; how will a future charmap identify capable clients?

name: Client generations and candidate minimum client floors
why: The baseline is one kernel (7.3) and libcephfs at main; their current formats are session open v7, request v6 with head v3, single-message reconnect v3 (v5 parts above ~2 GiB), the old snap-trace format for the kernel, and no kernel bits 10, 19, 23, 24.
subset: Serve these formats; older generations, the CentOS Stream rows and candidate floors F1-F7 are out (legacy).
risk: CentOS Stream 9 kernels (5.14.0-757) match the 7.3 request formats but open sessions with MClientSession v4, which a v1/v7-only decoder refuses.
question: Decode MClientSession by version (v4 costs nothing) to admit RHEL/CentOS 9 kernels?

name: Session state machine
why: Clients see the session lifecycle through OPEN, CLOSE, STALE, RENEWCAPS and REJECT, and session ls shows the state; open follows a durable record, close follows REQUEST_CLOSE with a matching seq, kill follows eviction.
subset: State names and transitions as in C++; state_seq and projection mechanics are internal.
risk: libcephfs keeps sending requests on a STALE session.

name: Session open handshake (REQUEST_OPEN, journaled open, OPEN)
why: Both clients open a session per rank with REQUEST_OPEN v7 and queue requests until OPEN; the MDS must persist the session (metadata, auth_name) before replying OPEN v7 with supported_features, metric_spec and cap_auths (D7, D9).
subset: Persistence in the new session store (D2), not ESession/SessionMap; REQUEST_OPEN v2-v5 and OPEN v1 are out (see F-PROTO-026 for decoding by version).

name: Session open admission checks and rejection reasons
why: Security and Ganesha correctness depend on the open checks: fs-name caps, blocklisted address, mount root inside the cap path, duplicate uuid (reclaim) and refuse_client_session (required before fs rename).
subset: In C++ order: refuse_client_session (REJECT), closing (wait), already open (F-PROTO-037), stopping (drop), blocklisted (REJECT + SESSION_BLOCKLISTED), missing required or floor bits, root empty, not '/'-prefixed or outside the cap path (REJECT), duplicate uuid (REJECT); skip the root check when the key is absent (Ganesha reclaim sessions). Out: feature inference and broken-root_squash flagging.
risk: A 'sessionless' REJECT to a RENEWCAPS from an open kernel session trips a kernel WARN and marks the session REJECTED (requests then fail with -EACCES).
question: For session ops other than REQUEST_OPEN on a connection without a session, mark the connection down (the kernel's peer-reset path reopens) instead of sending REJECT?

name: REJECT encoding and blocklist signalling to clients
why: A refused or blocklisted client learns it only from REJECT: the 7.3 kernel uses flags SESSION_BLOCKLISTED (v5+) for recover_session=clean, libcephfs logs error_string and fails with -EPERM.
subset: Always v7 with flags and error_string; v1 REJECT for sessions without bit 8 and the kernel's v3/v4 'blacklisted' substring scan are legacy (keeping the C++ string costs nothing).
risk: REJECT outside OPENING/RECONNECTING makes the kernel WARN.

name: MClientSession encoding and the ops the MDS sends
why: libcephfs ceph_abort()s on any session op other than OPEN, CLOSE, RENEWCAPS, STALE, RECALL_STATE, FLUSHMSG, FORCE_RO and REJECT; the kernel reads features only from v3+, flags from v5+ and cap_auths from v6+.
subset: Emit v1 for head-only ops and v7 otherwise; decode client v1 and v7 (v2-v5 legacy, see F-PROTO-026).
risk: cap_auths must use the exact MDSCapAuth v1 {MDSCapMatch v1 {uid, gids, path, fs_name, root_squash}, readable, writeable} layout; the kernel parses it positionally.

name: Session op dispatch and rank-state gating
why: Clients renew from up:reconnect (kernel) or up:rejoin (libcephfs) and expect answers; any client message counts as liveness for idle detection.
subset: RENEWCAPS in every state from reconnect on; REQUEST_OPEN, FLUSHMSG_ACK and FLUSH_MDLOG once serving (clientreplay is P1, D7); REQUEST_CLOSE see F-PROTO-049.

name: Unknown session op handling
why: Unmodified clients send only the five client ops, so an unknown op only has to be harmless.
subset: Log and drop (or REJECT) an unknown session op; the C++ eviction with blocklisting is optional; never crash.

name: Client metadata capture and use
why: The MDS uses root (cap check), uuid (duplicate check, reclaim), timeout (Ganesha) and hostname, and mgr modules read the metadata from client ls: stats needs hostname and root, volumes evicts by client_metadata.root, the dashboard shows versions.
subset: Store and persist kv metadata, client features and metric spec; expose them in session ls with client_metadata.<key> filters; feature inference from ceph_version/kernel_version is out.
risk: Ganesha's short-lived reclaim sessions carry only the timeout key (no root or hostname).

name: Duplicate REQUEST_OPEN answered with OPEN (NOTIFY_SESSION_STATE)
why: Both current clients set bit 16 and re-send REQUEST_OPEN after a client-side session re-init; the MDS answers with OPEN carrying push_seq and supported_features, which resynchronizes the client.
subset: Unlike C++, include metric_spec in the duplicate OPEN (the C++ omission clears libcephfs's metric spec and stops its spec-gated metrics); the silent drop for clients without bit 16 is legacy.

name: FORCE_RO: read-only MDS notification
why: Clients learn that metadata is read-only only from FORCE_RO (then fail Fw/Fx cap waits with -EROFS); without it writers wait for caps the MDS will never grant.
subset: Send FORCE_RO to open and stale sessions when a rank-wide read-only state is entered, and after every OPEN or reconnect in that state.
question: FORCE_RO is session-wide (all shards of the rank); per-shard read-only (D10 containment) needs another path (-EROFS on W ops, no Fw/Fx in that shard). Does P0 have any rank-wide read-only state?

name: FLUSHMSG / FLUSHMSG_ACK session barrier
why: Shard migration between ranks (D6) needs the barrier that C++ subtree export uses: the client has processed every counted cap message and flushed its cap releases (FLUSHMSG_ACK) before caps move.
subset: FLUSHMSG with seq = push_seq; waiters complete on FLUSHMSG_ACK >= seq, on stale or on close; EXPORT_PEER is assumed (all baseline clients).

name: REQUEST_FLUSH_MDLOG and the client sync paths
why: Kernel fsync/syncfs/unmount and libcephfs fsync (every NFS COMMIT, stable WRITE and SETATTR through Ganesha) send FLUSH_MDLOG, then wait for safe replies and flush acks.
subset: Accept op 12 without reply in any serving state; commit at once the WALs (shards) that hold pending work of that session; advertise SERVER_LUMINOUS so clients send it.
risk: With safe-only replies (D7) nothing is unsafe, so the remaining sync cost is the FLAG_SYNC cap-flush commit; group-commit delay directly bounds Ganesha's synchronous throughput.

name: Force-opened sessions (imports, rejoin, cross-MDS rename)
why: When a shard moves to another rank (D6), caps are imported for clients that may never have opened a session there; they receive an unsolicited OPEN before the cap IMPORT messages.
subset: Contract kept: the importing rank opens and persists the session, sends OPEN (queued until the client connects) and FORCE_RO if needed; importing sessions are not closed by REQUEST_CLOSE, kill or idle eviction until the import ends; a failed import closes sessions the client never opened. Mechanism: the new MDS-to-MDS migration protocol, not EImportStart/ESessions.

name: Cap renewal (REQUEST_RENEWCAPS / RENEWCAPS)
why: Clients trust caps and leases only while RENEWCAPS replies arrive within session_timeout (kernel every timeout/4 with v7 and oldest_client_tid, libcephfs every timeout/3 with v1).
risk: RENEWCAPS must echo the request seq (the kernel accepts only seq == s_renew_seq); a stale session is reopened with notable-caps re-issue (bit 11).

name: Stale session detection and the STALE message
why: A dead client's caps must stop blocking others after session_timeout: the MDS invalidates them, revokes without waiting, sends STALE, and evicts if a write-cap revoke was pending.
subset: Includes the default deferred staling of F-PROTO-044.

name: Deferred stale marking for quiet sessions (mds_defer_session_stale)
why: With the C++ default a silent session goes stale only when the MDS needs something from it (a revoke or a flush), which is the behaviour clients observe today.
subset: Implement the default (deferred) policy; the dev option mds_defer_session_stale itself is optional.

name: Session autoclose eviction
why: Silent sessions are evicted (blocklisted by default) after session_autoclose; this bounds dead clients, including Ganesha sessions whose timeout rule the defaults never reach.
risk: The autoclose check runs before the timeout check, so a Ganesha restart that takes longer than session_autoclose loses the old session to eviction rather than to reclaim.

name: Per-session timeout metadata
why: NFS-Ganesha V15.7 always sets timeout=300: while the MDS stays up, its sessions are never marked stale and are kept, with their caps and locks, until the successor reclaims them, they are killed, or autoclose evicts them.
subset: Idle rules as in C++. At rank recovery a `timeout` session that misses reconnect is evicted like any other session (decision 6).
override: Decision 6 (2026-10-11): no recovery hold. A session that misses reconnect is evicted whether or not it carries `timeout`; every shard goes active at once.

name: Eviction deferral while OSDs are laggy
why: Opt-in (defer_client_eviction_on_laggy_osds default false); no default flow enables it.

name: Cap-revoke non-responder eviction
why: Opt-in (mds_cap_revoke_eviction_timeout default 0); by default slow revoke responders are never evicted, which Ganesha delegations rely on.

name: Client-initiated close with push-sequence handshake
why: Unmount, Ganesha's ceph_set_uuid and the kernel manual reset close sessions with REQUEST_CLOSE carrying the push seq; the MDS persists the close, removes caps and leases and answers CLOSE.
risk: seq < push_seq is dropped silently and the client resends only when another counted message arrives; a counting mismatch stalls unmount for mount_timeout or client_shutdown_timeout.
question: Handle REQUEST_CLOSE before the rank is fully active? C++ waits for up:active, which stalls ceph_set_uuid while pending reclaims hold clientreplay.

name: Counted messages and the session push sequence
why: Both clients count CAPS, LEASE, SNAP and QUOTA messages received on the session, REQUEST_CLOSE is honoured only when the counts match, and both sides restart at 0 on reconnect.
subset: Never send MQuarantineDisable in P0 (libcephfs does not count it).
risk: When many shards send on one session, the count must be taken in send order on that session's connection.

name: Client eviction: OSD blocklist, epoch barrier and session kill
why: Operator client evict (D13) and mgr volumes and dashboard rely on eviction blocklisting the client through the mon, waiting for that OSDMap and raising the OSD epoch barrier before the session is killed.
risk: Killing without the barrier lets other clients use objects the evicted client may still write; the session is killed without CLOSE (mark_down).

name: OSDMap blocklist-driven session kill
why: Blocklisting by anyone (mon, another rank, an admin) must kill the client's sessions on every rank, and blocklisted addresses are rejected at open and dropped before reconnect.

name: Eviction of sessions with oversized metadata
why: Per-session completed-request state can grow without bound (libcephfs never sends oldest_client_tid in RENEWCAPS), so the new session store needs a bound with warning (MDS_CLIENT_OLDEST_TID) and eviction; the 16 MiB omap threshold is C++-format specific.
risk: Unbounded growth affects every tenant that shares the rank's session store.

name: Session termination at rank shutdown
why: A stopping rank (max_mds shrink, D6) must hand off its shards and then close the remaining client sessions with CLOSE; when the last in rank stops (fs set down, max_mds 0) clients are evicted and must remount.

group: MDS failover reconnect and NFS-Ganesha reclaim
name: Reconnect trigger and client-side ordering
why: Cold-standby takeover (D9): clients re-send unanswered requests and early cap flushes, then MClientReconnect on the new connection once the rank shows up:reconnect; the MDS must gather all persisted sessions and accept these messages in that order.
subset: With safe-only replies (D7) no request carries REPLAY in P0; retried requests are answered from the completed-request table.
risk: libcephfs closes its session and drops caps if it never sees up:reconnect, so the rank must stay visibly in up:reconnect while clients reconnect.

group: MDS failover reconnect and NFS-Ganesha reclaim
name: MClientReconnect encodings (v1 to v5, multi-message)
why: The 7.3 kernel sends one v3 message (v5 parts above ~2 GiB) and libcephfs sends v5 with 'more' to an MDS with bit 12.
subset: Decode v3 and v5 (compat 4, payload in the data segment, cap_reconnect_t v2 with flock blob and snap_follows, raw 24-byte realm records in v3, snaprealm_reconnect_t in v5); v1/v2 are out.
risk: A session's reconnect completes only with the part that has no 'more' flag.

group: MDS failover reconnect and NFS-Ganesha reclaim
name: Reconnect processing and outcomes
why: Clients act on OPEN (success), CLOSE (denied: caps and dirty state dropped with -EIO) or REJECT (no session) after a reconnect; the deny reasons (window over, read-only, refuse flag, missing bits) are client visible.
subset: Reconnect OPEN always v7; feature inference is out.

group: MDS failover reconnect and NFS-Ganesha reclaim
name: Snap realm reconnect
why: Snap realms exist in P0 for the root, quota roots and subvolume roots (D8) and clients report their realms in reconnect; a client with an older realm seq must get an MClientSnap UPDATE.
subset: Accept realm records from v3 (raw) and v5 reconnects and send the catch-up UPDATE; no snapshot state in P0.

group: MDS failover reconnect and NFS-Ganesha reclaim
name: Client reactions to MDSMap rank changes
why: Clients decide when to talk to a rank from MDSMap states that the MDS drives through beacons: requests only to up:active (the kernel ignores states <= 0), renewals from up:reconnect, reconnect at up:reconnect (exactly, for libcephfs), metrics only to active ranks.

group: MDS failover reconnect and NFS-Ganesha reclaim
name: Session reclaim (MClientReclaim with CEPH_RECLAIM_RESET)
why: NFS-Ganesha V15.7 calls ceph_start_reclaim(uuid, RESET) at every cmount creation and on nodeid takeover; libcephfs returns -EOPNOTSUPP without MDS bit 10, and FSAL_CEPH then fails the export (it ignores only -ENOENT).
