subset: RESET only: find the session by metadata uuid, require the same auth_name (-EPERM), kill it or evict and blocklist it, reply {0, OSDMap epoch, old addrs} after the kill; unknown uuid gives {0, epoch 0, no addrs}; -EINVAL for an empty uuid or other flags; FLAG_FINISH alone is a no-op. uuid, timeout and auth_name persist across MDS failover. The non-RESET path (dead code) is out.
risk: Every rank 0..num_in-1 must answer (each searches its own sessions), and start_reclaim waits until each one serves; MClientReclaimReply.result is a raw host errno.

name: MClientRequest versioned head (head v1, v2, v3)
why: The 7.3 kernel and libcephfs send MClientRequest v6 with head v3 to an MDS that advertises bits 18 and 20 and FS_BTIME.
subset: Decode head v3 (skip unknown trailing head bytes by struct_len); owner_uid/gid for CREATE, MKNOD, MKDIR, SYMLINK; caller_uid/gid and gid_list for cap checks; mdsmap_epoch ignored. Heads v1/v2 are out.
risk: C++ asserts on owner -1 for a new-inode op; return -EINVAL instead.

name: Legacy 88-byte request head (message version below 4)
why: Legacy: only kernels up to v5.10, Ceph 10.2.x, or clients facing an MDS without FS_BTIME send the 88-byte head.

name: Request message tail: stamp, gid_list, alternate_name, fscrypt fields
why: The v6 tail carries the client stamp (ctime/mtime/btime of mutations, POSIX timestamps), gid_list (supplementary groups for MDS cap checks), alternate_name and the fscrypt fields.
subset: Decode the full v6 tail; use stamp and gid_list. Non-empty alternate_name or fscrypt fields come only with fscrypt or charmap (P2; bits 15 and 22 not advertised): reject (-EOPNOTSUPP) or store them opaquely; alternate_name > 8 KiB gives -ENAMETOOLONG. Message v2-v5 tails are out.
question: Reject or store non-empty alternate_name/fscrypt fields while fscrypt and charmap are P2? libcephfs does not test bit 15, so it can still send fscrypt SETATTRs.

name: Request flags REPLAY, WANT_DENTRY and ASYNC
why: WANT_DENTRY is set on most namespace requests (null-dentry trace on -ENOENT); REPLAY and ASYNC only follow unsafe replies or Dc/Dr directory caps, which P0 never produces (D7).
subset: WANT_DENTRY in full; REPLAY answered from the completed-request table (needed once early replies arrive in P1); ASYNC is P1 (never sent while Dc/Dr are not granted).

name: Request argument union per op
why: Every op's parameters travel in the 56-byte args union.
subset: All members except snapdiff and blockdiff (P1, D8); args.open.pool only from CREATEPOOLID connections; read setattr uid/gid only for SETATTR (C++ reads them for every op).

name: Embedded cap and dentry-lease release records
why: Both clients piggy-back cap and dentry-lease releases on requests and drop the bits locally before sending, so the MDS must apply them before the op instead of waiting for its own revocation.
subset: Ignored for REPLAY requests and for stale mseq or another cap_id.

name: Request data segment per op
why: Creates carry their initial xattrs (POSIX ACLs and LSM labels, D14) and SETXATTR its value in the data segment.
subset: Initial-xattr map for CREATE/MKNOD/MKDIR/SYMLINK and SETXATTR values, decoded fallibly (-EINVAL); the fscrypt last-block SETATTR is P2; the MKSNAP payload is unused (MKSNAP refused with EPERM, D8); SNAP_METADATA is P1.

name: Path encoding on the wire
why: The kernel sends (ino, relative path) with .snap as an empty component and mounts by (1, server path); libcephfs and Ganesha address everything relative to cached inode numbers (#ino).
subset: With snapshots P1, an empty first component still resolves to the snapdir (empty LSSNAP, ENOENT inside).

name: Op code numbering and the write bit
why: The op numbers and the write bit define what clients send and which ops are mutations (read-only refusal, completed-request recording).
subset: All ops current clients send except READDIR_SNAPDIFF, FILE_BLOCKDIFF and SNAP_METADATA (P1) and LOOKUPHASH (not reachable through the libcephfs API); MKSNAP gives EPERM and LSSNAP is empty (D8); internal or unknown ops give -EOPNOTSUPP; may_write uses CEPH_O_* flags; SETFILELOCK is never recorded as completed.

name: Client-chosen inode number (head.ino)
why: head.ino is set only on replays of unsafe-replied requests and on kernel async creates with delegated inos, both P1 (D7); the inode-number reservations must leave room for them.
subset: P0: never trust a non-zero head.ino blindly (C++ asserts); create exactly that ino only if the session owns it, else fail the request.

name: Client-side rank selection and the hints the MDS provides
why: Clients route each request themselves from caps, DirStat auth hints and random choice, so hints must name the rank that owns the shard (D6) and the directory hash must match readdir ordering.
subset: Trivial fragtree (D5): DirStat {frag 0, auth = owning rank or -1, dist empty}, no fragtree splits in InodeStat, dl_dir_hash = 2 (rjenkins) on new directories; no replica dist hints.
risk: Requests still reach any rank (random choice, LOOKUPINO), see F-PROTO-076 and F-PROTO-099.

name: Request forwarding (MClientRequestForward)
why: With several ranks (D6) a request that reaches a rank not owning the shard is answered with MClientRequestForward and the client resends; the MDS never relays.
subset: num_fwd strictly increasing; the target is the shard owner from the shard map (one hop) instead of the C++ discover-or-forward logic.
risk: Kernel BUG_ON if a forward arrives for a tid that already got a reply; -EMULTIHOP if num_fwd does not increase.

name: Retry counters and attempt limits (32BITS_RETRY_FWD)
why: Clients send 32-bit retry and forward counters in head v3 to an MDS with bit 18; a non-zero retry count makes the MDS consult the completed-request table.
subset: The 8-bit widening and the 256-attempt client fallback are legacy.

name: Request identity, tid ordering and requests without a session
why: Requests are identified by (client, tid); Ganesha's shared sessions deliver many concurrent requests out of tid order, and a duplicate of an active request must be dropped.
risk: oldest_client_tid lags behind the slowest outstanding non-SETFILELOCK request, which limits completed-table trimming.

name: MClientReply head and error codes
why: Every request is answered with MClientReply; the kernel selects the extra parser from head.op and both clients require the front to be consumed exactly (libcephfs asserts).
subset: Linux errno values; never -EDQUOT (clients enforce quotas).
risk: Trailing bytes abort libcephfs; replies must go over the session's current connection.

name: Reply trace layout
why: Traces let clients update their caches (dentries, inodes, null dentries on -ENOENT with WANT_DENTRY), and both clients assume the layout exactly.
subset: snapbl carries the target realm's trace; traceless replies only for completed-request hits.
risk: libcephfs hits ceph_abort_msg on a traceless reply whose dentry is no longer linked, and asserts an empty trace in a safe reply that follows an unsafe one.

name: InodeStat versioned encoding (v9, REPLY_ENCODING)
why: Clients with bit 9 parse InodeStat v9 (compat 1, struct_len skip) and the kernel's fixed 221-byte prefix must be byte-identical.
subset: Send v9 with inline_version = CEPH_INLINE_NONE (inline OUT), empty fscrypt fields and optmetadata (P2), zero snap_btime, snap_metadata and rsnaps (P1), dir_pin as set, subvolume_id = the shard/subvolume id (immutable once non-zero).
risk: Never emit struct_compat > 1.

name: Legacy (connection-feature-conditional) reply encodings
why: Legacy: header-less encodings go only to sessions without bit 9 (kernels up to v5.0, Ceph up to 13.2.x).

name: DirStat and LeaseStat records
why: Every trace and readdir entry carries DirStat v1 and LeaseStat v2 (with alternate_name) for bit-9 clients.
subset: DirStat trivial per D5 (frag 0, auth = owner or -1, dist empty); LeaseStat with real leases (VALID|PRIMARY_LINK, 30 s) or null leases; the raw 10-byte lease and header-less DirStat are out.

name: Caps, xattrs and inline data carried inside InodeStat
why: InodeStat carries the cap issued with the reply, the xattr blob and max_size, and clients rely on their versioning rules.
subset: Caps and xattr rules per F-CAPS-009 and F-NS-068; inline_version always CEPH_INLINE_NONE, never 0 (D12 inline OUT; libcephfs asserts inline_version > 0 after an inline GETATTR); readdir stops on the max_bytes estimate.

name: Snap trace encoding and format selection
why: Snap traces accompany every reply, cap IMPORT and MClientSnap even without snapshots (D8); the kernel never sets bit 19 and needs SnapRealmInfo, while libcephfs decodes SnapRealmInfoNew when the MDS advertises bit 19.
subset: Advertise bit 19; old format for sessions without client bit 19, new format (last_modified, change_attr, flags) for those with it; P0 realms carry no snaps.
risk: A snap trace the kernel cannot parse makes it blocklist itself.

name: Readdir and LSSNAP reply format and ordering contract
why: Directory listing is POSIX readdir; the kernel enforces max_entries and non-decreasing hash order from the continuation point and needs the extra on every successful READDIR/LSSNAP.
subset: Entries ordered by rjenkins name hash, then name, even with one frag (D5); resume by path2 or offset_hash; FRAG_END/FRAG_COMPLETE/HASH_ORDER/OFFSET_HASH; LSSNAP empty with FRAG_END in P0. Readdir without REPLY_BITFLAGS (kernels before v4.7) is out.
risk: Kernel BUG_ON for an LSSNAP reply with zero entries and no FRAG_END during NFS get_name, NULL dereference for a successful READDIR without extra, -EIO above max_entries.

name: CREATE reply: created inode and delegated inode ranges
why: Both clients choose the CREATE extra parser from the MDS's DELEG_INO bit, which the MDS must advertise to keep clients on their current path.
subset: Always openc_response_t {created_ino, delegated_inos} for a CREATE that made an inode, with an empty delegated set in P0 (delegation P1, D7); empty extra when CREATE opened an existing file; no extra on MKNOD/MKDIR/SYMLINK replies (kernel -EIO). Raw u64 is out.
risk: A raw u64 fails every kernel CREATE with -EIO and throws in libcephfs; delegated ranges must start at >= 0x1000 and stay <= 8192 per session.

name: GETFILELOCK, GETVXATTR and FILE_BLOCKDIFF extra payloads
why: GETFILELOCK (fcntl F_GETLK, D14) and GETVXATTR (MDS-served ceph.* vxattrs that mgr/volumes reads, e.g. ceph.dir.subvolume) need their exact extra formats; clients send GETVXATTR only to an MDS with bit 17.
subset: GETFILELOCK raw 41-byte ceph_filelock; GETVXATTR ENCODE_START(1,1){string} filling the section exactly; FILE_BLOCKDIFF is P1 (bit 23 not advertised).

name: Early (unsafe) and safe replies
why: Early (unsafe) replies are a latency feature deferred by D7; P0 sends one safe reply after durable commit.
subset: P0: exactly one safe reply per request, carrying trace and extra, with mdsmap_epoch set. P1: at most one unsafe then one traceless safe reply per tid, REPLAY handling.

name: Reply content invariants enforced by clients
why: Clients enforce these properties on every trace, several with a kernel BUG_ON or a libcephfs abort.
risk: Kernel BUG_ON: dentry-trace directory != locked parent (ino or snapid), LOOKUPNAME trace without target; -EREMOTEIO for inos in [0x100, 0x1000); directories must report nlink 1 (libcephfs aborts on POSIX-style counts); version, truncate_seq, time_warp_seq, xattr_version and change_attr monotonic; subvolume_id immutable once non-zero.

name: MClientCaps encoding (v14, xattrs in the middle segment)
why: Caps are the core client consistency protocol; the kernel sends v12 and parses up to v12, libcephfs at main sends and expects v14.
subset: Emit v14 compat 1; decode v12 and v14 (xattr blob in the middle segment, EXPORT/IMPORT peer records for D6); v1/v2 encodings and other decoded versions are legacy; inline fields empty.
risk: Validate xattr_len against the middle segment without asserting (C++ asserts).

name: MClientCapRelease encoding and the OSD epoch barrier
why: Both clients batch cap releases in MClientCapRelease v2 with their OSD epoch barrier, which the MDS must honour before further RADOS ops.

name: MClientLease encoding
why: Dentry leases let clients cache lookups: the MDS revokes them with REVOKE, the kernel renews and acks, libcephfs releases.
subset: P0 never sends MClientLease (every reply carries the null LeaseStat of F-CAPS-038) and drops incoming lease messages without aborting. The REVOKE/RENEW/RELEASE contract (libcephfs accepts only REVOKE) comes with real leases in P1 (F-CAPS-039..044).
risk: Revoke uses mask 1 (userspace numbering) and last = CEPH_NOSNAP.
override: Reconciles PROTO (P0 contract) with CAPS (real dentry leases are P1; directory Fs is the P0 dentry cache).

name: MClientSnap encoding
why: Without snapshots (D8) P0 still creates realms for quota and subvolume roots, tells clients with SPLIT and catches up reconnecting clients with UPDATE.
subset: SPLIT (split inos and realms, trace starting with the split realm) for realm creation and moves, UPDATE for reconnect catch-up; mksnap/rmsnap and global-realm notifications are P1. Counted in push_seq.
risk: libcephfs asserts that nothing follows the trace.

name: MClientQuota encoding
why: Quota enforcement is client side (the MDS never returns EDQUOT), so clients holding caps on a quota realm inode need MClientQuota pushes of usage and limits; subvolume quotas are P0.
subset: The noquota cap state (connections without MDS_QUOTA) is out.
risk: No trailing bytes (libcephfs asserts); counted in push_seq.

name: MClientMetrics encoding and client send rules
why: D11: client metrics must be accepted and must never break a session; with MDS bit 14 the kernel sends MClientMetrics once per second and libcephfs every tick to rank 0.
subset: Advertise bit 14 and metric spec 0-15 (16 with P1 subvolume metrics); decode types 0-16, skip unknown types by their ENCODE_START length, drop while not active; aggregation and forwarding to the mgr per F-QOS-011/012.
risk: A metrics decode error must drop the message, never fault the session's connection.

name: MQuarantineDisable encoding
why: Quarantine is P2 (D12) and only libcephfs (bit 24) would receive this message; no kernel advertises the bit.
risk: If built, do not count it in push_seq: libcephfs does not, and C++ counting stalls its REQUEST_CLOSE.

group: Client-specific expectations (kclient, libcephfs, ceph-fuse, NFS-Ganesha, Samba)
name: Mount flow requirements
why: Mounting depends on GETATTR resolving a root-relative multi-component path (kernel, sent to any rank) and, for libcephfs, GETATTR of every ancestor up to / (quota realms).
risk: The kernel sends the mount GETATTR to a random rank, so any rank must resolve or forward a path that crosses shard roots (D6).

group: Client-specific expectations (kclient, libcephfs, ceph-fuse, NFS-Ganesha, Samba)
name: Inode-number addressed access (NFS file handles, #ino paths, LOOKUPINO)
why: Ganesha file handles and the kernel NFS export resolve inode numbers with LOOKUPINO, LOOKUPPARENT and LOOKUPNAME sent to a random rank (D6: answerable from any rank).
risk: -ESTALE for purged or private inodes; Ganesha handles carry {ino, snapid, fscid} and must stay valid across MDS restarts.

group: Client-specific expectations (kclient, libcephfs, ceph-fuse, NFS-Ganesha, Samba)
name: Inode number ranges clients accept
why: The kernel refuses inode numbers in [0x100, 0x1000) and ceph-fuse aliases inode numbers >= 2^48, so the new allocator (per-shard range leases, D3) must stay inside these bounds.
subset: The 65534-snapids-per-inode ceph-fuse limit matters only with snapshots (P1).

group: Client-specific expectations (kclient, libcephfs, ceph-fuse, NFS-Ganesha, Samba)
name: Shared sessions: NFS-Ganesha and Samba libcephfsd
why: By default a Ganesha daemon holds one session per rank carrying requests of many NFS clients and users for all exports below one cmount path, so one session spans shards (D4) and per-request credentials decide access.
risk: Serializing a session's requests or cap flushes would defeat the goal of scaling synchronous NFS writes across cores; ceph_ll_open runs as uid 0, so root_squash grants refuse Ganesha write opens (C++ behaviour).

group: Client-specific expectations (kclient, libcephfs, ceph-fuse, NFS-Ganesha, Samba)
name: NFS-Ganesha delegations built on caps
why: D12: NFS delegations are cap-based; the MDS has no delegation code, only cap revocation (P0) that tolerates acks delayed up to the delegation timeout.
subset: Nothing delegation-specific; do not evict slow revoke responders by default (F-PROTO-048).

group: Cluster client libraries sharing the MDS identity (MonClient, MgrClient, Objecter)
name: MonClient obligations
why: The MDS needs the monitors for MonMap and config bootstrap, authentication (global id = FSMap gid), service tickets, MDSMap/OSDMap/MgrMap subscriptions, mon commands (blocklist) and the cluster log (transport 7.5).
subset: msgr2 AUTH_MODE_MON only; msgr1 MAuth is out.
risk: Re-authenticating without the previous ticket yields a new global id, which the FSMap treats as a different daemon.

group: Cluster client libraries sharing the MDS identity (MonClient, MgrClient, Objecter)
name: MgrClient obligations
why: status, dashboard and prometheus (D13) read MDS perf counters and task status that the MDS sends in MMgrReport after MMgrOpen and MMgrConfigure.
risk: Values are packed without keys in lexicographic order of the declared paths; any other order shifts every value on the mgr side.

group: Cluster client libraries sharing the MDS identity (MonClient, MgrClient, Objecter)
name: Objecter obligations (OSD client protocol)
why: All metadata persistence goes to RADOS through an Objecter that must follow OSDMaps, place objects exactly like the C++ OSDMap/CRUSH code, resend correctly and honour epoch barriers and -EBLOCKLISTED.
subset: MOSDOp v9 (SERVER_SQUID OSDs); older encodings are out.
risk: librados is a separate identity (own address and nonce): OSD traffic that does not leave from the beaconed address is not fenced when the monitor blocklists a failed MDS.
question: Rust OSD client: own implementation on the MDS messenger, or a librados variant that shares the MDS address vector (F-PROTO-106)?

group: Cluster client libraries sharing the MDS identity (MonClient, MgrClient, Objecter)
name: Fencing identity: one address vector for clients, monitors and OSDs
why: The monitor serves the MDS's mdsmap subscription by matching its address vector against the FSMap and fences a failed MDS by blocklisting that vector at the OSDs, so one addrvec must be beaconed, used for the mon session, presented to OSDs and listened on for clients.
subset: msgr2 CLIENT_IDENT only; the msgr1 banner identity is out.
risk: A mismatch leaves the MDS without its MDSMap, or unfenced after a failover (split brain).

group: Cluster client libraries sharing the MDS identity (MonClient, MgrClient, Objecter)
name: Peer-MDS connections
why: Multi-rank is P0 (D6), so ranks need a transport between them, but only Rust daemons speak it (constraint 3), so policies and protocol are free.
subset: msgr1 protocol 36 and its race rules are out.

name: Cap bit model and composite masks
why: Fixed wire layout of cap bits and composite masks shared with kclient and libcephfs (ceph_fs.h); every cap message, reply cap and getattr mask uses it (capabilities 3.1).
risk: Never grant Fa. On directories Fc and Fr mean Dc and Dr; the whole CEPH_CAP_ANY_DIR_OPS mask (Fc|Fr|Fa|Fl) must stay off directory caps until async dirops (P1).

name: Open mode to wanted caps
why: The MDS must derive wanted caps from the open mode exactly as clients do (ceph_flags_to_mode, ceph_caps_for_mode); the kclient re-registers missing wanted bits with OPEN requests every 5 s (capabilities 3.8).
risk: libcephfs lists Fr|Fc in wanted for a directory opened with open(); on directories these are Dr|Dc and must not be granted in P0.

name: Capability record, cap ids and sequence numbers
why: cap_id, seq, issue_seq and mseq rules are the client-visible consistency protocol: kclient treats seq <= cap->seq as pre-IMPORT, takes issue_seq only from replies and IMPORT, and messages with another cap_id or older mseq are stale (kclient 7 item 13, capabilities 7 items 1-2).
subset: Contract on the counters and confirm_receipt semantics; the in-memory record is free and is never persisted.
risk: Seqs must rise per cap in delivery order: in a multi-core MDS all messages for one (inode, client) must be serialised onto the session connection in seq order. New cap_ids must exceed every id reported in reconnects.

name: Lock-state-derived allowed caps
why: The C++ lock tables are internal (D16), but the cap combinations they produce are the coherency contract: at most one holder of any x bit, s bits revoked before a conflicting change, shared writers get Fr|Fw without Fc/Fb, Fl only if wanted, no dir-op bits on directories (lock-types 7 item 1).
subset: Compute allowed caps from the new engine's per-inode state. Legacy NOINLINE/NOPOOLNS step out (F-CAPS-007); replica column OUT (F-CAPS-035); quiesce and quarantine masks come with QOS (P2).
risk: Granting an x bit to two clients, or Fc/Fb while several clients write, silently corrupts client caches.

name: Loner selection (exclusive client)
why: Loner selection is internal, but its outcome is the main single-client performance contract: a sole writer must get Fx|Fb|Fc (buffered I/O, local size and mtime), otherwise every write goes synchronously to the OSDs (capabilities 3.3).
risk: Do not carry over the C++ rule that directories with subtree-root dirfrags never get a loner (no Fx on pinned subvolume roots): a shard root is never split.

name: Wanted-cap-driven stable-state policy
why: Internal policy that decides cached, buffered or synchronous I/O (one writer buffered, writers plus others uncached Fr|Fw, readers Fs|Fc|Fr); clients observe only the caps they get (capabilities 3.3).
subset: Policy is free as long as F-CAPS-004 combinations hold; a read-only file system grants only shared caps.

name: Cap restrictions for old clients (connection feature bits)
why: Legacy (old-clients): only connections lacking feature bits 40, 58 or 47 are restricted; the 7.3 kernel and libcephfs advertise all three.

name: Lazy I/O cap (Fl)
why: LazyIO is P2 (D12). Fl is issued only when wanted (CEPH_FILE_MODE_LAZY), so never granting it is safe: clients keep normal coherent I/O.
risk: Until implemented, never grant Fl.

group: Cap issue, revocation and client cap messages
name: Caps in request replies
why: Every reply trace inode and readdir entry carries ceph_mds_reply_cap (caps, wanted, cap_id, seq, mseq, realm, AUTH flag); clients take max_size only from an AUTH cap and rstat or dir_pin only from AUTH or newer replies (kclient 3.8.2), and a reply never revokes.
subset: Legacy inline-data payload out (always CEPH_INLINE_NONE). Pre-granting liked caps is policy but cheap to keep.
risk: InodeStat inline_version must be CEPH_INLINE_NONE, never 0 (libcephfs asserts). A reply must never remove bits.

group: Cap issue, revocation and client cap messages
name: New caps on open, create, mknod and mkdir
why: Open, create, mknod and mkdir must create or extend the client's cap (wanted = caps for the mode) and return it in the reply; the creator owning the new inode's x caps and an initial [0, stripe_unit] write range avoids an immediate revoke and max_size round trip.
subset: With D7 the reply follows the durable commit, so the C++ exception of a range granted before the create is durable disappears.
risk: cap_id 1 for a new inode matches the kclient's fabricated async-create cap (P1).

group: Cap issue, revocation and client cap messages
name: Cap grant and revoke messages (GRANT/REVOKE)
why: Clients require REVOKE whenever bits are removed and answer every REVOKE with a cap message, possibly only after writeback or page-cache invalidation; a GRANT may carry only max_size or field updates (capabilities 7 item 3).
subset: Keep the nlink 0 rule: add Ls to wanted and push a grant so clients drop the unlinked inode (F-BG-008).
risk: A message that revokes must never add bits. Every cap message carries osd_epoch_barrier and counts toward the session push_seq.

group: Cap issue, revocation and client cap messages
name: Client cap message processing (handle_client_caps)
why: UPDATE, FLUSH, DROP, RELEASE and RENEW are all cap updates: revoke acks (confirm_receipt with seq), wanted changes and dirty flushes; clients rely on stale messages (other cap_id, older mseq, non-owner rank) being dropped and re-send flushes after IMPORT or reconnect.
subset: Mask the client's caps with issued before confirm_receipt (the kernel sends its implemented set). C++ frozen-inode deferral becomes the shard-migration quiesce; snapflush branches P1.
risk: A lost or mis-applied revoke ack stalls every conflicting operation with no timeout.

group: Cap issue, revocation and client cap messages
name: Wanted caps tracking (issue_seq rule)
why: Wanted is replaced only when issue_seq == last_issue, otherwise only extended, so a stale update cannot undo a newer open; otherwise the kclient falls back to OPEN retries every 5 s (capabilities 3.8).
subset: OpenFileTable logging is C++ storage (D2); reopening files with caps after failover belongs to the reconnect design.

group: Cap issue, revocation and client cap messages
name: Xattr blob and inline data carried on caps
why: Clients serve getxattr/listxattr locally under Xs and setxattr locally under Xx when the blob fits max_xattr_size, so the blob and xattr_version must travel on grants and replies and be accepted from flushes (capabilities 3.7).
subset: Xattr half only; the inline-data half is legacy (deprecated inline_data flag) and out.
question: C++ ignores an oversize flushed blob but still bumps xattr_version, so the client's change is lost silently; keep that or reject differently?

group: Cap issue, revocation and client cap messages
name: Truncate notification (CEPH_CAP_OP_TRUNC)
why: A shrinking truncation must be pushed to every cap holder (CEPH_CAP_OP_TRUNC with truncate_seq/size) after it commits; clients truncate their page caches from it.
risk: The kernel WARNs if truncate_seq rises while it still holds Fr or Fl: revoke everything but Fc|Fb before a shrinking truncate commits (capabilities 7 item 13).

group: Dirty metadata flush, max_size and file size recovery
name: Dirty metadata flush and FLUSH_ACK
why: Buffered writers and Ax/Xx/Fx holders report size, times, mode, owner and xattrs only through cap flushes; FLUSH_ACK must follow the durable commit (D7) and the kernel treats it as cumulative per inode (capabilities 7 item 5). Ganesha's setattr-then-sync path depends on it.
subset: Field rules kept (size only grows, Fw times only newer, Fx may move mtime back, xattr version newer). Legacy parts out: inline data, feature gating of change_attr/btime (always apply).
risk: Acks for one inode must leave in commit order; flushed values must not be visible to other clients before commit.
question: C++ applies flushed Ax/Xx fields without checking that the cap holds those bits or the client's MDS auth caps, and drops atime unless Fx is dirty (kernel atime-forward under Fw is lost). Validate dirty against issued x bits and fix atime?

group: Dirty metadata flush, max_size and file size recovery
name: Flush idempotency (completed_flushes, oldest_flush_tid)
why: Clients re-send unacked flushes with their original tids after IMPORT and reconnect, and Fx/Ax fields are not monotonic, so applied flushes must be recognised exactly once across retransmission and failover.
subset: Durable completed flush tids per session, trimmed by oldest_flush_tid, recorded with the cap update in the shard WAL; MDS_CLIENT_OLDEST_TID health and clog warning as in F-ADM-075. SessionMap format out (D2).
question: Flush tids are per client session while updates land in per-shard WALs: the completed set must be rebuilt after a rank failure and follow a shard on migration (or all acks must precede EXPORT on the connection).

group: Dirty metadata flush, max_size and file size recovery
name: Synchronous flush and journal-flush heuristics
why: fsync, Ganesha COMMIT and the sync Ganesha runs after every SETATTR wait for a FLAG_SYNC flush ack whenever metadata is buffered in caps; with per-shard WAL group commit (D7) the ack comes at commit, not after the C++ 5 s tick (motivating use case: synchronous NFS writes across cores).
subset: Commit FLAG_SYNC flushes, and flushes someone waits on, immediately; the C++ _need_flush_mdlog and tick heuristics are dropped.

group: Dirty metadata flush, max_size and file size recovery
name: max_size and per-client writeable ranges (client_ranges)
why: A client may write only below max_size, takes it only from its AUTH cap (from a GRANT only when it includes a file-write bit) and blocks until a GRANT raises it; the range must be durable before it is granted so size recovery knows how far to probe (capabilities 3.9).
subset: client_ranges persisted in the new inode format (D2); the growth formula is policy.
risk: Never advertise a max_size above the durable range; a raised range is pushed with a GRANT (seq+1) to every Fw|Fb holder.

group: Dirty metadata flush, max_size and file size recovery
name: File size recovery after loss of a writer
why: When a client holding a writeable range dies or is evicted, or a rank fails over, size and mtime must be recovered by probing data objects up to the range, otherwise acknowledged writes past the recorded size disappear (durability, D9).
subset: Outcome: size = max(recorded, probed), never shrink, block conflicting access until done, bounded parallel probes. C++ PRE_SCAN/SCAN lock states are internal.
risk: C++ marks the whole rank damaged on a probe error; contain it per shard (D10).

name: Snapshot COW of cap state and SNAP_SYNC gating
why: Snapshots are P1 (D8); P0 refuses MKSNAP, so no written inode is ever COWed. Design the cap side together with the snapshot redesign.

name: FLUSHSNAP / FLUSHSNAP_ACK protocol
why: Comes with snapshots (D8): clients send FLUSHSNAP only for capsnaps, which need a new snapshot in their realm.
risk: If one arrives in P0, ack it from a rank where the client holds a cap, echoing snap_follows and tid (libcephfs asserts otherwise).

name: Null snapflush inference
why: Only needed while snapflushes are pending (snapshots, D8); P0 ignores CEPH_CLIENT_CAPS_PENDING_CAPSNAP.

name: Snapflush nudge
why: Forcing slow snapflushes only matters once snapshots exist (D8).

name: XLOCKSNAP: truncate with pending snapflush
why: Truncation must wait for buffered data owed to a pending snapshot; only relevant with snapshots (D8). The XLOCKSNAP state itself is internal (D16).

group: Cap release, staleness, recall and late revocation
name: Batched cap release (MClientCapRelease)
why: Clients give up caps through MClientCapRelease (and embedded releases); a release whose issue_seq < last_issue must not remove a cap re-issued meanwhile, and the kclient also releases caps named by GRANT/REVOKE/IMPORT for inodes it lacks (capabilities 3.12).
subset: Removing a cap also drops that client's fcntl/flock locks and writeable range (needs size recovery if the client was killed).
risk: Removing a cap on a stale issue_seq loses a cap the client believes it holds.

group: Cap release, staleness, recall and late revocation
name: Cap and dentry-lease releases embedded in requests
why: kclient and libcephfs drop caps (and dentry leases) inside requests so the requester's own Fs or lease need not be revoked; the MDS applies them before locking and re-issues suppressed grants at cleanup (lock-types 7 item 9).
subset: Skipped for replayed requests. The dentry-lease part is a no-op until real leases exist (P1).

group: Cap release, staleness, recall and late revocation
name: Stale-session cap handling
why: CEPH_SESSION_STALE makes clients treat all caps as p; revoking write caps from a stale client evicts (blocklists) it, other bits are force-revoked, and RENEWCAPS re-issues caps with a GRANT then a REVOKE (capabilities 3.13, kclient 7 item 4).
subset: Legacy full re-issue for clients without LAZY_CAP_WANTED out. Writer loss triggers size recovery (F-CAPS-022).
risk: Other clients must not use caps before the blocklist epoch: stamp the new osd_epoch_barrier on later cap messages.

group: Cap release, staleness, recall and late revocation
name: Late revocation warnings, health and eviction
why: With no lock-level timeout, the late-revoke health warning is the operator's only signal that one client blocks others; mon, mgr and dashboard show MDS_CLIENT_LATE_RELEASE (operator essential, D13).
subset: P0: per-client late-revoke tracking, MDS_CLIENT_LATE_RELEASE(_MANY) in the beacon health (F-ADM-075), clog warning with backoff. Eviction after mds_cap_revoke_eviction_timeout (default off) is P2 (F-PROTO-048).

group: Cap release, staleness, recall and late revocation
name: Cache-pressure cap recall (CEPH_SESSION_RECALL_STATE)
why: Caps pin MDS memory; RECALL_STATE with max_caps is how the MDS bounds per-client cap counts with many clients, and MDS_CLIENT_RECALL is a standard health warning; clients shrink only as fast as applications drop inodes (libcephfs 7.1 item 18).
subset: Wire: CEPH_SESSION_RECALL_STATE max_caps, release accounting, MDS_CLIENT_RECALL(_MANY). Thresholds and decay throttles redesigned for per-shard memory accounting (D3).
risk: Recall never evicts: the MDS must keep working with clients that cannot shrink.

group: Cap release, staleness, recall and late revocation
name: Cap re-establishment after MDS failover (cap side)
why: Cold standby takeover with reconnect is P0 (D9): caps are rebuilt from reconnect records (client cap_id, reported issued, seq/issue_seq/mseq zero), cap ids are raised above every reported id, and flushes re-sent early during reconnect are accepted.
subset: Mask reported issued bits with what the new policy allows (strip dir-op bits and Fa). Choosing lock states from caps (F-CLU-090) is redesigned.

name: Replica caps and MInodeFileCaps
why: With whole-shard ownership only the owner rank issues caps (D5, no replicas) and MInodeFileCaps is MDS-to-MDS; clients accept a reply whose cap record is empty and reach the owner through routing and forwards.
question: Who owns a shard-root inode: the child shard (keeps dirstat, quota, layout local; recommended) or, as in C++, the parent shard's rank? If the parent answers lookups of the shard root without caps, AUTH-only fields (max_size, rstat, dir_pin) still come from the owner.

name: Cap migration to clients (EXPORT / IMPORT)
why: Live whole-shard migration and per-rank failover are P0 (D6, D9); EXPORT/IMPORT is the only way to move a client's auth cap between ranks without losing dirty state (also used when reconnect caps reach a non-owner, F-CLU-088).
subset: EXPORT peer {importer cap_id, importer last_seq+1, mseq+1, rank}; IMPORT seq equal to that issue_seq, FLAG_AUTH, sent by the owner only; peer.mds = -1 drops the cap. Cross-rank rename use disappears (EXDEV, D4).
risk: kclient adds every IMPORTed cap as AUTH and ignores an EXPORT whose cap_id does not match its cap from that rank.

name: Dentry lease issue
why: Every trace dentry and readdir entry must carry a LeaseStat, but correctness does not need real leases: clients fall back to directory Fs with shared_gen or to a LOOKUP, which is what they already do whenever C++ sends mask 0.
subset: Always encode the no-lease record (mask 0, duration 0, seq 0, alternate_name); real 30 s leases P1.
question: Real leases help only when several clients share a directory that is being modified (no Fs): path walks there re-LOOKUP every component. They add lease revocation to every namespace mutation; measure before P1. PROTO rates MClientLease (F-PROTO-093) P0 contract; with this choice P0 only drops unexpected lease messages.

name: Negative dentry leases
why: Performance only: without a lease or directory Fs the kclient simply does not keep the negative dentry (kclient 3.8.3); comes with real leases.

name: CEPH_LEASE_PRIMARY_LINK hint
why: The kclient uses it only for async unlink (P1, D7) and for reconnect path hints; with no real leases in P0 it is never set (C++ also omits it from mask-0 records).
risk: Without it the kclient omits regular-file paths from CLIENT_RECONNECT; reconnect must locate inodes by number.

name: Lease renewal (CEPH_MDS_LEASE_RENEW)
why: Renewal (kclient only) exists only for real leases (P1); with none issued in P0 no MClientLease arrives.
risk: Never abort on an unexpected lease action (C++ calls ceph_abort): drop it.

name: Lease revocation on dentry change
why: Needed once real leases are issued: every lease on a dentry must be revoked and acked (kclient REVOKE_ACK, libcephfs RELEASE) or expire before its linkage changes.
risk: libcephfs asserts the action is REVOKE; a silent client delays a dentry change up to the lease duration.

name: Lease expiry and cleanup
why: Server-side lease state, TTL expiry and cleanup on stale or closed sessions come with real leases (P1); memory-only.

name: Infinite leases on snapshot listings
why: LSSNAP returns no entries in P0 (D8), so no snapshot lease record is ever sent; comes with snapshots.

name: Directory-wide dentry validity via Fs
why: Without real leases this is the clients' only dentry cache: kclient and libcephfs trust cached dentries and answer ENOENT locally while holding Fs on a complete directory, so the MDS must revoke Fs from every other client before any namespace change in that directory (leases 3.1.6).
risk: A missed revoke gives other clients stale lookups or false ENOENT (silent POSIX violation). Directory caps must never include Fc/Fr/Fa/Fl.

group: Lock caches, async directory operations and delegated inode numbers
name: Directory-operation cap bits Dc and Dr
why: Kernel async dirops are P1 (D7); the C++ MDS itself never grants Dc/Dr today (leases 8 G1).
risk: P0 must mask CEPH_CAP_ANY_DIR_OPS out of every directory cap: the kclient (nowsync default) and libcephfs (directories opened with open()) put these bits in wanted.

group: Lock caches, async directory operations and delegated inode numbers
name: Lock cache creation
why: Async dirops are P1 (D7). MDLockCache is a C++ mechanism (D16); what to redesign is the promise behind Fx|Dc/Dr: the holder's creates and unlinks in that directory proceed without waiting on other clients.

group: Lock caches, async directory operations and delegated inode numbers
name: Lock cache attachment
why: Request-locking fast path of the C++ lock cache (D16); a P1 Dc/Dr design (F-CAPS-048) defines its own. Never exercised today (leases 8 G1).

group: Lock caches, async directory operations and delegated inode numbers
name: Lock cache invalidation and lifecycle
why: The client-visible part (Dc/Dr revoked when another client touches the directory, on shard migration, on cap loss) comes with async dirops (P1, D7).

group: Lock caches, async directory operations and delegated inode numbers
name: Forced auth pins for lock-cache requests
why: The mechanism is internal (D16), but its hazard stays with P1 async dirops: the kclient acks a Dc/Dr revoke only after its in-flight async ops are answered, so a shard quiesce or migration must keep serving those ops.

group: Lock caches, async directory operations and delegated inode numbers
name: Forcing async-operation flush for readers
why: With async dirops (P1) another client's access to the directory must first revoke Fx/Dc/Dr from the async client, whose ack waits for its in-flight ops, so readers see their results.

group: Lock caches, async directory operations and delegated inode numbers
name: Per-session inode-number preallocation
why: Per-session preallocated numbers exist for early create replies and delegation, both P1 (D7); P0 allocates from per-shard range leases (D3). D7 asks to design these reservations now.
subset: SessionMap and InoTable formats out (D2).
risk: C++ asserts on a client-named ino it does not own (leases 8 G4); never trust head.ino blindly.

group: Lock caches, async directory operations and delegated inode numbers
name: Inode-number delegation to clients
why: Delegated inode ranges serve only kclient async create (P1, D7); libcephfs discards them.
subset: P0: DELEG_INO (bit 13) is advertised and every CREATE reply carries openc_response_t with an empty delegated set (F-PROTO-087).
risk: Delegated ranges must start at >= 0x1000, stay <= 8192 per session and never repeat.

group: Lock caches, async directory operations and delegated inode numbers
name: Asynchronous create (kclient)
why: Async create is P1 (D7) and never happens against the C++ MDS today (leases 8 G1); it starts only when an MDS grants Fx|Dc with delegated inos.
risk: Once enabled, the reply must create exactly head.ino with caps consistent with the kclient's fabricated inode (cap_id 1, max_size = stripe_unit).

group: Lock caches, async directory operations and delegated inode numbers
name: Asynchronous unlink (kclient)
why: Async unlink is P1 (D7); it needs Fx|Dr plus PRIMARY_LINK from real leases, and never happens against the C++ MDS today.

group: Lock caches, async directory operations and delegated inode numbers
name: Replay of unsafe and async creates after failover
why: REPLAY requests follow only unsafe replies and ASYNC ones only Dc grants, both P1 (D7); in P0 clients merely retry unanswered requests.
subset: P0: a retried completed CREATE is answered from the durable completed-request table with the created ino (namespace/membership entries).

name: Per-object lock catalogue
why: C++ lock partition and per-object order (D16); clients see only the four cap groups (F-CAPS-001) and the new engine chooses its own granularity. Dead-code legacy parts out.

name: SimpleLock state machine (sm_simplelock)
why: C++ state machine (D16); its client-visible outcomes (shared caps when readable, exclusive caps for one client, s revoked before a change) are kept by F-CAPS-004/006/067. Dead-code legacy part out.

name: ScatterLock state machine (nestlock, dirfragtreelock)
why: Scatterlocks exist because one directory's stats are updated on several ranks; directories are not split across ranks (D5) and cross-shard rstat aggregation is a new mechanism (D4). Dead TSYN family out.

name: FileLock state machine (sm_filelock)
why: C++ state machine (D16); the F-cap sets per sharing mode are kept by F-CAPS-004/006 and size recovery by F-CAPS-022.

name: XSYN: rdlock while a loner keeps buffered data
why: Performance refinement without contract: when another client stats a file a sole writer buffers, C++ revokes Fs/Fx/Fr/Fw but lets the writer keep Fc|Fb, so no writeback is forced; the new cap policy can add an equivalent later.

name: Local locks (versionlock, quiescelock)
why: versionlock pipelining and the quiescelock are C++ mechanisms (D16); quiesce itself is P2 (QOS).

name: Gather engine (eval_gather) and cap revocation gather
why: Its contract is client-visible: a conflicting operation waits until every client's issued (not merely pending) conflicting bits are acked or force-revoked, with no lock-level timeout, and clients keep only what the transition allows meanwhile (lock-types 7 items 1 and 7).
risk: Completing on pending instead of issued lets two clients hold conflicting caps.

name: Lock-mode grant rules (rdlock / wrlock / xlock compatibility)
why: Superseded by the S/X/IS/IX lock manager (D16); the POSIX atomicity it serves is owned by the namespace entries.

name: Lock-request-driven state changes and journal nudging
why: Lock kicking is internal (D16), and with commit before reply plus group commit (D7) there are no early-replied lock holders to nudge.

name: Scatter data exchange and writebehind
why: Multi-rank dirstat/rstat gathering inside one directory disappears (D5); cross-shard rstat aggregation is a new mechanism (D4, tenancy).

name: Scatter nudging
why: Same as F-CAPS-070; rstat freshness toward clients is owned by tenancy entries (F-SNAP-036).

name: Inter-MDS lock protocol (MLock)
why: MDS-to-MDS only; without replicated lock states there is nothing to synchronise. Dead-code legacy part out.

name: Replica-initiated lock state requests
why: Replica lock requests disappear with whole-shard ownership (D5, D16).

name: Lock state across replication, migration and rejoin
why: Lock states never cross ranks in the new design; shard migration ships cap and file-lock state instead (F-MULTI-006).

name: acquire_locks and lock vectors
why: Superseded by the transaction engine's plan and acquire steps (D16).

name: Per-object lock order
why: C++ deadlock-avoidance convention (D16).

name: Cross-object ordering rules and no upgrades
why: C++ deadlock-avoidance rules (D16).
risk: The new engine must give rename and link the same deadlock freedom by its own ordering or detection.

name: Ancestor snaplock/policylock try-rdlocks and layout inheritance
why: Mechanism (D16); intention locks on ancestors in the new engine serialise policy changes (layout, quota, snapshots) against operations below. Layout inheritance itself is owned by namespace and tenancy entries.

name: Path traversal locking and path helpers
why: C++ path-locking helpers (D16); path resolution and routing are owned by namespace and cache entries.

name: Implicit versionlock (pipelining and peer rollback)
why: Projection pipelining and peer rollback guard of the C++ MDS (D16, no cross-rank 2PC in P0 per D4).

name: Implicit quiescelock wrlock
why: Lock side of quiesce (F-QOS-045), which is P2 (D12); the barrier would be built into the new engine differently.

name: Local auth pins on locked objects
why: Auth pins and freezing are C++ internals (D16).

name: Remote auth pins and the rename frozen auth pin
why: Remote auth pins serve cross-rank operations; no cross-rank namespace transactions in P0 (D4).

name: Remote xlocks and remote wrlocks
why: Remote xlocks and wrlocks serve cross-rank link, unlink and rename (D4: EXDEV across shards).

name: Remote lock teardown and peer failure
why: Teardown of cross-rank lock state (D4, D16).

name: FIFO lock waiters with synchronous wake-up
why: C++ waiter queues and synchronous wake-ups (D16).
risk: Fairness and head-of-line blocking become properties of the new scheduler (per-shard fair scheduling, D11).

name: Non-blocking lock helpers
why: C++ lock helpers (D16).

name: Freeze versus auth-pin deadlock breaker
why: Freeze versus auth-pin deadlock is a C++ freezing artefact (D16).
risk: Shard migration still needs a timeout and cancel when its quiesce cannot drain (F-MULTI-022).

name: Lock waits on a degraded cluster
why: Waits for replicated lock recovery disappear with whole-shard ownership and per-shard recovery (D5, D16).

name: xlock lifecycle
why: C++ xlock mechanics (D16); the creator's immediate exclusive caps are kept by F-CAPS-010.

name: XLOCKDONE: read-your-own-unsafe-writes
why: Exists only with early (unsafe) replies, P1 (D7): the same client may build on its unsafe change while other clients wait for durability.
risk: P0 invariant regardless: no client sees another client's non-durable metadata through replies or caps (hold write intents until commit; C++'s only exception is MClientQuota from projected rstat).

name: Early-reply rdlock release and journal flush policy
why: Only meaningful with early replies (P1, D7): decides how long others wait behind an unsafe request and keeps layout or snapshot changes ordered after unsafe requests below.

name: Lock release at safe reply and cleanup
why: C++ lock release order (D16).

name: Cap and lease counters and dumps
why: Default mgr flows read cap counters: fs status and telemetry use mds_mem.cap, the dashboard and the shipped Grafana dashboard use mds.caps, and session ls num_caps is an operator essential (D13).
subset: P0: mds.caps and mds_mem.cap (priority high enough to reach the mgr), session ls num_caps and num_leases. Other counters and the dump inode cap view P2.

name: Lock state dumps and lock-related op events
why: Dumps of C++ lock states are internal (D13: internal dumps OUT or P2); ops in flight (P0, ADM) should still say what an op waits for (lock, revoke from which client).
subset: C++ lock-state dumps and event strings are not reproduced; new event strings are free.

group: Request intake, dispatch and execution model
name: Client op set and dispatch switch
why: The op set is the client metadata API; every op that kclient, libcephfs, Ganesha and the mgr modules send in default flows must be handled (request-lifecycle 3.5, POSIX contract 5.1).
subset: P0 full: LOOKUP, GETATTR, LOOKUPHASH, LOOKUPINO, LOOKUPPARENT, LOOKUPNAME, GETVXATTR, SETATTR, SETXATTR, RMXATTR, READDIR, OPEN, CREATE, MKNOD, MKDIR, SYMLINK, LINK, UNLINK, RMDIR, RENAME, SETFILELOCK, GETFILELOCK. P0 fixed answers (D8): LOOKUPSNAP -> ENOENT, LSSNAP -> empty list, MKSNAP -> EPERM. DUMMY and 0x1500-0x150f -> EOPNOTSUPP. P1: RMSNAP, RENAMESNAP, SNAP_METADATA (P0 ENOENT), READDIR_SNAPDIFF, FILE_BLOCKDIFF (P0 EOPNOTSUPP). P2: SETLAYOUT, SETDIRLAYOUT. Keep may_write() = write bit or OPEN with O_CREAT/O_TRUNC.
risk: READDIR_SNAPDIFF and FILE_BLOCKDIFF carry the write bit (EROFS on a read-only MDS, recorded as completed).

group: Request intake, dispatch and execution model
name: Request intake gating by rank state and session
why: Clients rely on requests being held (not failed) until the MDS can serve them and on silent drops for sessionless or closed sessions; gating should be per shard so one shard's recovery does not stall the others (multi-tenant replay goal).
subset: Queueing of REPLAY/ASYNC requests during reconnect is P1 (D7: P0 sends no unsafe replies and grants no Dc/Dr). Retried requests (num_retry > 0) must be held and checked against completed requests in P0.

group: Request intake, dispatch and execution model
name: Request identity and in-flight duplicate detection
why: Requests are identified by (client entity, tid); a resent request that is still executing must not run twice, and the client's request stamp becomes the op stamp for every time the mutation sets.
subset: The peer-request forward race is C++-internal and OUT.

group: Request intake, dispatch and execution model
name: Re-entrant handler execution (restart from the top)
why: C++ restart-from-the-top execution under mds_lock (D16); the transaction engine replaces it and no peer sees it.
risk: Do not copy its consequence that a woken request skips checks (quarantine wakeups, request-lifecycle 8 item 6).

group: Request intake, dispatch and execution model
name: Per-op path resolution and locking helpers
why: Path resolution and per-op lock planning are needed (resolve -> plan -> lock in the transaction engine); the client-visible parts are the error codes and the null-dentry trace on ENOENT with WANT_DENTRY.
subset: Must traverse multi-component and #ino-relative paths (kclient expectations 7 item 7; mounts of a subvolume path start at /) and forward at shard boundaries; two-path ops require depth-1 paths (EINVAL). C++ lock-ordering helpers are internal (D16).

group: Request intake, dispatch and execution model
name: GETATTR/LOOKUP batching (BatchOp)
why: Coalescing of identical GETATTR/LOOKUP under mds_lock; superseded by concurrent lock-free reads. No peer depends on it.
risk: If reintroduced, each follower must run its own access and quarantine checks (C++ leaks attributes across MDS-cap restrictions).

group: Request intake, dispatch and execution model
name: Request kill and abort
why: In-flight requests of a closed or evicted session, or of a shard being exported or stopped, must be terminated cleanly, while a mutation already committing still completes durably.
subset: Admin 'op kill' is P2 (F-ADM-036, D13); quiesce- and quarantine-driven kills follow those P2 features.

group: Request intake, dispatch and execution model
name: Internal (MDS-originated) requests
why: C++ reuse of the request machinery for fragmentation, export, scrub, quiesce and quarantine work (D16); the Rust MDS has its own internal transaction types. Client-sent internal op codes get EOPNOTSUPP (F-NS-001).

group: Request intake, dispatch and execution model
name: Request-path fault injection and test kill points
why: QA kill points and delays tied to C++ code positions, used only by qa suites. The Rust MDS needs its own failpoints for crash-recovery testing, which is test infrastructure, not a catalog feature.

name: Journaled mutation commit and safe reply
why: D7: a mutation is acknowledged only after durable commit and other clients observe it only after commit; this safe reply is the durability point fsync, syncfs and NFS COMMIT rely on.
subset: Per-shard WAL with group commit; only safe replies in P0.
risk: Acknowledging before durability loses acknowledged mutations on failover, since P0 has no clientreplay.

name: Early (unsafe) replies
why: Latency feature (D7). Wire contract when added: one unsafe reply with the full trace, then a traceless safe reply; only the requester sees the uncommitted state.
subset: The P0 recovery state machine and inode-number reservations must allow adding it (D7).
risk: libcephfs asserts that a safe reply following an unsafe one has an empty trace (Client.cc:1781-1785).

name: Completed-request table and idempotent retries/replays
why: Even with safe-only replies, clients resend unanswered requests after a failover or session reconnect; a committed but unacknowledged UNLINK, RENAME or O_EXCL CREATE must be answered, not re-executed (wrong ENOENT/EEXIST).
subset: Record (client, tid, created ino) atomically with the mutation in the shard WAL; trim by oldest_client_tid (which excludes SETFILELOCK); the records must move with the shard on migration (C++ keeps them per rank, request-lifecycle 8 item 1).
risk: kclient fails a reply with EIO if extra_bl is non-empty for MKNOD/MKDIR/SYMLINK (C++ bug, request-lifecycle 8 item 26): answer such retries with a trace or an empty extra.

name: Replay of unsafe requests after an MDS restart
why: Replays exist only for requests that got an unsafe reply and for kernel async creates, both P1 (D7).
subset: When added: no early reply, reuse head.ino, traceless reply with the reconnected cap, completed ones answered from F-NS-012.

name: Per-op reply trace contents
why: Traces are how clients learn results and receive caps and leases; kclient and libcephfs parse them strictly.
risk: kclient BUG_ON if the dentry trace's directory is not the request's locked parent (rename: destination dir) or a LOOKUPNAME trace lacks the target; extra_bl only for CREATE/READDIR/LSSNAP/GETFILELOCK/GETVXATTR; the trace must be consumed exactly (EIO otherwise).

name: On-demand journal flush for fsync, syncfs and sync writes
why: fsync, syncfs and Ganesha's ceph_ll_sync_inode (NFS COMMIT) wait for durability through FLUSH_MDLOG and sync cap flushes (POSIX contract 3.3.10).
subset: With safe-only replies a FLUSH_MDLOG has nothing unsafe to wait for but must be accepted; sync cap flushes commit at once. Flush only the shards involved, not the whole rank (NFS sync scaling goal).

group: Validation gates and POSIX error ordering
name: Read-only and snapshot EROFS gates
why: EROFS for writes on a read-only MDS, for mutations under .snap paths (clients can send them in P0) and in MDS-private directories.
subset: Read-only state should be per shard (D10).

group: Validation gates and POSIX error ordering
name: Full metadata pool gate
why: Keeps a full metadata pool from wedging the file system while deletes still free space; the 'f' auth-cap flag (MAY_FULL) lets privileged clients proceed (F-STORE-099).
subset: Refuse space-consuming ops (CREATE, SYMLINK, LINK, RENAME, SETXATTR, RMXATTR, SETATTR growth; MKNOD/MKDIR too if the team agrees) with one ENOSPC; do not copy the EACCES-then-ENOSPC double reply.

group: Validation gates and POSIX error ordering
name: Create/remove name gates and their error order
why: Fixed POSIX error order for created and removed names (EINVAL, EROFS, EEXIST or ENOTEMPTY for . and .., ENOENT, EEXIST) and exactly one winner among concurrent creators; libcephfs relies on the MDS for these errors.
subset: Quarantine wait is P2 (D12); no NAME_MAX in the MDS (F-NS-088).

group: Validation gates and POSIX error ordering
name: Directory entry limits (ENOSPC)
why: Admin ENOSPC limits: mds_dir_max_entries is off by default and the dirfrag-size limit is meaningless with one frag per directory (D5).
subset: Optional mds_dir_max_entries only; drop mds_bal_fragment_size_max checks.
risk: UNLINK, RMDIR and RENAME must never fail with ENOSPC because an internal stray area is full (C++ stray-dirfrag artifact).

group: Validation gates and POSIX error ordering
name: Permission checking split: clients enforce POSIX, the MDS enforces auth caps
why: Clients enforce mode bits, ACLs, sticky bit and ownership; the MDS enforces MDS auth caps against client-asserted ids at fixed points (F-ADM-018). Keeping this split is a documented departure (D14).
subset: Legacy EIO branch for clients without FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2 is OUT.

group: Validation gates and POSIX error ordering
name: ESTALE recovery of unknown inode numbers
why: Clients address inodes by number, so any ino a client still holds must be found even when it is not cached on the receiving rank or its shard moved (D6: lookup by ino from any rank).
subset: Replace find_ino_peers/open_ino backtrace chasing with an FS-wide ino -> shard index (D2: purpose in scope); also recover on the vxattr path, which in C++ returns ESTALE at once.

name: GETATTR (stat by inode)
why: stat/statx of any inode whose cached caps do not cover the fields; values must be at least as fresh as rdlock semantics (conflicting exclusive caps revoked or flushed first).
subset: CEPH_STAT_RSTAT requests are served by the inode's owner (F-SNAP-039).

name: LOOKUP of one name in a directory
why: Core name resolution (kclient parent ino + name with WANT_DENTRY, libcephfs path walks) with parent, dentry, lease and target in one reply; lookups of names under uncommitted mutations wait for the commit.

name: Negative lookup replies (null-dentry traces)
why: Clients cache negative dentries from null-dentry traces, and the kernel splices its snapdir only when a LOOKUP of the snapdir name returns ENOENT (lookup 7.2).
risk: Anything but ENOENT for '.snap' breaks kernel snapshot-dir access.

name: LOOKUPINO and LOOKUPHASH (resolve an inode number)
why: NFS handles (Ganesha ceph_ll_lookup_inode, knfsd), libcephfs ll APIs and kclient fetches of quota-realm roots resolve bare inode numbers, including uncached ones (D6: answerable on any rank).
subset: LOOKUPHASH = LOOKUPINO; inos in [0x100, 0x1000) and purged inos -> ESTALE; the snapid branch is P1 (F-SNAP-025).
risk: C++ stalls while any rank recovers (open_ino waits for all ranks); per-shard resolution must not.

name: LOOKUPPARENT (parent directory of an inode)
why: Reconnecting NFS file handles (knfsd get_parent, libcephfs/Ganesha parent lookups); cheap once the ino index records the primary parent.

name: LOOKUPNAME (name of an inode under its parent)
why: knfsd get_name and libcephfs name lookups need the primary name of an inode under its parent; cheap once the ino index records (parent, name).
question: Kernel NFS re-export is not a mgr default flow; LOOKUPNAME could move to P1 if the ino -> (parent, name) record is deferred.

name: Reads at a snapshot id (LOOKUPSNAP, snapshot LOOKUPINO, open and readdir in snapshots)
why: Reads at a snapshot id exist only with snapshots (D8); in P0 .snap paths are handled by F-SNAP-021/022 and writes by the EROFS gate (F-NS-017).

name: OPEN of an existing file or directory
why: open(2) of an existing file: validate flags and register the mode's wanted caps, which revokes conflicting caps of other clients (Ganesha delegations rely on this).
subset: CEPH_O_LAZY (Fl) is P2 (D12); legacy inline-data EPERM is OUT.

name: O_TRUNC on open
why: libcephfs sends OPEN with O_TRUNC for existing files (Ganesha, mgr/volumes rewriting auth metadata with O_CREAT|O_TRUNC); sets mtime/ctime even at size 0 and truncates through F-NS-062.
subset: Safe reply only in P0.

name: READDIR paging of one dirfrag in hash order
why: readdir, telldir/seekdir and Ganesha cookies derive offsets as (hash << 28) | n, so entries must come in non-decreasing name-hash order with a stable order for equal hashes, resumable by last name or offset_hash.
subset: One frag per directory (D5), but the directory index must still iterate in (hash, name) order using the hash function reported in InodeStat dir_layout. Replies without REPLY_BITFLAGS are legacy and OUT.
risk: kclient fails with EIO on more than max_entries entries or an offset below its position.

name: Readdir across dirfrags: frag selection and adjustment
why: Clients send a frag and adopt the frag reported in DirStat; with a trivial fragtree this reduces to one leaf.
subset: Always serve frag_t() (whole directory); accept any client frag value and map it to the single leaf; set FRAG_END/FRAG_COMPLETE; no split or merge handling (D5); legacy no-bitflags path OUT.

name: Readdir cap-acquisition throttle
why: Admission control against a client acquiring millions of caps through readdir protects shard memory (robustness goal); no peer requires it.
subset: Per-session or per-shard cap-acquisition throttling; the C++ knobs need not be kept.

group: Creating names: create, mknod, mkdir, symlink
name: CREATE (open with O_CREAT, optionally O_EXCL)
why: open(O_CREAT[|O_EXCL]) atomically creates and opens with exactly one winner; the created ino in the reply tells kclient and libcephfs (Ganesha open-with-create) whether the file was created.
subset: Async create (ASYNC flag, delegated ino) is P1 (D7); legacy charmap EPERM is OUT.
risk: If DELEG_INO is advertised the created-ino extra must be an openc_response_t, otherwise a bare u64 (kclient EIO, libcephfs misdecode).

group: Creating names: create, mknod, mkdir, symlink
name: MKNOD (regular file, FIFO, device, socket)
why: mknod/mkfifo, and for the kernel every vfs_create caller (knfsd, mknod of S_IFREG), send MKNOD; a regular file must get RDWR caps and a writable range.

group: Creating names: create, mknod, mkdir, symlink
name: MKDIR
why: mkdir: stored nlink 1, setgid inheritance, parent nsubdirs + 1, creator gets exclusive caps on the new directory.
subset: Ephemeral random-pin evaluation is tolerate-or-OUT (D12); legacy charmap EPERM OUT.
risk: libcephfs aborts if a directory reports nlink other than 0 or 1.

group: Creating names: create, mknod, mkdir, symlink
name: SYMLINK (and readlink without an MDS op)
why: symlink stores the target with size = rbytes = target length and readlink is served from InodeStat; mgr/volumes' clone index relies on symlink st_size == target length.
subset: Legacy charmap EPERM OUT.

group: Creating names: create, mknod, mkdir, symlink
name: New inode initialization
why: New inodes: owner from the request head, setgid-directory inheritance, all times = op stamp, initial ACL/security xattrs stored verbatim; the MDS applies no umask (POSIX contract 7.1 item 2).
subset: Legacy head < v3 owner fallback and inline data are OUT.

group: Creating names: create, mknod, mkdir, symlink
name: Inode number allocation (session preallocation and InoTable)
why: Create-type ops need unique, stable inode numbers (NFS handles keep them); D3: per-shard range leases from an FS-wide allocator.
subset: Session preallocation and delegation serve only P1 early replies and async create (D7), but the allocator must support them.
risk: User inodes must be >= 0x1000 (root is 1; the kernel refuses inos in [0x100, 0x1000) with a warning); keep inos within 48 bits (ceph-fuse); never reuse an ino a client may still hold (NFS handles).

group: Creating names: create, mknod, mkdir, symlink
name: Client-specified inode number (head.ino) on create
why: Only replays of unsafe creates and kernel async creates carry a client-chosen head.ino, both P1 (D7).
risk: Validate any client head.ino against the session's reservations and reject otherwise; C++ asserts on crafted values (request-lifecycle 8 item 27).

group: Creating names: create, mknod, mkdir, symlink
name: File layout selection and validation at create
why: New files take the nearest ancestor layout or the default; mgr/volumes sets pool and pool_namespace layouts on subvolume dirs and libcephfs can pass a layout in CREATE; invalid layouts -> EINVAL.
subset: Data pools must belong to the file system (MDSMap); wait for the client's osdmap epoch for newly named pools.

group: Creating names: create, mknod, mkdir, symlink
name: Parent directory updates on link and unlink
why: POSIX parent mtime/ctime on entry changes, exact nfiles/nsubdirs (directory nlink) and a change_attr (NFS change attribute) that moves on every entry change and never backwards.
subset: Implement as commutative deltas (sum, max) so creates in one directory do not serialize; with one frag per directory every change bumps change_attr (fixes the C++ multi-frag miss).

group: Removing and relinking names: link, unlink, rmdir, rename
name: LINK (hard link)
why: D14 hard links within a shard; LINK across subvolumes or shards returns EXDEV (D4, F-SNAP-052); target nlink + 1 and ctime.
subset: Remote-target 2PC OUT (F-NS-054); global snaprealm on first link P1 (F-SNAP-011); legacy charmap EPERM OUT.

group: Removing and relinking names: link, unlink, rmdir, rename
name: UNLINK of a primary link
why: unlink: nlink - 1, the inode stays in the shard's stray area while open (D14 unlink-while-open), parent counts and times updated.
risk: Must not fail with ENOSPC for internal stray capacity (C++ stray-dirfrag limit).

group: Removing and relinking names: link, unlink, rmdir, rename
name: UNLINK of a remote (hard-link) dentry
why: Removing a hard link inside a shard (no stray, nlink - 1); no cross-rank 2PC because links never cross shards (D4).

group: Removing and relinking names: link, unlink, rmdir, rename
name: RMDIR with emptiness checks
why: rmdir must refuse non-empty directories exactly; libcephfs leaves ENOTEMPTY/ENOTDIR to the MDS and mgr/volumes rmtree relies on ENOTEMPTY.
subset: Own-snapshot ENOTEMPTY check comes with snapshots (P1); witnesses OUT (F-NS-055); rmdir of a shard root (mgr/volumes purge in _deleting) uses the D4 shard-removal mechanism.

group: Removing and relinking names: link, unlink, rmdir, rename
name: Unlinked-but-open inodes stay usable until the last cap is released
why: D14 unlink-while-open: the inode stays usable until the last cap goes, then its objects are purged; D3 makes strays and the purge queue per shard.
subset: Snapshot-aware stray retention (past-parent snapshots) is P1.

group: Removing and relinking names: link, unlink, rmdir, rename
name: RENAME of a file or directory (move, same-inode no-op)
why: D14 rename atomicity; mgr/volumes needs atomic overwrite (.meta.tmp -> .meta), renames inside a subvolume and moves of a subvolume root between non-subvolume parents (trash to _deleting).
subset: Shard-root moves within the root shard use the dedicated D4 mechanism; renames across shards -> EXDEV (F-SNAP-052).

group: Removing and relinking names: link, unlink, rmdir, rename
name: RENAME over an existing target
why: rename over a file or an empty directory replaces the target atomically; the replaced inode goes to the shard's stray area (unlink-while-open).

group: Removing and relinking names: link, unlink, rmdir, rename
name: RENAME validation and error order
why: Fixed rename error order (EBUSY, EINVAL for a directory moved below itself, ENOTEMPTY/EISDIR/ENOTDIR, same-inode no-op, EXDEV last); libcephfs callers rely on the MDS for several of them.
subset: Legacy charmap EPERM OUT; witness-related skips not needed.

group: Removing and relinking names: link, unlink, rmdir, rename
name: MDS-originated RENAME (stray reintegration and migration)
why: MDS-to-MDS rename messages exist because strays are per rank; with per-shard strays (D3) and no cross-shard links (D4) reintegration is a local transaction (purpose owned by F-BG-011), and stray migration is replaced by whole-shard handoff (D6).

name: Which rank serves each op (auth requirement, forward or discover)
why: D6: each request must reach the rank owning its shard; forwarding is client-resend with MClientRequestForward and strictly increasing num_fwd, and clients route by DirStat auth hints.
subset: Shard-map routing replaces subtree auth and discover; no replicas except shard-root inodes visible in the parent shard (D5); forward at shard boundaries during multi-component traversal.
risk: kclient BUG_ON on a forward for a request that already has a reply; a non-increasing num_fwd aborts the request with EMULTIHOP.

name: Peer requests and the LINK/UNLINK two-phase commit
why: Cross-rank LINK/UNLINK 2PC is unnecessary: a shard lives on one rank and cross-shard links get EXDEV (D4).

name: RMDIR witness protocol
why: Witnesses exist for dirfrag subtrees spread across ranks; D5 gives one frag per directory and a shard lives on one rank. Removing a shard root uses the D4 mechanism.

name: RENAME cross-rank two-phase commit
why: No general cross-rank 2PC (D4): renames across shards get EXDEV; shard-root moves in the root shard use a dedicated mechanism.
question: The design proposal's Phase 4 plans atomic cross-shard transactions; under D3 (shard = subvolume or admin-marked root) cross-shard rename is always EXDEV, so confirm that general cross-shard rename is never needed.

name: Inode authority and cap migration inside a cross-rank rename
why: Inode and cap migration inside a cross-rank rename disappears with F-NS-056; cap EXPORT/IMPORT for shard migration is owned by the multi-MDS category (D6).
subset: Legacy path for sessions without EXPORT_PEER is OUT.

name: SETATTR request: mask, locks, error order and common tail
why: SETATTR carries chmod, chown, utimes and truncate when the client holds no exclusive cap (and Ganesha's setattr path); fixed mask semantics, lock and revoke behaviour, ctime/change_attr tail.
subset: fscrypt bits P2 (F-NS-064); legacy < v6 branch OUT.

name: chmod and chown, with set-user/group-ID clearing
why: chmod/chown semantics including S_ISUID/S_ISGID clearing on chown of executables and libcephfs KILL_SUID/KILL_SGID on writes.

name: Explicit times (utimes) and btime, with time_warp_seq
why: utimes/utimensat set explicit atime/mtime (time_warp_seq + 1); libcephfs and Ganesha can set btime, which statx and mgr/volumes (created_at) read.
subset: Legacy BTIME clearing for old heads OUT.

name: Size growth through SETATTR
why: truncate growth: size = rbytes = new size, mtime = op stamp, client ranges recomputed; EFBIG and EDQUOT stay client-side.

name: Truncate (shrink) with asynchronous OSD truncation
why: Shrinking must bump truncate_seq, send CEPH_CAP_OP_TRUNC to cap holders and truncate OSD objects with truncate_seq/size so OSDs discard stale writes; pending truncations survive failover.
subset: Persistence of pending truncations is redesigned in the shard WAL; the realm SnapContext is empty in P0.
risk: kclient applies TRUNC only if truncate_seq advances; a failing or stuck OSD truncate must not crash the MDS (C++ asserts) or block other shards.

name: Timestamps from the client clock and change_attr
why: Every ctime/mtime comes from the client's request stamp; change_attr (NFS change attribute, statx change cookie) increments on each metadata change.
risk: Version fields (change_attr, time_warp_seq, truncate_seq, xattr_version) must be monotonic (kclient expectations 7 item 11).

name: fscrypt inode fields and last-block truncate
why: Kernel fscrypt needs opaque fscrypt_auth/fscrypt_file storage and the last-block read-modify-write truncate; fscrypt is P2 (D12) and no default mgr flow sets it.
subset: P0 decodes the MClientRequest v6 fscrypt fields, encodes empty fscrypt fields in InodeStat and refuses the FSCRYPT_AUTH/FSCRYPT_FILE setattr bits; legacy < v6 branch OUT.

name: Layout ops SETLAYOUT and SETDIRLAYOUT (kernel layout ioctls)
why: Only the kernel layout ioctls send SETLAYOUT/SETDIRLAYOUT; the layout vxattrs (F-NS-072) give the same function and are what mgr/volumes uses.
subset: Until implemented, answer EOPNOTSUPP.

group: Extended attributes, ACLs and virtual xattrs
name: SETXATTR and RMXATTR of stored xattrs
why: setxattr/removexattr with CREATE/REPLACE semantics for user, security, trusted and system names (Ganesha user xattrs, ACLs); mgr/volumes earmark/enctag need zero-length values stored and returned as such.
subset: Other ceph.* names than vxattrs and the two ceph.mirror names -> EINVAL.
question: C++ RMXATTR does no MDS-cap check at all; add MAY_WRITE (no peer depends on the gap)?

group: Extended attributes, ACLs and virtual xattrs
name: Total xattr size limit (max_xattr_size)
why: max_xattr_size comes from the MDSMap (fs set); the kclient uses it to choose local or synchronous xattr updates; larger maps get ENOSPC.

group: Extended attributes, ACLs and virtual xattrs
name: xattr blob delivery to clients
why: Clients cache the whole xattr map from InodeStat and cap messages and serve getxattr/listxattr locally, versioned by xattr_version.
risk: When Xs is requested the reply must carry the xattrs (libcephfs client_debug_getattr_caps aborts otherwise).

group: Extended attributes, ACLs and virtual xattrs
name: POSIX ACLs stored as opaque xattrs
why: D14 POSIX ACL storage: opaque system.posix_acl_* xattrs and initial ACLs in create payloads stored verbatim; evaluation is client-side (Ganesha sets client_acl_type=posix_acl).

group: Extended attributes, ACLs and virtual xattrs
name: ceph.mirror.* xattrs for snapshot mirroring
why: Only snapshot mirroring (mgr mirroring peer_add, cephfs-mirror dirty_snap_id) uses them; mirroring is P1 (D8).
subset: Storing them as plain xattrs is trivial and may land early.

group: Extended attributes, ACLs and virtual xattrs
name: Virtual xattr set/remove path (common rules, p flag)
why: mgr/volumes, Rook and admins change layout, quota, subvolume and pin policies through ceph.* setxattr, gated only by the MDS-cap p flag (MAY_SET_VXATTR, not MAY_WRITE).
subset: P0 names: ceph.dir.layout*, ceph.file.layout*, ceph.quota*, ceph.dir.subvolume, ceph.dir.pin, ceph.dir.pin.distributed; ceph.dir.pin.random tolerate (validate EDOM/EINVAL, store, ignore; D12). P1: ceph.dir.subvolume.snaps.visible. P2: ceph.dir.charmap/casesensitive/normalization/encoding, ceph.quiesce.block (refused until then). CREATE/REPLACE flags ignored; realm-changing names reply after commit and notify realm changes.
risk: Recover uncached inodes instead of returning ESTALE (C++ gap, attributes 8 item 14).

group: Extended attributes, ACLs and virtual xattrs
name: Layout virtual xattrs (ceph.dir.layout*, ceph.file.layout*)
why: mgr/volumes sets ceph.dir.layout.pool/pool_namespace and walks ancestors up to / for ceph.dir.layout.pool, so the root must carry a layout; clients compute composite layout names from InodeStat and GETVXATTR serves pool_name, pool_id and json.
subset: Legacy EIO for clients without FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2 OUT.
risk: C++ aborts when GETVXATTR reaches the root without a layout: create the root with the default layout and never crash.

group: Extended attributes, ACLs and virtual xattrs
name: GETVXATTR op
why: kclient and libcephfs send GETVXATTR for any ceph.* name missing from their tables and only if CEPHFS_FEATURE_OP_GETVXATTR is advertised; mgr/volumes reads ceph.dir.subvolume and layout json through it.
subset: Serve ceph.dir.subvolume ('0'/'1'), ceph.{dir,file}.layout.{json,pool_name,pool_id}, ceph.dir.pin, ceph.dir.pin.distributed, ceph.dir.pin.random; ENODATA for every other ceph.* name (charmap, quiesce, unknown) so libcephfs falls back to stored xattrs. Reply = ENCODE_START(1,1) + string, no trace.
risk: kclient requires value_len == remaining bytes; any error but ENODATA for an unset name breaks callers that only tolerate NoData (mgr/volumes info).
question: C++ does no access check here, so path-restricted clients read values outside their path; add the MDS-cap path check?

group: Extended attributes, ACLs and virtual xattrs
name: Client-synthesized ceph.* vxattrs (InodeStat contract)
why: Most ceph.* names users and mgr/volumes read (rstats, dirstats, quota, layouts, pin) are computed by clients from InodeStat v9 fields, so every field must be present and correct.
subset: P0 encodes zero or empty snap_btime, snap_metadata, fscrypt fields and optmetadata; a set of ceph.dir.rctime or ceph.caps (kclient forwards them) -> EINVAL.

group: Extended attributes, ACLs and virtual xattrs
name: Case-insensitive and normalized directories (charmap)
why: Charmap/case-insensitivity is P2 (D12) and default mgr/volumes flows do not set it (only --casesensitive/--normalization do).
subset: P0: no charmap metadata; charmap vxattr sets refused, GETVXATTR -> ENODATA; legacy EPERM gate OUT.
question: D15: bit 22 means CHARMAP to libcephfs and SUBVOLUME_METRICS to the 7.3 kernel; decide what to advertise.

group: Extended attributes, ACLs and virtual xattrs
name: alternate_name on dentries
why: Only fscrypt (kernel) and charmap (libcephfs) clients produce alternate_name, both P2 (D12).
subset: P0: LeaseStat v2 carries an empty alternate_name; reserve an optional per-dentry field in the format.

name: SETFILELOCK: POSIX fcntl byte-range locks
why: D14: POSIX fcntl and OFD record locks; kclient, libcephfs and Ganesha (NFSv4 locks) send SETFILELOCK; cluster-wide arbitration in MDS memory, owner = (session, owner[, pid]).
subset: Lock tables are not journaled and must move with the shard on migration; fix the 32-bit merge overflow (flock.cc:452).
risk: A resent SETFILELOCK is re-executed (never in completed requests), so same-owner relock and unlock must be idempotent.

name: BSD flock whole-file locks
why: flock(2): mgr/volumes authorize uses blocking LOCK_EX on auth metadata files and cephfs-mirror takes LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB on directories (EWOULDBLOCK); D14.

name: Blocking lock waits and wake-ups
why: D14 blocking lock waits (F_SETLKW, blocking flock) parked in the MDS without timeout until granted or cancelled.

name: Lock wait interruption (FCNTL_INTR / FLOCK_INTR)
why: Signals interrupt blocked lock waits through *_INTR unlocks; the original request then returns EINTR.

name: fcntl deadlock detection (EDEADLK)
why: D14: the C++ MDS returns EDEADLK for fcntl wait-for cycles (up to 5 hops), which applications can observe.
subset: Detection scope per rank as in C++ (cycles spanning ranks are not detected).

name: GETFILELOCK (F_GETLK)
why: F_GETLK returns the first conflicting lock; reply extra = raw 41-byte ceph_filelock, no trace.

name: Lock cleanup on cap removal and session end
why: Eviction and cap removal must release a client's locks so others can proceed; clients then fail lock calls and I/O with EIO.

name: Lock reinstatement after an MDS restart
why: D9 failover: held locks are resubmitted in MClientReconnect and must be reinstated; pending waits are resent and executed afresh.
subset: Reinstate for every inode of the shard named in the reconnect, not only cached ones (C++ gap); legacy flockbl in MClientCaps OUT.

name: Directory link count and size presentation
why: Clients present directory nlink as 2 + nsubdirs and size as entries or rbytes, so the MDS must store directory nlink 1 (0 once unlinked) and report exact nsubdirs.
risk: libcephfs calls ceph_abort() for a directory nlink other than 0 or 1.

name: Access time is not maintained by the MDS
why: Documented departure kept (D14): atime is stored and settable but never updated on reads; fstests already treat atime as not maintained.

name: Timestamp range limited to unsigned 32-bit seconds
