why: Wire ceph_timespec seconds are unsigned 32-bit and the kernel sets s_time_min/max to match; keep the range.

name: Limits enforced only by clients, and no hard-link limit
why: Documented departures kept (D14): NAME_MAX, max_file_size (EFBIG) and quotas are client-enforced; no EMLINK.

name: Unsupported Linux extensions: renameat2 flags and O_TMPFILE
why: No MDS op exists: kclient and ceph-fuse refuse renameat2 flags and the kernel offers no O_TMPFILE for ceph; adding them would need client changes.

name: Data-path coherency departures outside the MDS
why: Coherency comes from cap revocation driven by MDS lock states; the documented O_APPEND, mmap and object-boundary departures are kept (D14).
subset: LazyIO (Fl) is P2 (D12).

name: statfs is answered by the monitors
why: statfs goes to the monitors; the MDS only serves libcephfs's quota-root GETATTR and supplies quota and rbytes (F-SNAP-048). Nothing else to build.

name: Conformance suites in the tree (pjd-fstest, xfstests)
why: pjd-fstest and xfstests are the acceptance gate for D14 (POSIX contract 7.1); nothing to implement in the MDS.
subset: Run pjd-fstest (all directories except chflags) and xfstests with the existing ceph.exclude list on kclient and ceph-fuse mounts as release criteria.

name: Inode record field set (inode_t)
why: Every client-visible attribute (InodeStat, MClientCaps, vxattrs) derives from this record, so its field set and semantics are needed; the C++ inode_t encoding is OUT (D2).
subset: Keep every field that reaches clients: ino, mode/uid/gid, nlink, rdev, times, time_warp_seq, change_attr, size, client_ranges/max_size, truncate_*, layout+pool_ns, dir_layout, dirstat, rstat, quota, pins/flags, xattrs, symlink, version, xattr_version; reserve room for fscrypt/optmetadata blobs (P2); drop backtrace_version, scrub stamps (P1), file_data_version, oldest_snap.
risk: Directories must report nlink 1 and size 0 (libcephfs ceph_abort()s on any other directory nlink).

name: Refusal of client operations on private and system inodes
why: Clients must never see MDS-private numbers and must get ESTALE for numbers that name nothing (kernel and libcephfs reject [0x100,0x1000)).
subset: LOOKUPINO/LOOKUPHASH/LOOKUPPARENT/LOOKUPNAME on a number below 0x1000 (other than root 1) or not in use returns ESTALE; the new design exposes no system directories (~mdsN, strays, lost+found), so the EPERM/EROFS paths do not arise.
risk: An exposed number in [0x100,0x1000) makes kernel lookups fail with -EREMOTEIO.

name: Timestamps, time_warp_seq and change_attr
why: POSIX timestamps and the NFS change attribute: the kernel exposes change_attr as i_version with STATX_ATTR_CHANGE_MONOTONIC, and NFS re-export relies on it.
subset: Legacy InodeStat encoding and the pre-bit-59 cap-flush gates are out.
risk: change_attr and time_warp_seq must never go backwards, including after failover, shard migration and in the shard-boundary copy (C++ replicas miss btime/change_attr updates).

name: Truncation state fields
why: Clients pass truncate_seq/truncate_size on every OSD data op and OSDs apply TRIMTRUNC semantics, so truncation ordering between MDS, clients and OSDs rests on these fields.
risk: New inodes must start with truncate_seq 1 and truncate_size -1 (OSD 'no truncation'; the kernel fabricates the same values for async creates); other values let OSDs truncate client data.

name: File layout field and layout inheritance
why: Clients compute data placement from the layout (pool, namespace, striping) and mgr/volumes sets pool layouts on subvolumes and groups; inheritance from the nearest ancestor and the size-0 rule for changes are client-visible.
subset: Legacy 28-byte encoding for old daemons and Fr/Fw withholding for clients without FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2 are out; InodeStat keeps the 28-byte layout plus pool_ns.
question: Inheritance crosses the shard boundary (group-level ceph.dir.layout from `subvolumegroup create --pool_layout`): a shard needs the effective layout of its root-shard ancestors.

name: Inline data
why: Inline data is OUT (D12), but InodeStat and MClientCaps must still carry inline_version = CEPH_INLINE_NONE, which libcephfs requires and which keeps both clients off their inline-data paths.
subset: Always send inline_version CEPH_INLINE_NONE with an empty blob; ignore inline data in cap flushes; ignore the deprecated MDSMap inline_data flag.
risk: Any other value makes clients treat files as inline (empty) data.

name: fscrypt metadata fields
why: fscrypt is P2 (D12) and only the kernel uses it.
subset: Leave room in the inode record for opaque fscrypt_auth, fscrypt_file and last-block blobs and in dentries for alternate_name.

name: Inode version and client-visible version
why: kclient and libcephfs apply attributes only from the auth and only when version > (cached & ~1); the MDS sends 2 x version (+1 when projected).
subset: Mechanism free: a durable per-inode monotonic counter suffices (the C++ parent-dirfrag counter is internal); the +1 appears only with early replies (P1).
risk: A version that goes backwards after failover or shard migration makes clients silently ignore attribute updates.

name: Snapshot-range identity of inodes and dentries
why: Snapshots are P1 (D8): dentries and inodes must then exist in several snapshot-era versions ([first,last]).
subset: Design the P0 format so dentry versions keyed by (name, last snapid) and per-inode old versions can be added.

name: Inode projection (read-copy-update)
why: Projection chains are C++ concurrency internals (D16); the transaction engine provides isolation and P0 replies show only committed state (D7).
subset: Dead pop_and_apply_projected_inode is out.

name: Dirfrag version sequence and fnode projection
why: Dirfrag version sequences and fnode projection are C++ commit-tracking internals (D2, D16).

name: Projected dentry linkage (primary, remote, null)
why: Linkage projection is internal (D16); the needed linkage kinds (primary, hard link) are persisted per F-STORE-049/050 and alternate_name storage comes with fscrypt/charmap (P2).

name: Dirty tracking on journal segments
why: Per-segment dirty lists are C++ write-back bookkeeping, replaced by per-shard checkpointing (F-STORE-016).

name: Write-back only at journal segment expiry
why: Cache view of F-STORE-016/018: dirty state must reach the backing store so WALs can be truncated and clean state evicted.
subset: `flush journal` equivalent is P0 (F-STORE-020); `flush_path` is P2; C++ segment-count triggers are internal.

name: Commit error handling and read-only mode
why: Write-back failures must never be silently acknowledged; the outcome (respawn when blocklisted, otherwise read-only with FORCE_RO and MDS_READ_ONLY) is the policy of F-STORE-100.
subset: Per-shard containment preferred (D10); the stray ENOENT special case is C++ internal.

name: Underwater item reconciliation after replay
why: Reconciling replayed dirty items with already written objects is an artifact of C++ lazy write-back.

name: Directory completeness and authoritative negative lookups
why: A wrong ENOENT or an incomplete readdir is a POSIX violation visible to every client.
subset: Answer misses only from a complete directory index (in memory, or a keyed read of the store); C++ completeness flags are internal.

name: Bloom filter of trimmed names
why: Optimization of negative lookups after trimming, with no external contract.

name: Null dentries
why: In-cache representation of negative and pending-delete entries; negative-dentry leases to clients belong to the lease entries (caps category).

group: Cache object model: references, auth pins, freezing, waiters
name: Reference counts and upward pinning
why: Pin and refcount machinery is C++ internal (D16); the outcome it serves (purge an unlinked file only after its last cap and request) belongs to the stray and purge entries.

group: Cache object model: references, auth pins, freezing, waiters
name: Inode maps and object registry
why: In-memory indexes of the C++ cache, with no external contract.

group: Cache object model: references, auth pins, freezing, waiters
name: Auth pins with one-level nested accounting
why: Auth pins are named in D16 as C++ internal.

group: Cache object model: references, auth pins, freezing, waiters
name: Dirfrag freeze (freeze_dir)
why: Used only by directory fragmentation, which D5 removes; freezing is internal (D16).

group: Cache object model: references, auth pins, freezing, waiters
name: Subtree freeze (freeze_tree)
why: Subtree freezing is a C++ mechanism (D16, like F-MULTI-003); the needed whole-shard drain at handoff (block, then forward) is carried by F-MULTI-018 and the handoff by F-MULTI-001/021 and F-STORE-033.

group: Cache object model: references, auth pins, freezing, waiters
name: Single-inode freeze, ambiguous inode auth and frozen-inode tracking
why: Serves only cross-rank rename (EXDEV across shards, D4) and lock-cache bookkeeping; internal (D16).

group: Cache object model: references, auth pins, freezing, waiters
name: Waiter queues on cache objects
why: Waiter queues are C++ internal (D16).

group: Cache object model: references, auth pins, freezing, waiters
name: Waiter completion semantics
why: Continuation completion semantics are C++ internal (D16).

name: Authority of cache objects and the auth bit
why: Every object needs exactly one authoritative rank; with D3 the authority of any inode, dentry or directory is the owner rank of its shard.
subset: Per-dirfrag authorities, the STATE_AUTH bit and filelock/nestlock scattered across ranks are dropped (D5, D16).

name: Subtree map
why: The partition of the namespace among ranks becomes the shard map (D3, D6): shard -> owner rank, file-system-wide, durable and epoch-versioned, replacing per-rank subtree maps and ESubtreeMap.

name: Subtree create, merge and bounded-adjust primitives
why: Dynamic subtree splitting and merging is replaced by whole-shard ownership; shard roots come from ceph.dir.subvolume (D3).

name: Ambiguous authority and WAIT_SINGLEAUTH
why: Ambiguous dir_auth states belong to C++ migration and 2PC; a shard has one owner per placement epoch and requests during handoff wait or are forwarded (F-CACHE-036, F-MULTI-018).

name: Subtree map maintenance on directory rename
why: Cross-shard renames return EXDEV (D4) and shard ownership does not depend on paths, so renames never change the shard map.

name: Aux subtrees
why: Aux subtrees implement C++ export pins; ceph.dir.pin becomes a whole-shard placement hint (D6).

group: Path traversal and lookup by inode number
name: Path traversal (path_traverse)
why: Every client request names (base ino, relative path) and relies on the traversal error codes (ENOENT, ENOTDIR, EIO for damage, ESTALE for unknown bases, EINVAL for a misplaced snapdir).
subset: Keep addressing relative to any inode and the empty first component for .snap (empty LSSNAP in P0, D8); C++ traversal flags are internal and lock-cache attachment is P1.
question: Paths cross shard boundaries; the owning rank must also know the absolute path of its shard root for MDS auth-cap path checks, and that path changes on the mgr/volumes trash rename.

group: Path traversal and lookup by inode number
name: Forward-or-discover for non-auth objects
why: Clients route themselves and resend on MClientRequestForward; with multi-rank P0 (D6) misrouted requests must be forwarded to the shard owner.
subset: Forward with num_fwd+1 to the owner of the target shard, never relay; no discover-based replication to break loops (D5); mds_forward_all_requests_to_auth not needed.
risk: The kernel aborts with -EMULTIHOP if the forward count does not increase and BUG_ONs on a forward for a tid that already got a reply.

group: Path traversal and lookup by inode number
name: Hard-link target resolution
why: Hard links within a shard are P0 (D14); since links never cross shards (D4), resolving a remote dentry is shard-local through the inode-number index.
subset: Keep the C++ outcome for an unresolvable target: EIO on traversal, entry omitted from readdir, damage recorded.

group: Path traversal and lookup by inode number
name: Lookup by inode number (open_ino)
why: NFS file handles (kernel nfsd, Ganesha), libcephfs ll_lookup_inode and kernel quota-realm lookups resolve bare inode numbers with LOOKUPINO/LOOKUPPARENT/LOOKUPNAME sent to any rank (D6).
subset: Durable ino -> shard routing readable on every rank (e.g. range leases plus exceptions), forward to the owner, which resolves through its per-shard index (F-STORE-062); LOOKUPHASH comes with snapshots (P1).
risk: Return ESTALE only for numbers not in use; while the owning shard recovers, wait (as C++ does): ESTALE makes NFS clients treat the file as deleted.
question: Directories that become shard roots after creation (mgr/volumes v2 creates <base>/<uuid> before setting ceph.dir.subvolume on <base>) bring inodes numbered from the root shard's ranges.

group: Path traversal and lookup by inode number
name: open_ino peer protocol
why: MDS-to-MDS inode search (free, D2); replaced by the inode-number index (F-CACHE-047).

group: Path traversal and lookup by inode number
name: Batched dentry-key fetches for open_ino
why: C++ batching of backtrace-driven dentry fetches during rejoin.

group: Path traversal and lookup by inode number
name: ESTALE recovery via find_ino_peers
why: Requests addressed by an inode number this rank does not cache must still be served or forwarded (F-NS-022); ESTALE reaches clients only for unknown numbers.
subset: Resolve through the inode-number index (F-CACHE-047): load locally if the shard is owned here, else forward; no find_ino peer queries.

group: Path traversal and lookup by inode number
name: Foreign mdsdir and stray base resolution
why: Per-rank ~mdsN and stray directories are not exposed, and cross-rank stray operations disappear with per-shard strays (D3).

name: Replica map and nonces
why: Replica bookkeeping of the C++ MDS-to-MDS protocol; no general replicas (D5).

name: Discover protocol (pull replication)
why: Pull replication between ranks is removed by D5.

name: Replica encodings
why: MDS-to-MDS encodings are free (D2, D5).

name: Replica subtrees at delegation boundaries
why: D5 keeps replicas only at shard boundaries: the parent shard must answer lookup, getattr and readdir entries for a shard-root inode with current attributes (mode, times, rstat, quota, realm).
subset: A boundary copy of each shard-root inode in the parent shard, refreshed on change (including btime and change_attr, unlike C++ lock payloads).
question: Who issues caps on a shard-root inode reached through the parent rank (C++ replicas issue non-auth caps and the auth gathers revocations), and how fresh must the copy be?

name: Push link/unlink to replicas
why: Dentry replicas do not exist (D5) and MDS-to-MDS messages are free.
subset: Dead snapbl branch is out.

name: Replica refresh through lock-state payloads
why: Lock-state payloads are C++ internals (D16); the needed refresh of shard-root copies is part of F-CACHE-055.

name: Replica expiry (MCacheExpire)
why: Replica expiry protocol, removed with replicas (D5).

name: Dentry LRUs (lru and bottom_lru)
why: LRU policy is internal; the memory-budget contract is F-CACHE-061.

name: Pin reasons that block eviction
why: The MDS can shrink only as clients release caps after RECALL_STATE; kclient, libcephfs and Ganesha (handle cache, ino_release_cb) release at their own pace.
subset: Cap state for every inode a client holds stays valid (resident or reloadable); shrink through per-session recall; never evict a client for not shrinking.
risk: A client holding caps on millions of inodes exhausts memory if cap state cannot be bounded or spilled.

name: Memory-based soft cache limit
why: Rook sets mds_cache_memory_limit to 0.5 x the pod memory limit and cephadm's autotuner subtracts it from host memory; MDS_CACHE_OVERSIZED is a mon-visible health check.
subset: Honour mds_cache_memory_limit (with mds_cache_reservation and mds_health_cache_threshold) as the budget of all cached metadata and caps and raise MDS_CACHE_OVERSIZED above it; per-shard budgets are internal.
risk: Ignoring the limit risks pod OOM kills; while MDS_CACHE_OVERSIZED is reported the mon refuses Rook's unconfirmed `mds fail`/`fs fail`.

name: Trim throttle
why: Trim-throttle tuning of the C++ LRU.

name: Trim pass and per-object removal
why: C++ trim-pass mechanics.

name: Upkeep thread
why: C++ upkeep thread; the duties it drives (lease expiry, cap recall, memory sampling) belong to their own entries.

name: Heap release to the OS
why: tcmalloc-specific heap release.

name: Empty-subtree trimming and empty-import return
why: Empty-subtree and empty-import handling of the C++ subtree map.

name: Expiry of a stopping peer's mdsdir replicas
why: No replicas of another rank's mdsdir exist; a stopping rank hands off its shards instead (D6).

name: Recovery-time non-auth trimming
why: Non-auth cache cleanup for C++ resolve and rejoin; no replicas (D5).

name: Standby-replay cache maintenance
why: Standby-replay is P1 (D9); a follower tailing shard WALs must keep its cache bounded.

name: mkfs base hierarchy creation
why: Cache view of F-CLU-064: up:creating must create the root shard with the root inode and an empty root directory.
subset: No ~mdsN/stray hierarchy; per-shard internal areas instead.

name: Root and system inode initial attributes and default layouts
why: Clients and mgr/volumes see the root's initial attributes after `fs new`: S_IFDIR 0755, uid/gid mds_root_ino_uid/gid (0/0), ctime=mtime=btime, default layout on the first data pool, dl_dir_hash rjenkins.
subset: Root inode only; system inodes are internal.

name: Global snaprealm dummy inode
why: The global realm (ino 3) gives hard-linked inodes outside subvolumes their snapshot semantics, so it comes with snapshots (D8); clients merely keep realm 3 when they receive it.
subset: Keep number 3 reserved.

name: Boot-time opening of the base hierarchy and the open gate
why: A rank must load its shards' base state before serving and hold requests until then; failures must be contained (D10).
subset: Open each shard independently, recreate missing internal structures, and let a damaged shard fail alone rather than taking the rank down:damaged; the legacy 'stray' name is out.

group: Fragment identity, name hashing and client exposure
name: Fragment identifier and fragment tree (frag_t, fragtree_t)
why: Clients decode frag_t and fragtree encodings in InodeStat and readdir replies; D5 exposes one frag per directory.
subset: Encode the trivial fragtree (no splits) and frag_t() everywhere; accept any frag value in requests and map it to frag_t(); no per-frag objects; the byte-swap decode fix is out.

group: Fragment identity, name hashing and client exposure
name: Dentry name hash per directory (dl_dir_hash)
why: Clients hash names with dir_layout.dl_dir_hash to compute readdir positions and to route; the MDS must order and look up entries with the identical hash.
subset: New directories use rjenkins (2); values 0/1 only make kernel routing and LOOKUPHASH disagree; the legacy pre-v4 decode is out.

group: Fragment identity, name hashing and client exposure
name: Fragtree and dir_layout in InodeStat
why: Every directory InodeStat carries fragtree and dir_layout, and libcephfs and the kernel replace their tree from it.
subset: Always the empty tree plus dir_layout, versioned InodeStat only (the legacy DIRLAYOUTHASH form is out).

group: Fragment identity, name hashing and client exposure
name: Hash-ordered dentry storage and readdir order
why: With REPLY_BITFLAGS the kernel and libcephfs build readdir offsets from the 24-bit name hash and need entries in non-decreasing (hash24, name) order, resuming at offset_hash or after the last name.
subset: The directory index (store and cache) must iterate in (hash24, name) order; names compare bytewise without folding (charmap is P2); legacy readdir without bitflags is out.
risk: An entry below the current position makes the kernel's ceph_readdir return EIO.

group: Fragment identity, name hashing and client exposure
name: Readdir fragment mapping and resume across refragmentation
why: Fragment side of readdir resume (F-NS-033); with one frag per directory (D5) it reduces to mapping.
subset: Any requested frag maps to frag_t(); the reply names frag 0; resume by offset_hash or path2 (F-CACHE-077).

group: Fragment identity, name hashing and client exposure
name: DirStat delegation hints
why: Clients route by the DirStat {frag, auth, dist} hints carried in every trace and readdir reply.
subset: frag 0, auth = owner rank of the directory's shard (-1 when equal to the inode auth), empty dist (no replicas, D5); versioned envelope only.

group: Fragment identity, name hashing and client exposure
name: Per-dirfrag size limit (ENOSPC)
why: The 100000-entry per-dirfrag ENOSPC is an artifact of C++ fragment storage; with one client-visible frag (D5) it would cap every directory, so the new store scales directories internally (F-STORE-047).
risk: If the new directory index cannot scale, an explicit bound must replace silent degradation (OSD LARGE_OMAP_OBJECTS at 200000 keys per object).

group: Fragment identity, name hashing and client exposure
name: Per-directory entry limit
why: Optional admin cap (default off) that no peer sets; cheap to keep.

name: Size-triggered split and split checks
why: Directory fragmentation is removed by D5: no size-triggered splits.

name: Fast split
why: No fast split: fragmentation is removed by D5.

name: Temperature-triggered split
why: No temperature-triggered splits or popularity counters (D5).

name: Size-triggered merge
why: No merges: fragmentation is removed by D5.

name: Fragmentation preconditions and exclusions
why: No fragmentation to gate (D5); the legacy /.ceph exclusion is out too.

name: Fragment operation (FRAGMENTDIR)
why: No FRAGMENTDIR operation (D5).

name: Dentry repartitioning and stat-delta preservation
why: No in-memory refragmentation (D5); internal partitioning of the new store keeps exact stats by its own means.

name: New dirfrag object write and old object purge
why: No dirfrag object rewrite (D5); dirfrag objects are C++ format (D2).

name: Replica notification of refragmentation
why: No refragmentation notifies; MDS-to-MDS messages are free (D5).

name: Fragtree propagation through dirfragtreelock
why: No fragtree changes and no scatterlocks (D5, D16).

name: Subtree map maintenance on split and merge
why: No subtree-map edits on split or merge (D5).

name: Abort, requeue and cancellation of fragment operations
why: No fragment operations to abort or requeue (D5).

name: Recovery of in-flight fragment operations
why: No in-flight fragment operations to recover (D5).

name: Forced refragmentation during replay, resolve and rejoin
why: Replay never refragments (D5).

name: Migration and fragmentation mutual exclusion
why: Nothing to exclude: shard migration has no fragmentation to race with (D5).

name: Effects of a fragment freeze on clients
why: No fragment freezes (D5); client stalls during shard handoff belong to the migration entries.

name: Journal pointer object (front/back journal inode)
why: C++ journal pointer format (D2), read only by cephfs-journal-tool and QA; the new WAL locates its per-shard streams by its own naming.
subset: Legacy back-pointer paths are out.

name: Journaler header object
why: C++ Journaler header (D2); WAL positions belong to the new WAL design (F-STORE-007, F-STORE-036).

name: Striped journal byte stream and its RADOS objects
why: Striped byte-stream layout of the C++ journal (D2).
risk: Whatever names the new WAL uses must not collide with mgr-owned objects in the metadata pool (F-STORE-102).

name: RESILIENT journal entry framing
why: C++ entry framing read by cephfs-journal-tool (D2); the new WAL should frame records with length, sequence and checksum (C++ has no checksum).
subset: Legacy format-0 framing is out.

name: LogEvent envelope and event type ids
why: C++ event envelope and type ids, read only by C++ tools (D2).
subset: Legacy classic envelope and type 11 are out.

name: Legacy-format journal rewrite through the back pointer
why: Legacy (old-data) rewrite of format-0 journals; the new MDS never opens C++ journals (D1, D2).

name: Per-rank write-ahead metadata journal with one submission order
why: D7: a mutation is safe only after durable commit; the C++ single ordered journal per rank couples all subvolumes (an fsync flushes everyone's events).
subset: Per-shard WAL stream(s) in RADOS: one atomic record per transaction, concurrent submission, ordering by transaction dependencies, acknowledgement only after commit.
question: Stream granularity (one per shard or several) and how the D4 cross-shard operations order their records.

name: Group commit: flush and wait_for_safe
why: Group commit carries synchronous NFS writes and fsync throughput (D7, use case 3); in C++ one flush writes every subvolume's buffered events.
subset: Batch concurrent commits per shard stream without waiting for an explicit flush, so FLUSH_MDLOG and sync cap flushes cost nothing extra and no tenant waits for another.

name: Periodic journal flush on tick
why: The kernel assumes un-flushed journal entries become durable within about 5 s (mds_tick_interval) when it waits for safe replies after fsync.
subset: Mechanism free: commit-as-soon-as-possible group commit meets the bound; it must also hold while the monitor link is laggy (the C++ tick then skips its flush).

name: Ordered completions and the safe position
why: Ordered completions on one finisher and safe_pos are C++ internals; the WAL redesign (F-STORE-007) must only acknowledge records that are completely durable.

name: Safe reply only after the journal commit (early unsafe reply)
why: Journal side of F-NS-010/011: the safe MClientReply, FLUSH_ACK and session OPEN/CLOSE replies go out only after durable commit (D7).
subset: P0 sends safe replies only; early (unsafe) replies, mds_early_reply and REPLAY of unsafe requests are P1.

name: Journal prezeroing ahead of the write position
why: Prezeroing exists only for the C++ probe-based end-of-journal detection; the new WAL finds its end from record sequence and checksums (F-STORE-036).
risk: Never delete objects by name outside the MDS's own names (mgr objects share the pool).

name: Journal header refresh
why: C++ header refresh policy (D2).

name: Journal write-error policy (damaged or respawn)
why: A WAL write failure must stop acknowledgements and be visible to the monitor and operator; D10 asks for containment instead of taking every tenant down.
subset: -EBLOCKLISTED abandons the rank (F-STORE-095); other errors stop the affected shard with health and cluster-log reporting; rank-level down:damaged (cleared by `ceph mds repaired`) only for rank-wide state.

name: Log segments as units of lazy writeback (segment expiry)
why: WALs must be truncatable and the cache shrinkable, so dirty state must be checkpointed to the backing store; in C++ one slow object holds back every subvolume's trimming.
subset: Per-shard checkpoint of directory entries, inodes, allocator and session state that records the WAL position it covers; only clean state is evicted.

name: Segment boundaries and rotation policy
why: The segment structure of the C++ journal and the stray rotation coupled to it are internal (D2).
subset: Dead ELid(seq) constructor is out.

name: Background journal trimming with throttle
why: Unbounded WAL growth lengthens replay and fills the metadata pool, so trimming must run in the background for every shard.
subset: Size or age budget per shard WAL and an MDS_TRIM-equivalent warning when behind; C++ segment counts and decay throttle are not needed.
risk: While MDS_TRIM is reported the mon refuses Rook's unconfirmed `mds fail`/`fs fail`; raise it only when a WAL is really behind.

name: Major-group trimming and journal object deletion
why: Major-group trimming and Journaler object deletion are C++ format details.
risk: Keep the invariant: delete WAL objects only after the checkpoint that covers them is durable.

name: flush journal admin command
why: D13 lists a flush-journal equivalent as an operator essential; operators, QA (e.g. test_volumes.py before `dump inode`) and `cache drop` use `ceph tell mds.<fs>:0 flush journal`.
subset: Same command and {message, return_code} output; semantics: checkpoint every shard of the rank and truncate its WALs; EROFS when read-only.

name: Journal capping when a rank stops
why: Rank shrink through max_mds is P0 (D6): a stopping rank must hand off its shards and leave nothing to replay before beaconing down:stopped.
subset: Hand off shards, close sessions, checkpoint and seal per-rank state so that up:starting needs no replay.

name: EMetaBlob after-image container
why: C++ after-image container (D2); the new WAL record format is free (logical records avoid journaling whole inodes plus ancestors).
subset: Legacy v1-v7 decode is out.

name: EMetaBlob path context and ancestor images
why: Ancestor path context serves C++ replay and eager rstat propagation; D4 makes ancestor aggregation a separate, eventually consistent mechanism.

name: Snapshot COW images in the journal
why: Copy-on-write of dentries and inodes at snapshot boundaries comes with snapshots (D8); the WAL record format must leave room for it.

name: ESubtreeMap: major boundary with the subtree map
why: ESubtreeMap anchors replay of a rank-wide journal; per-shard WALs carry their own identity and the shard map replaces subtree claims (F-CACHE-036).

name: EUpdate: generic mutation record
why: C++ generic event type (D2); journaling of mutations is F-STORE-007 and session force-open on cap import is part of F-STORE-033.

name: EOpen: open-file journaling
why: EOpen keeps open inodes in the C++ journal; the outcome is provided by per-shard open-file tracking (F-STORE-084).
subset: Snapflush-related re-journaling comes with snapshots (P1).

name: Session events: ESession and ESessions
why: Session open and close must be durable before the OPEN/CLOSE reply, and Ganesha reclaim needs uuid, timeout and auth_name to survive failover.
subset: Per-rank session records (sessions span shards, D4), including sessions force-opened on the importer during shard migration; legacy type 11 is out.
risk: Losing auth_name or uuid makes Ganesha reclaim fail (EPERM/ENOENT) after failover.

name: Completed client request ids in journal and SessionMap
why: Retried requests after failover must be answered, not re-executed, and a create must return the same inode again (F-NS-012).
subset: Record (client, tid, created ino) atomically with each mutation in the shard WAL, rebuild at replay, trim by oldest_client_tid, persist at checkpoint, move with the shard on migration.

name: Completed cap flush ids in journal and SessionMap
why: Clients re-send dirty cap flushes after failover and expect exactly-once application (F-CAPS-019).
subset: Record (client, flush tid) with the cap-flush transaction, trim by oldest_flush_tid, move with the shard.

name: Destroyed inode records
why: Bookkeeping for C++ replay and OpenFileTable prefetch; the new store simply must not resurrect purged inodes.

name: Cross-rank two-phase-commit records
why: General cross-rank 2PC is out (D4: EXDEV), but the cross-shard operations D4 keeps (create or mark, trash-rename and remove shard roots, between the root shard and a subvolume shard) still need crash-safe coordination.
subset: Only these shard-root operations (e.g. an intent record in the root-shard WAL plus idempotent completion); no link/rename/rmdir 2PC.

name: Subtree migration records and rename subtree hints
why: Live shard migration is P0 (D6); with per-shard WALs in shared RADOS, migration hands over WAL and store ownership instead of journaling a copy of the subtree (EImportStart).
subset: Durable ownership change (shard-map epoch), exporter drained before the importer writes, client sessions force-opened on the importer for imported caps; a crash at any step resolves to exactly one owner.

name: EFragment journal protocol and old dirfrag object cleanup
why: Directory fragmentation is removed (D5) and EFragment is C++ journal format (D2).

name: Journal open and recovery thread
why: Pointer, back-journal and format checks of the C++ journal (D2); opening and recovering a shard WAL is F-STORE-036/037, error policy F-STORE-040, fencing reaction F-STORE-095.
subset: Legacy back-journal and reformat paths are out.

name: End-of-journal probe and torn-tail handling
why: After a crash the true end of each WAL must be found and a torn last record discarded, never acknowledged.
subset: Self-describing records (sequence, length, checksum) instead of the C++ prezero-and-probe scheme.

name: Journal replay pipeline
why: Takeover replays the WAL to rebuild state; multi-tenant journal replay is a motivating use case, while C++ replays one ordered journal per rank under mds_lock.
subset: Per-shard replay from the last checkpoint, in parallel and idempotent against checkpointed state; one shard's slow or damaged WAL must not hold back the others.

name: Cache reconstruction from after-images
why: Replay of C++ after-images (D2); covered by F-STORE-037.

name: Version-gated redo of table operations
why: Version-gated redo of C++ tables; the new checkpoint records its WAL position so replay is idempotent (F-STORE-016, F-STORE-037).

name: Replay error policy and the damaged rank
why: D10: unreadable or inconsistent metadata must be contained (EIO, damaged shard) while the rest of the rank keeps serving.
subset: A corrupt WAL record or checkpoint damages only its shard; never assert on decoded data (C++ aborts on trailing bytes and subtree mismatches); rank down:damaged only when rank-wide state is unreadable; dev skip options are out.
question: How a damaged shard is reported (MDS_DAMAGE, damage ls) and repaired, given that the monitor only knows rank states.

name: Post-replay session and InoTable consistency check
why: Consistency assertion between the C++ SessionMap and InoTable.

name: Single-writer fencing before reading rank state
why: D9: before touching a failed rank's state the replacement waits for an OSDMap at least as new as last_failure_osd_epoch, so OSDs reject the old holder (single writer).
risk: C++ gaps: FSMap::erase can zero the epoch, up:starting/creating never wait, wait_for_map does not re-check; consider waiting for the latest OSDMap at every takeover.

name: Standby-replay journal tailing (journal side)
why: Standby-replay is P1 (D9); per-shard WALs must be tailable by a follower without racing trimming.
subset: Legacy back-journal and reformat steps are out.

name: Journal creation and append-only open per rank state
why: The mon decides up:creating, up:starting or up:replay, and the MDS must create fresh state, reopen a cleanly stopped rank without replay, or replay.
subset: Rank state in the new format; shard WALs belong to shards, not ranks; the legacy reformat step is out.

group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
name: Metadata object naming and placement
why: The new on-disk format needs its own object naming in the metadata pool (D2); C++ names are read only by C++ tools.
subset: Use names or a dedicated RADOS namespace that cannot collide with mgr, cephfs-mirror or ceph-csi objects (F-STORE-102); per-shard prefixes allow shard teardown; byte-swapped frag decode is out.

group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
name: Special inode numbers and per-rank ranges
why: The kernel and libcephfs reject [0x100,0x1000), treat 1 as the mount root and 3 as the global realm, and ceph-fuse needs numbers below 2^48 (F-PROTO-100).
subset: Keep: root 1, 3 reserved, no user number below 0x1000, every number below 2^48; drop: per-rank 2^40 ranges, the 0x200-0x600 C++ object numbers, .ceph (2) and lost+found (4).
risk: Kernel lookups fail with -EREMOTEIO on [0x100,0x1000); ceph-fuse builds inode numbers as (stag << 48) | ino.

group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
name: Dirfrag omap object and fnode header
why: Directory contents and per-directory stats must persist (D2 purpose), and with one client-visible frag (D5) large directories must still scale.
subset: Per-directory entry index partitioned internally across RADOS objects (OSD LARGE_OMAP_OBJECTS at 200000 keys or 1 GiB), iterable in (hash24, name) order for readdir (F-CACHE-077), with a dirstat/rstat header.
risk: C++ users keep millions of entries per directory through fragmentation.

group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
name: Dentry omap keys, including snapshotted dentries
why: C++ omap key format (D2); snapshotted dentry versions are F-CACHE-011 (P1) and names are stored bytewise as sent (F-CACHE-077).

group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
name: Primary dentry value with embedded inode (InodeStore)
why: Every inode's persistent state (F-CACHE-001 fields, symlink target, user and ACL xattrs, realm node with quota and subvolume flags) must be stored; embedding it in the primary dentry is a C++ choice.
subset: Store it so the inode-number index can find it (F-STORE-062); the legacy 'I' marker is out.

group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
name: Remote (hard link) dentry value
why: Hard links within a shard are P0 (D14): the extra names store target ino and d_type.
subset: alternate_name comes with fscrypt/charmap (P2); legacy 'L' decode is out.

group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
name: Dirfrag fetch from RADOS
why: C++ dirfrag read path; reading directory entries is part of F-STORE-047 and damage on load is F-BG-053.

group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
name: Dirfrag commit to RADOS
why: C++ dirfrag write-back ops; checkpoint writes are F-STORE-016 and F-STORE-047.

group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
name: Base inode objects (.inode)
why: Inodes without a parent dentry in their own shard need a home: the file-system root in the root shard and each shard's root inode (D5 boundary).
subset: The legacy 'inode' xattr fallback is out.
question: Is a shard-root inode owned by its shard (C++ base-inode style) with a copy in the parent shard (F-CACHE-055)?

group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
name: Per-rank mdsdir and stray directories
why: Unlink-while-open and hard-link primaries need a hidden holding area (D14), and D3 makes stray handling per shard.
subset: Per-shard stray area instead of ~mdsN/stray0-9 and stray rotation; unlinked inodes leave the subvolume's rstat and quota at unlink as in C++; the legacy 'stray' name is out.

group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
name: Object creation for a new rank (mkfs)
why: Storage view of F-CLU-064: `fs new` (on an empty metadata pool) followed by up:creating must write the initial state.
subset: Root shard store, file-system-wide tables (inode-number allocator, shard map) and per-rank state; no C++ tables.

group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
name: Boot-time object loading
why: Storage view of F-CLU-063: a booting rank loads its state, and errors must map to damage or respawn per D10.
subset: Unreadable state damages the affected shard and -EBLOCKLISTED respawns; the C++ object list and the QA DAMAGED_ON_START expectations are out.

group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
name: Legacy on-disk formats still decoded
why: Legacy C++ formats (D1, D2); the new MDS reads none of them.

name: Backtrace parent xattr on object 0
why: No current peer reads backtraces (clients never do; only C++ tools, OUT by D2); lookup by number moves to an index (F-STORE-062).
risk: If the design reuses backtraces as the index they become P0 and must be written in the creating transaction, not lazily at segment expiry.
question: Keep data-pool backtraces or an equivalent for offline disaster recovery of the new format (P2)?

name: Layout and symlink xattrs on object 0
why: Read only by cephfs-data-scan (D2).

name: Backtrace copies in the default data pool and old pools
why: Backtrace copies serve C++ open_ino and tools only; no peer reads them.

name: Directory backtrace verification on fetch
why: Self-check of C++ directory backtraces.

name: Lookup by inode number through backtraces (open_ino storage path)
why: NFS handles (kernel nfsd, Ganesha) and libcephfs ll_lookup_inode carry only the 64-bit number and must resolve after restarts and cache trimming.
subset: Durable ino -> (shard, location, primary parent dirino and name) index updated in the same transaction as create/link/unlink/rename, serving LOOKUPINO, LOOKUPPARENT and LOOKUPNAME.
risk: C++ writes backtraces lazily at segment expiry; a lazy index would leave new files unresolvable by number.

name: Scrub tag xattr on object 0
why: C++ scrub tags are OUT unless a peer reads them (D10); only cephfs-data-scan does.
subset: Legacy client-side tag filtering is out.

name: Data object naming and striping shared with clients
why: Clients read and write data objects `<ino hex>.<objno %08x>` in (pool, namespace) with the Striper mapping themselves, so the inode numbers and layouts the MDS hands out define that namespace.
risk: Purge must remove object 0 in the file's pool and namespace even for empty files (the client pool-permission probe creates it).

name: Data-object truncation (truncate start/finish and TRIMTRUNC)
why: POSIX truncate: once the truncate is durable clients get CEPH_CAP_OP_TRUNC and the MDS trims objects with TRIMTRUNC and the new truncate_seq, which OSD semantics make idempotent and safe against racing client I/O.
subset: Restart after failover (F-CLU-100); the fscrypt last-block write is P2.
risk: Never abort on OSD errors (C++ asserts on single-object truncate results).

name: File size and mtime recovery by probing data objects
why: When a writer is lost, size and mtime must be recovered by probing the data objects (F-CAPS-022); clients and OSDs offer no other source.
risk: C++ marks the whole rank damaged on any probe error; contain per shard and retry.

name: Inline data uninlining and the inline_version xattr
why: Legacy: inline data is OUT (D12) and exists only under the deprecated flag.

name: MDSTable: versioned single-object table persistence
why: C++ whole-object table persistence; allocator, session and shard-map state get new formats (F-STORE-069, F-STORE-075, F-CACHE-036).
subset: Legacy upgrade save and the dead shutdown path are out.

name: InoTable object and per-rank inode ranges
why: Inode numbers must be unique per file system and durable before use; D3 asks for per-shard range leases from a file-system-wide allocator.
subset: Durable FS-wide allocator issuing never-reused ranges inside [0x1000, 2^48); exhaustion returns ENOSPC instead of aborting (C++ asserts).
question: Encode the shard in the range lease for cheap ino -> shard routing, and decide how inodes that join a new shard keep resolving (see F-CACHE-047).

name: Inode number allocation in create paths
why: Create-type ops need a number allocated and journaled atomically with the create and returned again on retry.
subset: Allocate from the shard's leased ranges; a client-supplied head.ino is honoured only from that session's preallocated or delegated set (P1 async create and early-reply replay) and otherwise validated, never trusted.
risk: An unexpected head.ino crashes the C++ MDS (strict-erase assert).

name: Session inode preallocation and refill
why: Per-session preallocation is needed only for async-create delegation and early-reply replays (D7, P1), not for P0 throughput once shards hold range leases.

name: Release of preallocated and delegated numbers at session close (EPurged)
why: Release and purge of delegated numbers comes with async create (D7).
subset: Never re-issue a number once delegated, or purge its object 0 in the right pool and namespace (C++ FIXME, mds-tables G23).

name: Inode numbers are never reused after deletion
why: NFS handles carry no generation number and data-object names derive from the number, so a deleted inode's number must never be reused.
risk: With range leases, never re-issue a range, including those of deleted shards.

name: InoTable replay, gap repair and the taken-number guard
why: Repairs for C++ InoTable replay gaps; the new allocator must be crash-consistent by construction.

name: SessionMap object
why: Sessions must survive failover so that reconnect, eviction of clients that do not reconnect and Ganesha reclaim (client_metadata, auth_name, uuid, timeout) work.
subset: Per-rank session store (sessions span shards, D4); completed-request and flush records may live with the shard (F-STORE-029/030); session preallocation is P1.
question: Where completed-request records live: per session (rank) or per shard (atomic with the mutation, migrating with the shard)?

group: Table server/client 2PC and the SnapTable object
name: SnapTable object (mds_snaptable)
why: Snapshot ids must be unique and monotonic per file system and start above the data pools' existing snap seqs; this comes with snapshots (D8).
subset: Legacy format upgrade is out.

group: Table server/client 2PC and the SnapTable object
name: Table server/client two-phase commit and its journal events
why: The table 2PC is MDS-to-MDS (free); P1 snapshots can use a file-system-wide snapid allocator plus shard-local realm updates (F-STORE-077).
subset: Legacy anchor-table skip is out.

group: Table server/client 2PC and the SnapTable object
name: Table server placement on rank 0
why: MDSMap tableserver is produced by the mon and ignored by the kernel; placement of a P1 snapid service is free.

group: Table server/client 2PC and the SnapTable object
name: NOTIFY_PREP fan-out barrier

group: Table server/client 2PC and the SnapTable object
name: Server-local table updates and table queries

group: Table server/client 2PC and the SnapTable object
name: Table 2PC recovery and message delivery rules

group: Table server/client 2PC and the SnapTable object
name: Resolve integration of table commits

name: OpenFileTable tracking and Anchor records

why: C++ OpenFileTable load and redo journal (D2).

why: C++ EOpen suppression.

group: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy
name: Per-rank Objecter RADOS client

subset: Plain RADOS ops only (omap, xattrs, compound ops, cmpxattr guards); follow OSDMaps; bound in-flight ops per shard (C++ never enforces its budget).

group: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy
name: RADOS identity and request ids
why: OSDs deduplicate ops by (entity, incarnation, tid), so a new instance must never be mistaken for the previous holder of the rank.
risk: If the RADOS client reuses an entity name with tids from 0, set the incarnation (C++ uses the FSMap inc); OSD full exemptions also key on the mds entity type.

group: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy
name: FULL_FORCE: MDS I/O ignores full flags

group: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy
name: Continuous OSDMap following

group: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy

risk: Re-check the target epoch after waiting (C++ does not).

group: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy
name: I/O completion path and self-respawn when fenced
why: A blocklisted instance must stop acting for its rank and come back as a fresh daemon with a new address, which the monitor's fencing assumes (D9).
subset: Keep: -EBLOCKLISTED on any RADOS op abandons the rank and restarts with a new messenger nonce; drop the finisher/mds_lock completion model (D16).

group: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy
name: OSD epoch barrier in cap messages
why: kclient and libcephfs pause OSD I/O until they have the osd_epoch_barrier carried in MClientCaps, so an evicted client's writes are fenced before others use new caps.
risk: Keep the barrier monotonic (C++ setters can lower it).

group: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy
name: Metadata-pool-full ENOSPC policy
why: A full metadata pool must stop metadata growth before the OSD fail-safe silently drops MDS writes; kclient and libcephfs surface the error.

question: Return ENOSPC (intended, doc/cephfs/full.rst) instead of the EACCES clients see from C++ (double-reply bug)?

group: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy
name: Metadata write-error policy and read-only mode
why: D10: backing-store write failures must be contained and never acknowledged; the kernel marks sessions read-only on FORCE_RO and the mon shows MDS_READ_ONLY.
subset: -EBLOCKLISTED respawns; otherwise read-only (EROFS for writes, write caps revoked, FORCE_RO, MDS_READ_ONLY), ideally per shard; no aborts on RADOS errors (C++ asserts on several).
question: Per-shard read-only? FORCE_RO is per session (the kernel marks the whole session read-only), so a per-shard mode must rely on EROFS and write-cap revocation.

group: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy
name: Pool requirements for CephFS pools
why: The mon enforces the pool rules (replicated metadata pool, cephfs application tag, EC overwrite rules, no pool snapshots) and the MDS relies on them, using only MDSMap data_pools for layouts.
subset: Nothing to build beyond validating layout pools and using the MDSMap metadata pool.
question: Beacons must still advertise MDSMap incompat 1-12 (named after C++ formats) to get a rank; add a private incompat bit (`fs compat add_incompat`) to keep C++ daemons out (constraint 3)?

group: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy
name: Metadata pool shared with mgr-owned objects
why: mgr snap_schedule (`snap_db_v0.db.*`), mgr mirroring and cephfs-mirror (`cephfs_mirror*`, watch/notify) and Rook's ceph-csi (namespace csi) keep objects in the metadata pool.
subset: Never create, modify, delete or report as damage any object outside the MDS's own names.
risk: Collisions or deletions break snapshot schedules, mirroring and CSI provisioning.

group: Observability, offline tools and test knobs
name: Journal and OpenFileTable perf counters
why: Default mgr flows read mds_log counters: the dashboard mds_log.ev, the Grafana mixin evadd/ev/seg through prometheus, `ceph fs status` mds_log.replayed for standby-replay.
subset: Provide mds_log.ev, evadd and seg (aggregated over the rank's shard WALs, same meaning); replayed with standby-replay (P1); other mds_log and oft counters P2 or OUT.

group: Observability, offline tools and test knobs
name: Op tracker journal events
why: Op-tracker event names help operators but no tool parses them; the dumps themselves are P0 (D13).

group: Observability, offline tools and test knobs
name: Offline journal reset and EResetJournal
why: cephfs-journal-tool reset and EResetJournal are C++ tool compatibility (D2).
question: Disaster-recovery tooling for the new format (WAL inspect/reset) is a P1/P2 decision; the documented runbooks will not apply.

group: Observability, offline tools and test knobs
name: cephfs-journal-tool inspection, export/import, header and event commands
why: C++ offline journal tool (D2).

group: Observability, offline tools and test knobs
name: Other offline tools over the on-disk format
why: C++ offline tools and ceph-dencoder types (D2).

group: Observability, offline tools and test knobs
name: Developer and fault-injection options
why: C++ dev and fault-injection options used by QA; the new MDS needs its own test hooks.
subset: Dead mds_kill_journal_at is out.

name: Subtree authority hand-off protocol (export/import state machines)
why: Live shard migration is P0 (D6); the dirfrag/bounds state machines and MExportDir* messages are MDS-to-MDS and free. Needed: a shard-granular, crash-safe ownership transfer with one commit point.
subset: The shard is the unit (no dirfrags, bounds or bystanders). Legacy unused message ids out.
question: Where does the shard-to-rank map live (epoch-fenced, readable by every rank for forwarding and LOOKUPINO): an MDS-private RADOS object, the root shard, or a new MDSMap field (needs a mon change)?

name: Export preconditions and silent refusals
why: A shard migration needs explicit preconditions (target active, no failover in progress, shard not already moving; later not quiesced or quarantined); C++ refuses silently, the new placement engine should report it.
subset: C++ system-inode and stray-directory rules disappear (strays are per shard).

name: Subtree freeze and auth-pin drain
why: Freezing and auth pins are C++ internals (D16); the client-visible contract (requests block without error, then are forwarded) is kept by F-MULTI-018 through a shard-level quiesce.

name: Lock set held during migration
why: Scatter-gather locks exist because another rank sums the dirfrag's stats (D5, D16).
risk: Cross-shard rstat and quota aggregation (D4) must not lose or double-count deltas in flight while a shard changes rank.

name: Prep phase: spanning-tree replication and bound opening
why: Spanning-tree replicas and bound dirfrags do not exist for self-contained shards (D3, D5).

name: Metadata and cap transfer encoding (MExportDir)
why: The importer must receive the shard's volatile state consistently with its durable metadata: caps (cap_id, seq, mseq, issued, pending, wanted), client ranges, fcntl/flock tables and client identities; with per-shard journals the durable part can be handed over in RADOS instead of copied (D2, D3).
subset: MExportDir encoding out. File locks must survive migration; dentry leases are not migrated (revoke first, P1).
risk: The dashboard and Grafana read mds.exported_inodes and mds.imported_inodes: keep counting inodes moved with shards (ADM).
question: C++ does not migrate per-session completed requests; should per-shard idempotency tables move with the shard?

name: Bystander warning and notify
why: No third rank replicates shard contents (D5); other ranks learn the new owner from the shard map.

name: Cache-expire routing during migration
why: Cache expires exist only for cross-rank replicas (D5).

name: Empty import return
why: Empty-import bounce is an artefact of dirfrag subtrees; a shard is placed whole.

name: Export queue and in-flight size throttle
why: Rank shrink and re-placement can move many shards at once; bounding concurrent migrations per rank is prudent but not needed for correctness.

name: Export splitting of large subtrees
why: Shards are indivisible placement units (D3); no export splitting.

name: Cap EXPORT message to clients (CEPH_CAP_OP_EXPORT)
why: Live migration is P0 (D6); kclient and libcephfs move or drop a cap only on EXPORT (placeholder cap toward the importer, session open, in-flight flushes moved).
subset: head.cap_id = current exporter cap id, migrate_seq = m, seq and caps 0, peer {importer cap_id, importer last_seq+1, m+1, importer rank, 0} at the size offset, counted, osd_epoch_barrier; peer.mds = -1 to drop.
risk: kclient ignores an EXPORT whose cap_id does not match; libcephfs keys on peer.cap_id (0 = drop and set I_CAP_DROPPED).

name: Cap IMPORT message to clients and auth-cap switch (CEPH_CAP_OP_IMPORT)
why: Live migration is P0 (D6); only IMPORT makes the importer's cap the AUTH cap (higher mseq) and makes clients re-send in-flight flushes and max_size requests.
subset: Legacy IMPORT without peer block (no EXPORT_PEER) out. Queue IMPORT until the client's session is connected.
risk: IMPORT seq must equal the issue_seq announced in EXPORT (kclient placeholder seq = issue_seq - 1), it must come from the owner only and carry the snap trace of the cap's realm.

name: Migrate sequence (mseq) and stale cap-message handling
why: mseq orders a cap's incarnations across ranks (D6): clients switch the AUTH cap only to a higher mseq (ceph_seq_cmp) and stamp it on updates and releases; the MDS drops messages with an older mseq.

name: Writeable-range reconciliation on cap import
why: If a client listed in client_ranges arrives without an imported cap (blocklisted, no session), the importer must schedule size recovery (F-CAPS-022), else bytes written up to max_size can be lost.

name: Client session flush barrier before shipping (FLUSHMSG)
why: Before cap state moves (D6), every client with caps in the shard must flush its pending cap releases to the exporter: FLUSHMSG with seq = push_seq, FLUSHMSG_ACK echoing it.
subset: Legacy skip for connections without EXPORT_PEER out (every baseline client has it).
risk: A client that never acks must not stall the migration forever: complete on stale or eviction, or cancel (F-MULTI-022).

name: Forced client session open on the importer
why: The importer must hold a session for every client whose caps it takes before sending IMPORT; clients accept an unsolicited CEPH_SESSION_OPEN and queued messages (F-PROTO-041).
subset: Persisted in the new session format; an importing session cannot be closed or evicted mid-migration; forced sessions the client never used are closed if the migration is reversed.

name: Request blocking and forwarding around migration
why: Requests on a migrating shard must block without error and, once ownership moved, be bounced with MClientRequestForward (the client resends), never relayed between ranks; DirStat auth in replies updates client routing.
risk: Kernel BUG_ON if a forward is sent for a tid that already got a reply; num_fwd must strictly increase (else -EMULTIHOP).

name: Export-target publication (MMDSLoadTargets, MDSMap export_targets)
why: Unmodified kclients reconnect to an export target in up:reconnect even without a session and libcephfs pre-opens sessions to targets; that is what makes an importer crash right after taking a shard recoverable.
subset: Send MMDSLoadTargets naming the destination before migrating a shard, wait until the MDSMap lists it, drop it after completion. Decay counters and bystander hits dropped.
risk: Needs mon cap mds x (profile mds); every change bumps the FSMap epoch; an export target >= 256 in the MDSMap shuts kernel mounts down.

name: Non-auth cap migration to the auth rank (MExportCaps, MGatherCaps)
why: Exists only because replica ranks issue caps (F-CAPS-035 OUT); the owner issues all caps and sends quota pushes itself.

group: Migration durability, cancellation and failure handling
name: Migration journaling (EImportStart, EExport, EImportFinish)
why: A crash at any point of a shard migration must resolve to exactly one owner (D6, D9); EImportStart/EExport/EImportFinish are C++ formats (D2; cephfs-journal-tool OUT).
subset: New durable hand-off record with one commit point (for example epoch-fenced shard ownership) and per-shard WAL handover instead of re-journaling the metadata.

group: Migration durability, cancellation and failure handling
name: Export cancellation and reversal
why: A migration must be abortable until its commit point, with clients keeping the exporter's caps (nothing was sent to them yet), for example when the target fails or a client does not ack FLUSHMSG.
subset: Add timeout-driven cancel (C++ cancels only on failures and the freeze timeout).

group: Migration durability, cancellation and failure handling
name: Rank failure during migration and resolve interplay
why: Per-rank failover (D9) combined with live migration (D6): every in-flight migration must end with one owner when the exporter, the importer or another rank fails; the C++ resolve and ambiguous-import machinery is MDS-to-MDS and replaceable by the commit record.
risk: C++ has an assert after an early reverse (subtree-migration 8); reuse its crash points (mds_kill_export_at, mds_kill_import_at) as test cases.

group: Migration durability, cancellation and failure handling
name: Freeze deadlock breaker (mds_freeze_tree_timeout)
why: Export side of the freeze deadlock breaker (F-CAPS-089), a C++ freezing artefact (D16).

group: Migration durability, cancellation and failure handling
name: Quiesce and quarantine guards on migration
why: Quiesce and quarantine are P2 (D12); once quiesce exists a migration must not let a shard escape an active quiesce (refuse or carry the state, F-QOS-049), while the persistent quarantine flag simply travels with the shard (F-QOS-066).

name: Decayed popularity counters (DecayCounter, meta_load)
why: Popularity counters feed only the default balancer, which is out (D5).

name: Popularity hits on metadata operations
why: Same as F-MULTI-026 (D5); O(depth) counter updates per operation also disappear.

name: Popularity transfer on export, import, subtree change, rename and split
why: Same as F-MULTI-026 (D5).

name: Per-rank load (mds_load_t) and mds_bal_mode
why: Balancer load metric (D5); the load_cent and q gauges have no known consumer.
question: A later load-aware shard placer (P2) would need per-shard load, not this metric.

name: balance_automate file-system flag
why: The default balancer is out (D5); the flag lives in the monitor's MDSMap, is off by default, and the new MDS ignores it.
question: Reuse balance_automate to gate a future load-based shard rebalancer (P2)?

name: Heartbeat epoch exchange (MHeartbeat)
why: MDS-to-MDS heartbeat of the default balancer (D5).

name: Default rebalance target computation (prep_rebalance)
why: Default balancer planning (D5).

name: Export selection (try_rebalance, find_exports)
why: Default balancer export selection (D5).

name: Idle import return (mds_bal_idle_threshold)
why: Balancer-epoch behaviour (D5), off by default.

why: Monitor-owned MDSMap field used only by the balancer; optionally it can restrict which ranks the default placement uses for unpinned shards.

name: Mantle Lua balancer policy
why: Mantle is out (D12); experimental and off by default.

name: Mantle cluster log messages
why: Mantle is out (D12).

name: Set and remove ceph.dir.pin
why: mgr/volumes (fs subvolume pin, fs subvolumegroup pin export) and Rook subvolume-group pinning set ceph.dir.pin; they expect the C++ validation and errors (EACCES without p, EINVAL for root, non-directory or parse error, EDOM for >= 256, negative unsets, rank >= max_mds accepted) (D6).
subset: Persist on the directory and bump ctime/change_attr; placement effect only for shard roots and their root-shard ancestors (F-MULTI-040).
risk: Only RMXATTR removes; a SETXATTR without value is EINVAL in C++.
question: Pins on directories that are not shard roots (classic deployments pin /home/* to spread load) cannot split a shard: store and report only, or make the pinned directory an implicit shard root (then renames and links across it get EXDEV)?

name: Pin read-back (InodeStat dir_pin, GETVXATTR)
why: Clients serve getfattr ceph.dir.pin from InodeStat dir_pin (own pin, -1 when unset) and send GETVXATTR for ceph.dir.pin.random and .distributed; admins and test_volumes read them back.
subset: Legacy parts out (InodeStat without REPLY_ENCODING, client fallback without OP_GETVXATTR).

name: Pin inheritance and precedence resolution
why: Placement hints (D6): a shard's target rank comes from its own pin, else the nearest ancestor pin or distributed flag (group, /volumes, /), the documented closest-parent-wins rule; only shard roots are placed.
subset: Evaluated per shard root over root-shard ancestors; pins inside a shard have no placement effect; a distributed flag only spreads child shard roots; mds_bal_export_pin=false disables all hints.
risk: The mgr/volumes trash rename moves a subvolume under /volumes/_deleting and changes its inherited hint: do not migrate shards that are being purged.

name: Pin enforcement and aux subtrees (handle_export_pins)
why: The placement engine (D6) must re-evaluate shard targets on pin commits, shard creation, MDSMap changes and failover, and migrate shards whose target is another active rank; C++ aux subtrees and per-tick queue walks disappear.
subset: Retry while the target is not active.
question: When a pin is removed, C++ leaves the subtree where it is unless an ancestor pin applies; with a default placement for unpinned shards, should removal move the shard back to its default rank?

name: Delayed pins (target rank >= max_mds)
why: Pins to ranks >= max_mds are accepted (operators and Rook may pin ahead of scaling) and must take effect when max_mds grows (qa test_phantom_rank); falls out of a placement engine that re-evaluates on every MDSMap.

name: Pins veto balancer exports
why: Explicit pins must override any automatic placement of shards (the C++ balancer veto becomes: automatic placement never moves a pinned shard); only a stopping rank overrides pins (F-MULTI-049).
question: Default placement of unpinned shards: C++ with the balancer off leaves them where their parent lives (normally rank 0); should the new MDS spread them automatically?

name: Distributed ephemeral pins (ceph.dir.pin.distributed)
why: Rook sets ceph.dir.pin.distributed=1 on every CephFilesystemSubVolumeGroup by default and mgr/volumes exposes it (D6): the subvolume shards of such a group must be spread over ranks by a consistent hash.
subset: Hash each child shard (not dirfrags), no forced fragmentation (D5); vxattr stored and validated as in C++ (strict_strtob, EINVAL); on directories without child shards store and report only.

name: Random ephemeral pins (ceph.dir.pin.random)
why: D12 (tolerate or OUT): mgr/volumes (fs subvolumegroup pin random) and Rook pinning.random set it; rejecting the vxattr would fail those commands and reconciles.
subset: Accept, validate (EINVAL on parse error or above mds_export_ephemeral_random_max, EDOM outside [0,1]), persist and return through GETVXATTR; no placement effect.
question: Treat a random policy on a group as a spread hint like distributed?

name: Consistent hash into a rank bucket (hash_into_rank_bucket)
why: Hash placement must move few shards when max_mds changes (qa grow and shrink tests check minimal movement); the exact C++ function is not a contract (balancer 7.7).
subset: Any jump-style consistent hash of the shard id over max_mds (as in C++, hints may then name ranks that are not up yet).

name: Ephemeral pin redistribution on max_mds and config changes
why: Rank grow and shrink driven by max_mds are P0 (D6): hash-placed shards must be re-placed with minimal movement when max_mds changes.
subset: Honour runtime toggles of mds_export_ephemeral_distributed/random; C++ frag-bit recomputation drops.

name: Subtree hand-off by a stopping rank (max_mds decrease)
why: A stopping rank (max_mds decrease) must hand off every shard, ignoring pins to itself, before the monitor can mark it stopped (D6).
subset: Targets come from the placement engine over the remaining ranks (C++: parent's authority or rank 0).
question: Keep the root shard (/, /volumes, groups) on rank 0, which never stops?

name: Hot-directory replication (REP_ALL, MDirUpdate)
why: No hot-directory replication (D5); DirStat dist stays empty, so clients never send USE_ANY_MDS reads to replicas.

group: Snapshot ids and the snap table
name: Snapshot id and realm seq allocation from one monotonic counter
why: Snapshot ids must be unique and increasing file-system-wide, above every data pool's snap_seq (OSD self-managed snaps), and share the sequence with realm seq that clients compare (D8: P1).
subset: Design now: an FS-wide snapid/seq allocator usable by every shard (data pools are shared across shards); P0 realm seqs stay constant.

group: Snapshot ids and the snap table
name: Rank-0 snap table service (SnapServer) and per-rank SnapClient cache
why: The purpose, one FS-wide table of existing snapshots that every shard can consult, is needed with snapshots; the rank-0 SnapServer, its full-table NOTIFY_PREP 2PC and the mds_snaptable encoding are replaced (D2).
subset: Dead prepare_create_realm path and cephfs-table-tool compatibility are OUT.

group: Snapshot ids and the snap table
name: Deleted snapshots reported to the monitor (MRemoveSnaps)
why: OSDs trim clones only after the monitor marks snap ids removed: the MDS must send MRemoveSnaps (pool -> snapid and destroy seq) and re-send until the monitor echoes it.
subset: Pre-octopus removed_snaps handling is OUT.

group: Snapshot ids and the snap table
name: MDS data writes carry the realm SnapContext
why: MDS-issued purge and truncate writes must carry the realm SnapContext, or post-snapshot data leaks into snapshots.
subset: P0 sends an empty SnapContext but should plumb it through purge and truncate from day one; the uninline path is OUT.

group: Snapshot ids and the snap table
name: allow_multimds_snaps flag and MULTIMDS_WITH_OLDSNAPS health check
why: Legacy (old-data): guards pre-Mimic snapshots; new file systems start with ALLOW_MULTIMDS_SNAPS and never reach it.

name: Snap realms and effective snapshot sets
why: D8: realms must exist for /, quota roots and subvolume (shard) roots because clients find quota roots by walking realms; the persisted realm format must already hold everything P1 snapshots need.
subset: P0: realms for /, quota directories and shard roots with an empty effective snapshot set; persisted realm node with seq, created, last_created, last_destroyed, current_parent_since, snaps, past_parent_snaps, flags (PARENT_GLOBAL, SUBVOLUME, SNAPDIR_VISIBILITY), last_modified, change_attr. Snapshot, hard-link and past-parent realms P1; legacy past_parents and old sr_t versions OUT.

name: Realm membership of caps and realm split on creation
why: Creating a quota or subvolume realm on a directory in use (resize of an unsized subvolume, group quota) must tell each client exactly which cached inodes and child realms moved (SPLIT lists); cap grants name the containing realm.
subset: Per-shard realm membership tracking replaces the walk of inodes_with_caps under mds_lock.
risk: A cap grant naming a realm not yet sent in a trace makes the kclient WARN; readdir must not give caps on entries in another realm.

name: Snap trace contents and client interpretation
why: D8: every reply and cap IMPORT carries the snap trace from the target realm to the root; the kclient always gets the old format (it never sets bit 19), libcephfs the new one if the MDS advertises bit 19.
risk: A malformed trace or a wrong trace_len makes the kclient blocklist itself.
question: D15: advertise NEW_SNAPREALM_INFO (bit 19) in P0? Without it libcephfs decodes old-format traces and loses SNAPDIR_VISIBILITY and the snapdir mtime/change_attr.

name: Per-realm MClientSnap notification (always op SPLIT)
why: Quota and subvolume realm creation or change is announced with MClientSnap op SPLIT (lists filled only for a new realm), sent counted on the session before the request's reply.
risk: libcephfs asserts split != 0 and that the first trace element is the split realm; the messages count toward push_seq, which REQUEST_CLOSE checks.

name: Global realm broadcast on every snap-table operation
why: Needed only so that hard-linked inodes in PARENT_GLOBAL realms learn of new snapshots (P1); C++ sends one message per session on every rank for every snapshot op.
subset: With D3, hard links inside subvolumes never use the global realm; notify only sessions holding caps in global realms.

name: Hard-link global realm (PARENT_GLOBAL)
why: Hard-linked inodes outside subvolumes need snapshot coverage from all their parents; relevant only with snapshots and only in the root shard (links never cross shards, D4).
subset: Design now: P0 hard links in the root shard carry no global realm; P1 must convert them when snapshots arrive.

name: Past-parent snapshots on rename and unlink
why: Keeps renamed or unlinked inodes covered by the snapshots of the realm they left (prior_parent_snaps in traces); P1 with snapshots.
subset: The realm node carries past_parent_snaps from P0 (F-SNAP-006); per-shard strays must be able to keep such inodes (F-SNAP-028).

name: Create a snapshot (MKSNAP, mkdir in .snap)
why: D8: P0 refuses snapshot creation as when allow_new_snaps is off; full MKSNAP (mgr/volumes, snap_schedule, ceph-csi VolumeSnapshots, cephfs-mirror) is P1.
subset: P0: MKSNAP -> EPERM (EROFS on a read-only MDS). P1: the full op (SnapPayload, check order, realm creation, notifications).
risk: mgr/volumes snapshot create and ceph-csi snapshots and clones fail until P1.
question: Snapshots of directories above shard roots (/, /volumes, groups; snap_schedule on / is common) span many shards: support them in P1 with cross-shard coordination or refuse them? Decide before freezing the P0 format.

name: Remove a snapshot (RMSNAP, rmdir in .snap)
why: rmdir in .snap (mgr/volumes, snap_schedule pruning, cephfs-mirror); unreachable in P0 because no snapshot exists and clients look the name up first.
subset: P0 answers ENOENT.

name: Rename a snapshot (RENAMESNAP)
why: RENAMESNAP (cephfs-mirror propagates snapshot renames); P1 with snapshots.
subset: P0 answers ENOENT.

name: Snapshot metadata at creation (SnapPayload)
why: cephfs-mirror stores primary_snap_id as snapshot metadata at creation; P1 with MKSNAP.

name: Modify snapshot metadata (SNAP_METADATA op)
why: cephfs-mirror and the mgr mirroring module write sync checkpoints with SNAP_METADATA (CREATE, CREATE|EXCL, REMOVE); P1 (D8 mirroring).
subset: P0 answers ENOENT.
risk: The mirror daemon holds only 'allow r' MDS caps and depends on SNAP_METADATA doing no MDS-cap write check; do not add one.

name: allow_new_snaps filesystem flag
why: fs set allow_new_snaps gates MKSNAP once snapshots exist; P0 behaves as if the flag were off.

name: Per-directory snapshot limit (mds_max_snaps_per_dir)
why: EMLINK at mds_max_snaps_per_dir; mgr/snap_schedule reads this MDS option to size retention.

name: Snapshot uid range (mds_snap_min_uid, mds_snap_max_uid)
why: Admin uid-range restriction for snapshot ops; the defaults allow every uid and no peer depends on it.

name: Snapshot path encoding, traversal and LOOKUPSNAP
why: Clients send snapdir paths in P0: the kernel splices .snap on ENOENT, mgr/volumes stats .snap/<name> before mkdir and lists .snap on subvolume rm; they must get ENOENT or empty answers, not errors.
subset: P0: parse the empty first path component; LOOKUPSNAP and lookups under .snap -> ENOENT; mutations under .snap -> EROFS; never create dentries for snapshot paths. Snapshot name resolution (own names, _<name>_<ino>) and snapid traversal P1.

name: List snapshots (LSSNAP, readdir of .snap)
why: D8: P0 serves an empty LSSNAP; mgr/volumes (subvolume rm, snapshot ls), the Rook cleanup job and ls of .snap list the snapdir.
subset: Empty listing with FRAG_END|FRAG_COMPLETE, DirStat and the directory realm's trace; full listing (plain own names, _<name>_<ino> for inherited ones, path2 paging) P1.

name: Read-only snapshot semantics and snapshot caps
why: Snapshot inodes are read-only with read-only caps and snapflush-aware opens; P1. EROFS for mutations on snapshot paths is already P0 (F-NS-017).

name: Snapshot attributes in InodeStat (snap_btime, snap_metadata)
why: ceph.snap.btime (mgr/volumes snapshot info created_at) and snap_metadata (cephfs-mirror) come from InodeStat at a snapid; P1.
subset: P0 encodes a zero snap_btime and empty snap_metadata.

name: Snapshot inode lookup by ino (LOOKUPINO with snapid)
why: Kernel NFS export of snapshot file handles; P1 with snapshots.
subset: P0: LOOKUPINO with a snapid -> ESTALE.

name: Metadata copy-on-write (first/last ranges, snapped dentries, old_inodes)
why: Snapshot views need dentry and inode versions as of each snapshot; P1, but the P0 metadata format must allow several versions per name and per inode.
subset: Design now: versioned dentry keys ([first, last] with a head marker), first recorded on every dentry/inode from P0 (or defined as older than any snapshot), room for old_inodes and for snapped file inodes keyed (ino, last).

name: Ancestor pre-COW and the COW sequence (global or subvolume-local)
why: Directory stats as of each snapshot must be preserved (mgr/volumes clone progress reads rbytes/rentries of snapshot directories); P1.
subset: With shards a per-shard seq (C++ mds_use_global_snaprealm_seq_for_subvol=false behaviour) avoids FS-wide coupling.

name: Lazy trimming of deleted-snapshot metadata
why: Metadata of deleted snapshots must eventually be removed and strays with snapshot history kept; P1.

name: Directory snapshot diff (READDIR_SNAPDIFF)
why: cephfs-mirror incremental sync (D8: snapdiff and mirroring are P1).
subset: P0 answers EOPNOTSUPP.

name: File block diff between snapshots (FILE_BLOCKDIFF)
why: cephfs-mirror block-level sync (D8: P1); do not advertise CEPHFS_FEATURE_BLOCKDIFF (23) before then, so libcephfs returns EOPNOTSUPP itself.
risk: C++ asserts on swapped snapshot arguments (client input); return an error instead.

name: Realm state replication between ranks (MMDSSnapUpdate, snaplock payload)
why: Shards on other ranks must learn realm changes above their roots (a group quota realm becomes the parent of the subvolume realms below it) and notify their clients; MMDSSnapUpdate and snaplock payloads are C++ mechanisms (D16).
subset: P0: propagate realm creation and re-parenting above shard roots to the owning shards and their clients; P1: snapshot-set changes to every shard.

name: Snaprealm reconciliation at client reconnect and rejoin
why: D9 failover: clients report realms and per-cap realms in MClientReconnect; the MDS must correct clients whose realm view is stale (for example a quota realm created just before the failure).
subset: P0: accept the realm records and send traces/SPLIT for caps reconnected under an outdated realm; snapflush rebuild P1.
risk: Never emit SPLIT with split = 0 (possible in C++; libcephfs asserts).

name: Directory entry statistics (dirstat / fragstat)
why: Directory nlink (2 + nsubdirs), kclient directory size (entries), mtime/ctime and the NFS change attribute come from dirstat, which must be exact when read with Fs; rmdir emptiness depends on it.
subset: Exact at once within a shard with one frag per directory; remote dentries count in nfiles.

name: Recursive subtree statistics (rstat)
why: ceph.dir.rbytes/rfiles/rsubdirs/rctime, directory st_size = rbytes (libcephfs default; mgr/volumes bytes_used and resize --no_shrink) and quota usage all come from rstat.
subset: rsnaps stays 0 until P1. Keep the semantics: rbytes = logical size, rsubdirs counts the directory itself, a hard link counts once, unlinked files leave at once.

name: Eager upward stat propagation (predirty_journal_parents)
why: Stat changes must reach every ancestor inside the shard up to the shard root within a bounded lag (C++: the parent at once on one rank, each higher level within about 1-5 s); quota enforcement and mgr/volumes bytes_used read the subvolume data directory.
subset: Commutative deltas (sum, max) so concurrent creates in one directory do not serialize; crossing the shard root is F-SNAP-037.

name: Deferred stat propagation (dirty rstat, updated scatterlocks, tick and nudge)
why: Dirty-rstat lists, scatter_tick/nudge and LOCK_AC_NUDGE are C++ scatterlock machinery (D16); the bounded-lag requirement is carried by F-SNAP-035 (in shard) and F-SNAP-037 (across shards).

name: Scatter-gather of dirstat and rstat across dirfrags and ranks
why: D4: shard-root rstat must be aggregated into root-shard ancestors (group dirs, /volumes, /), eventually consistent as in C++: group bytes_used and Rook's subvolumegroup resize --no-shrink, fs volume info (statx /volumes), group quotas, root_r* counters.
subset: A cross-shard rstat delta channel from each shard root to the root shard; dirfrag-level scatter-gather and MLock payloads are OUT (D5, D16).

name: Journal segment expiry waits for stat folding
why: Couples rank-journal segment trimming to scatterlock folding; with per-shard WALs and no scatterlocks the generic WAL checkpoint invariant covers it.

name: rstat reads routed to the auth rank (GETATTR CEPH_STAT_RSTAT)
why: Clients send CEPH_STAT_RSTAT getattrs to the inode's auth and apply directory rstat (libcephfs also quota) only from replies with CEPH_CAP_FLAG_AUTH or a newer version.
subset: The shard owning an inode answers.
