question: Which shard is authoritative for a shard-root inode (attributes, quota, rstat, caps, vxattrs): the subvolume shard or the parent shard that holds its dentry?

name: Snapshot rstats (mds_snap_rstat)
why: mds_snap_rstat defaults to false (snapshot views show rstats as copied at COW time); optional once snapshots exist.

name: Stat mismatch detection and in-place repair
why: Stat verification and repair belong to online scrub and repair of the new format (D10: P1).
risk: Never assert on a stat mismatch or negative count in production (C++ asserts under debug options); clamp and report.

name: Quota vxattrs (ceph.quota, ceph.quota.max_bytes, ceph.quota.max_files)
why: mgr/volumes (subvolume --size, resize, group quotas, clones) and admins set ceph.quota.max_bytes/max_files (IEC suffixes, 0 removes) with the MDS-cap p flag.
subset: Broadcast the new quota after commit (C++ broadcasts before); fix removexattr of the combined ceph.quota returning EINVAL.

name: Quota directories become snaprealm roots
why: D8 hard client requirement: after a successful quota setxattr the directory must be its own realm root, else kclient and libcephfs return EOPNOTSUPP and never enforce the quota.
risk: The new realm must reach the requester before it processes the setxattr reply (SPLIT sent before the reply).

name: Quota and usage in InodeStat
why: Quota and recursive usage travel in every InodeStat (rsnaps from v4, subvolume_id in v9); clients enforce from them.
subset: Legacy encoding without REPLY_ENCODING is OUT.
risk: The quota sub-struct must have struct_compat == 1 (kclient EIO).

name: MClientQuota usage pushes with thresholds
why: Clients learn usage near the limit and quota changes by other clients only through MClientQuota pushes from the quota inode's owner; without them writers overrun quotas.
subset: Thresholds (7/8 of the limit, 1/16 of headroom) may be tuned; group-quota pushes go from the root shard to clients holding caps on the group dir; NOQUOTA caps (legacy) OUT.
risk: Exact packed layout: the kclient parses fixed offsets and libcephfs asserts no trailing bytes; the message counts toward push_seq.

name: Client-side quota enforcement (EDQUOT, cross-quota EXDEV)
why: Quotas are enforced by clients (EDQUOT, EXDEV across quota realms) from MDS-supplied realms and usage; the MDS must keep realm roots resolvable by LOOKUPINO and usage current enough.
question: Keep client-only enforcement (C++ parity) or add MDS-side checks (max_files on create, max_size grants capped at max_bytes) for per-subvolume SLAs?

name: Quota-based statfs
why: df inside a quota directory reports the quota; the MDS side is the quota and rbytes in InodeStat plus one forced GETATTR per libcephfs statfs.

name: Legacy pre-Mimic quota realm creation (create_quota_realm)
why: Legacy (old-data) path for pre-Mimic quota directories without a realm, ineffective since v16.1.

name: Subvolume flag (ceph.dir.subvolume)
why: D3: ceph.dir.subvolume marks a shard root; mgr/volumes sets it on every subvolume it creates, re-applies it on every subvolume open and reads it back through GETVXATTR ('0'/'1').
subset: Contract kept: idempotent cheap no-op when already set, EINVAL for non-directories and nested subvolumes, realm with the SUBVOLUME flag, SPLIT notification. New: setting it creates a shard from an existing, non-empty directory (<uuid> already exists).
question: C++ allows clearing the flag (shard merge) and marking a directory above an existing subvolume (nested shards; changes the kclient-sticky subvolume_id). Refuse both?

name: No nested subvolumes; outermost subvolume wins
why: Nested subvolumes are refused with EINVAL; the outermost subvolume defines the subvolume (shard) of an inode.

name: Cross-subvolume link and rename rejected with EXDEV
why: D4: link and rename between different subvolumes (shards) return EXDEV, which clients already handle; a subvolume root can still be renamed between non-subvolume parents (mgr/volumes trash to _deleting).
subset: The rule applies at every shard boundary, including admin-marked shard roots; shard-root moves use the D4 mechanism.

name: Snapshots only at the subvolume root
why: Restricts MKSNAP below a subvolume root (EPERM); meaningful only once MKSNAP exists (P0 refuses all, F-SNAP-013).

name: Subvolume id on the wire (InodeStat, MClientCaps)
why: InodeStat v9 and flush acks carry subvolume_id (the outermost subvolume root, i.e. the shard root; 0 outside subvolumes); kclient and libcephfs key per-subvolume metrics on it.
subset: Encode subvolume_id in InodeStat v9 and cap flush acks: the shard root ino for inodes inside a subvolume (outermost ceph.dir.subvolume root), 0 elsewhere. A non-zero value never changes for an inode (kernel WARN_ON_ONCE). Its use for subvolume metrics is P1 (F-QOS-015, F-QOS-017).
risk: The kclient keeps the first non-zero subvolume_id of an inode and ignores later different values (WARN_ON_ONCE): an inode's id must never change, so shard split or merge must respect it.
override: Reconciles F-SNAP-054 (P0 contract), F-PROTO-025 and F-QOS-015 (P1): the field is part of the P0 encodings; the metrics that consume it are P1.

name: Snapshot visibility flag (ceph.dir.subvolume.snaps.visible)
why: Advisory flag for hiding .snap (libcephfs with client_respect_subvolume_snapshot_visibility, default false), used by mgr/volumes snapshot_visibility set/get; meaningful only with snapshots.
subset: Cheap to store in the P0 realm node; reaches clients only with bit 19.

name: Per-rank stray directories (~mdsN/stray0..stray9)
why: Unlink-while-open (D14) needs a durable home for unlinked but still referenced inodes; per D3 it is a per-shard stray area, not ten per-rank ~mdsN/strayK dirfrags (C++ layout OUT, D2).
subset: Legacy 'stray' dentry-name fallback is out. Internal objects are never exposed to clients (their inos stay unaddressable, ESTALE).
risk: The stray area must sit outside the shard root's rstat and quota tree, otherwise unlink stops freeing quota and ceph.dir.rbytes (F-BG-002).

name: Deferred deletion: unlink, rmdir and rename-over move the inode to a stray
why: POSIX unlink/rmdir/rename-over must return without deleting data while openers keep using the inode (F-NS-048); rstat and quota of the old parent drop at unlink, pool usage only after purge (strays-and-purge 7).
subset: Keep: reply after durable commit (D7) without waiting for purge; parent rstat/quota decrement at unlink time; remember the prior path (or shard) for MDS auth-cap path checks of open unlinked files (stray_prior_path).
risk: Path-restricted clients (CSI subvolume mounts, Ganesha exports) lose access to their open unlinked files if the prior path is not kept for auth checks.
question: When mgr/volumes removes a subvolume (rename into /volumes/_deleting, rmtree, rmdir of the shard root), where do the shard's remaining strays (files still open) and pending purge items go: keep a zombie shard until drained, or move them to the root shard?

name: Stray directory rotation per log segment and pre-fragmentation
why: Rotation per log segment and pre-splitting exist only to spread one shared per-rank stray namespace over dirfrags; per-shard stray storage has no client-visible dirfrags (D3, D5).

name: ENOSPC on unlink when the current stray dirfrag is full
why: ENOSPC on unlink is an artifact of the shared C++ stray dirfrag layout, not a POSIX unlink error; no peer depends on receiving it.
risk: The per-shard stray store must have no small fixed capacity: kernel async unlink (P1) cannot report the error and silently drops the dentry.

name: Stray dentry replication to other ranks
why: Strays and every cap on a shard's inodes live on the shard's owning rank (D3, D5), so stray replicas and cap export to the auth disappear.

name: Purge eligibility decision (eval_stray)
why: POSIX unlink-while-open: data may be purged only when no client holds caps or leases on the inode, including stale sessions not yet evicted, and no file-size recovery is pending (F-NS-048).
subset: P0 conditions: caps of any session (stale included), leases, pending size recovery, in-flight internal references. Snapshot conditions (past-parent snaps, old_inodes) come with P1 snapshots (F-BG-009).
risk: Purging while a stale or reconnecting session still holds caps loses that client's data.

name: Stray re-evaluation triggers (NOTIFYREF hooks and delayed list)
why: The purge decision must re-run when the last blocker goes away (cap release, session close or eviction, lease expiry); NOTIFYREF hooks and the delayed list are the C++ mechanism (D16).
subset: C++ misses snapshot deletion and migrated strays as triggers; the new trigger set should not.
risk: Without event-driven re-evaluation space is reclaimed only by scans; some C++ strays wait for cache pressure or a restart.

name: Prompt cap release for unlinked inodes (nlink 0 grant with Ls)
why: A grant carrying nlink 0 with Ls makes the kernel prune dentry aliases and libcephfs trim the inode, so caps go away at last close and the purge is not held up by client caches (strays-and-purge 7).
subset: Also honour the cap releases the kernel embeds in UNLINK (ceph_drop_caps_for_unlink).
risk: Without it unlinked inodes stay pinned by idle client caches until cap recall, and pool space is not reclaimed.

name: Snapshot-aware purge decision (past-parent snaps, realm SnapContext)
why: Keeping strays that snapshots still need and deleting with the realm SnapContext (so OSDs keep clones) comes with snapshots (D8).
risk: P0 purges with an empty SnapContext, which is safe only while MKSNAP is refused (D8).
question: C++ never re-evaluates strays when a snapshot is deleted; choose that trigger in the P1 snapshot design.

name: Truncate-only purge for multiversion files (TRUNCATE_FILE)
why: Truncate-only purge of multiversion files exists only for files that snapshots still reference (D8).

name: Hard-link reintegration (silent link-merge rename)
why: Hard links within a shard are P0 (D14): removing the primary name must leave the inode reachable through its other links, with nlink and ctime from the unlink and no further visible change.
subset: Links never cross shards (EXDEV, D4), so any relink is shard-local; if inodes are stored by ino rather than embedded in a primary dentry, reintegration disappears.
risk: C++ leaks the stray when its internal rename is lost (no timeout) and finds remote links only through cached dentries; the redesign must not depend on either.

name: Stray migration between ranks
why: Hard links stay inside one shard (D4), a shard lives on one rank and rank stop hands off whole shards (D6), so strays never migrate between ranks.

name: PurgeQueue journal of PurgeItems
why: Purge needs a durable per-shard queue of pending object deletions (D3) that decouples fast unlinks from slow RADOS deletes; the Journaler PurgeItem format and cephfs-journal-tool support are OUT (D2).
subset: Legacy PurgeItem v1 decoding and the 'assuming this is an upgrade' recreation are out.

name: Durable deletion intent before stray metadata removal
why: The deletion intent must be durable before the stray record is removed, or a crash leaks the file's RADOS objects with nothing left to find them (cephfs-data-scan is OUT, D2).
risk: Never recycle purged inode numbers: kernel NFS handles carry only the ino (no generation, mds-tables 7), so reuse makes stale handles resolve to another file.

name: File data and backtrace object deletion (PURGE_FILE)
why: Data objects are named and striped by the client-visible layout (<ino hex>.%08x in the layout pool and namespace), so purge must delete exactly the objects clients may have written.
subset: Delete objects 0..N-1 with N from max(size, largest client writable range, max_size_ever) and the file's striping, in the layout pool/namespace; -ENOENT counts as done; ops carry FULL_FORCE so purge works on full pools; -EBLOCKLISTED stops the daemon. Realm SnapContext with P1 snapshots; backtrace and old-pool object-0 deletes only if the new MDS writes such objects.
risk: Using size alone leaks objects a crashed writer created up to its granted max_size; without FULL_FORCE nobody can free space on a full cluster.

name: Directory object deletion (PURGE_DIR)
why: Whatever per-directory RADOS objects the new format creates must be deleted when an empty unlinked directory is purged, or metadata-pool objects leak with every rmdir; C++ dirfrag/backtrace object names are OUT (D2).

name: Purge throttling and pacing
why: mgr/volumes trash purge turns subvolume removal into mass unlinks; unthrottled deletes would overload OSDs for every tenant, so purge needs a budget scaled to OSD capacity and fair across shards (D3 isolation).
subset: Honouring mds_max_purge_files (0 pauses) and mds_max_purge_ops[_per_pg] is desirable for operator runbooks; mechanism free.
question: Purge budget per rank split fairly across its shards, or cluster-wide? C++ divides PGs by max_mds and has no per-subvolume fairness.

name: Parallel execution with contiguous expire_pos progress
why: Contiguous expire_pos tracking is how the C++ Journaler-based queue persists progress; durable progress is part of the per-shard queue (F-BG-013, F-BG-019).
risk: Avoid the C++ head-of-line blocking where one huge file holds back expiry of all later items.

name: Purge recovery and at-least-once execution
why: Pending purges must resume after restart or failover without operator action (D9); at-least-once execution with idempotent deletes (-ENOENT tolerated) is the outcome to keep.
subset: Standby-replay specifics are P1 (D9).
risk: After replay an inode whose purge was already durable must not become reachable by LOOKUPINO again (C++ gap).

name: PurgeQueue error handling (read-only queue)
why: Purge-queue storage or decode errors must be contained to the shard (D10) instead of forcing the whole rank read-only, and -EBLOCKLISTED must stop the daemon (fencing).
subset: Retry or report OSD delete errors other than ENOENT instead of silently leaking objects; mds_action_on_write_error semantics are free.
risk: C++ can self-deadlock pushing to a read-only queue under mds_lock; do not copy the path.

group: Rank lifecycle: activation scan and rank stop
name: Activation stray scan
why: After recovery each shard must find its unpurged strays and re-run the purge decision; C++ loads every stray of the rank under mds_lock at activation.
subset: Per shard, incremental, not blocking activation.
risk: Never evaluate strays before the shard's reconnect phase has ended: reconnecting clients may still hold unlinked files open (C++ waits until after rejoin).

group: Rank lifecycle: activation scan and rank stop
name: Rank stop: export all strays to rank 0
why: Reducing max_mds must complete (mon, cephadm and Rook wait for down:stopped; D6); with per-shard strays, the strays and purge queue travel with each shard the stopping rank hands off, replacing the rank-0 sink.
risk: C++ can stay in up:stopping forever when a stray migration fails; the hand-off must always make progress.

group: Rank lifecycle: activation scan and rank stop
name: Rank stop: drain the PurgeQueue
why: No pending purge may be lost when a rank stops (D6); with per-shard queues the items move with their shard (F-BG-022) and the new owner resumes them at least once (F-BG-019), so the C++ full drain before down:stopped is not needed.
subset: Hand off rather than drain: finish or abandon in-flight deletes (idempotent), move queued items with the shard; any rank-level purge work (e.g. delegated inos, F-STORE-072) must finish or move first. The clog progress line is optional; peers only wait for down:stopped.
risk: A full drain can keep a max_mds reduction (cephadm and Rook upgrades) waiting for hours after a large subvolume deletion.
question: F-CLU-102 says 'drain purge work' before down:stopped; confirm that handing off the per-shard queues is enough.

group: Stray visibility to clients and operators
name: Purging inodes are invisible to clients (ENOENT / ESTALE)
why: NFS handles (kernel knfsd, Ganesha via ll_lookup_inode) resolve inodes by number: an unlinked but referenced inode must stay reachable by LOOKUPINO until its purge starts, then lookups fail with ENOENT/ESTALE.
subset: LOOKUPINO of a not-yet-purging stray succeeds; after purge starts path lookups give ENOENT and ino lookups ESTALE; LOOKUPPARENT of an unlinked inode and internal inos give ESTALE; reconnect ignores caps on purged inodes.
risk: The new ino-lookup index (D2 redesign, answerable from any rank per D6) must keep strays until purge.

group: Stray visibility to clients and operators
name: Namespace rules for stray and unlinked directories
why: POSIX: creating in or renaming into a removed directory fails with ENOENT, and rename between two links of the same inode is a no-op returning 0.
subset: Keep ENOENT for create/link/rename into an unlinked directory and the same-inode rename no-op; internal stray/system objects are simply unaddressable (ESTALE); MDS-originated rename validation is C++ internal and dropped.

group: Stray visibility to clients and operators
name: dump stray admin command
why: Documented troubleshooting command for space that is not reclaimed (pinned strays); no mgr module, cephadm or Rook calls it, so diagnosis can follow the MVP (matches F-ADM-047).
subset: List the rank's pending strays per shard with ino, prior path and cap holders; the C++ JSON quirks ('ino: ' keys) need not be kept.

group: Forward scrub: control, scheduling and reporting
name: scrub start command
why: Online scrub and repair of the new format are P1 (D10); keep the documented command so runbooks (disaster-recovery-experts.rst) and QA keep working.
subset: 'scrub start <path> [recursive,repair,force] [tag]' accepted at least on rank 0 (ceph tell mds.<fs>:0) with reply {return_code, scrub_tag, mode}; scrub_path and scrub_start legacy aliases out; ~mdsdir and scrub_mdsdir see F-BG-035.

group: Forward scrub: control, scheduling and reporting
name: Scrub tags and the scrub_tag object xattr
why: The scrub_tag xattr on first objects only serves cephfs-data-scan --filter-tag (OUT, D2/D10); tags as scrub names live on in F-BG-028/F-BG-037.

group: Forward scrub: control, scheduling and reporting
name: tag path command
why: tag path only prepares cephfs-data-scan --filter-tag, an offline tool bound to the C++ format (D2, D10).

group: Forward scrub: control, scheduling and reporting
name: Scrub traversal order and scheduling (ScrubStack)
why: Carrier of the P1 online scrub engine (D10): a per-shard walk that validates what the new format stores.
subset: Avoid the C++ breadth-first walk that loads and pins whole trees; the uninline step is legacy (inline data OUT, D12).

group: Forward scrub: control, scheduling and reporting
name: Scrub concurrency throttle
why: Scrub work must be bounded so it does not starve client traffic of the shard's tenants; mds_max_scrub_ops_in_progress is the C++ knob.
subset: Keeping the option name is optional.

group: Forward scrub: control, scheduling and reporting
name: Incremental scrub and the force option
why: Skip-unchanged (incremental) scrub is an optimisation; full scrubs, with 'force' accepted as a no-op, suffice until there is demand.

group: Forward scrub: control, scheduling and reporting
name: Scrub stamps on inodes and dirfrags
why: Lazily persisted scrub stamps in inode_t/fnode_t are C++ format fields that no peer reads; an incremental scrub (F-BG-033) would define its own.

group: Forward scrub: control, scheduling and reporting
name: Scrubbing ~mdsdir / ~mdsN and scrub_mdsdir (stray loading)
why: doc/cephfs/scrub.rst tells operators to run 'scrub start ~mdsdir recursive' to make the MDS evaluate strays; the new design has no mdsdir.
subset: Accept ~mdsdir/~mdsN and scrub_mdsdir as 'verify and re-evaluate the strays of this rank's shards' so the documented step does not fail.

group: Forward scrub: control, scheduling and reporting
name: Scrub pause, resume and abort
why: Operator control of P1 scrubs (D10) through the documented commands.
subset: scrub pause|resume|abort with the C++ JSON replies ({message, return_code} / {return_code}); cross-rank propagation is free MDS-to-MDS.

group: Forward scrub: control, scheduling and reporting
name: Scrub status, summary and mgr task status
why: scrub status is the operator view of P1 scrubs, and the ServiceMap task status 'scrub status' shows in ceph -s while scrubs run (F-ADM-085).
subset: scrub status JSON {status, scrubs} with the C++ status strings (QA polls 'no active scrubs running'); task-status key 'scrub status' while not idle, empty map when idle; scrub_stats uninline counters out (legacy).

group: Forward scrub: control, scheduling and reporting
name: Scrub counters and scrub purge_status
why: Scrub perf counters are diagnostics that no mgr module or orchestrator reads, and their C++ names are tied to C++ checks.
subset: Per-tag uninline counters, scrub purge_status and mds_scrub_stats_review_period are legacy (out).

group: Scrub checks, repairs and data uninlining
name: Backtrace validation
why: Lookup by inode number (NFS handles, hard links) depends on correct ino-to-location records; the P1 scrub checks whatever the new format uses, backtraces or an index (D2, D10).

group: Scrub checks, repairs and data uninlining
name: Backtrace repair
why: P1 repair of the new format's ino-lookup records (D10); the C++ rewrite through dirty_parent is format-specific.

group: Scrub checks, repairs and data uninlining
name: Journal trim after repairs
why: Forcing repaired metadata out of the C++ MDLog is journal-specific; repairs in the new design are durable at WAL commit (D7).

group: Scrub checks, repairs and data uninlining
name: InoTable "inode wrongly marked free" check and repair
why: Inode numbers must never be handed out twice; the P1 scrub should check in-use inos against the fs-wide allocator and per-shard range leases (D3) instead of a per-rank InoTable.

group: Scrub checks, repairs and data uninlining
name: Base inode on-disk validation (root, ~mdsN)
why: Validates C++ base-inode objects (<ino>.00000000.inode, ~mdsN) that the new format does not have; failures were only logged.

group: Scrub checks, repairs and data uninlining
name: Directory dirstat/rstat validation and repair
why: Directory sizes, ceph.dir.r* vxattrs and client-side quota enforcement read dirstat/rstat; the P1 scrub must verify and repair them, including the eventually consistent aggregation across shard boundaries (D4).

group: Scrub checks, repairs and data uninlining
name: Dirfrag fragstat/rstat validation and repair
why: Dirfrag-level fragstat/rstat is C++ structure (D5); the stat check and repair live in F-BG-044.

group: Scrub checks, repairs and data uninlining
name: Dentry snapshot-bound check during scrub
why: Checks the C++ dentry first/last snapid encoding (the case first-damage.py targets, OUT by D2); the P1 snapshot design brings its own invariants.

group: Scrub checks, repairs and data uninlining
name: Hard-link resolvability check
why: Hard links within a shard (D14) must resolve by ino; the P1 scrub verifies that link targets exist and link counts match.

group: Scrub checks, repairs and data uninlining
name: Data uninlining during scrub
why: Legacy: inline data is deprecated and OUT (D12), and the new MDS never reads inodes written with inline data.

name: Scrub work forwarding to authoritative ranks (MMDSScrub)
why: A scrub started on rank 0 for a path that spans shards on several ranks must reach the owning ranks; whole-shard ownership (D3) turns this into per-shard dispatch with a free protocol.

name: Scrub completion protocol (MMDSScrubStats epochs)
why: scrub status must know when a multi-rank scrub has finished; the MMDSScrubStats epoch protocol, with its liveness gaps, is free to replace.
subset: MMDSScrubStats v1 decoding and the uninline payload are legacy.

name: Scrub behaviour on rank failure and restart
why: Scrubs need defined behaviour on failover; with shards moving between ranks a scrub could follow its shard instead of being aborted as in C++.

group: Damage detection, DamageTable and its effects
name: DamageTable registry
why: Damage containment is P0 (D10): known-bad metadata must be recorded so requests fail fast with EIO, MDS_DAMAGE is raised and operators can list and clear entries; keep the registry per shard.
subset: UNINLINE_FILE entries are legacy. Registry overflow must not take the rank down (C++ makes every report fatal past mds_damage_table_max_entries).
risk: MDS_DAMAGE is sent at HEALTH_ERR: Rook stops reconciling while it is raised and the mon refuses unconfirmed 'fs set max_mds' while any MDS reports a health metric.
question: Report one tenant's shard damage at HEALTH_ERR (C++, alerts) or WARN so it does not stall Rook for all tenants (same question as F-ADM-078)?

group: Damage detection, DamageTable and its effects
name: Dirfrag load damage detection
why: Metadata that is missing or does not decode must be recorded as damage and fail only the affected requests with EIO (D10), never assert or take the rank down.
risk: C++ asserts on unexpected read errors and malformed omap keys; a Rust panic on bad on-disk data would stop every shard of the rank.

group: Damage detection, DamageTable and its effects
name: Dentry snapshot-bound corruption check at load and commit
why: Guards the C++ dentry first/last snapid encoding against a historical corruption (first-damage.py, OUT by D2); generic load-time validation is F-BG-053 and snapshot invariants come with P1 snapshots (D8).
risk: Keep the spirit: never persist metadata that fails its own invariants, but contain it to the shard instead of aborting the daemon.

group: Damage detection, DamageTable and its effects
name: Duplicate primary inode detection on dirfrag load
why: An ino found under two primary records is inconsistent metadata; contain it as damage (D10) instead of silently hiding a name as C++ does (clog only).
subset: Part of F-BG-053's load-time validation; impossible by construction if inodes are stored by ino.

group: Damage detection, DamageTable and its effects
name: Fatal damage takes the rank down:damaged
why: D10 prefers per-shard isolation: damage to one shard's essential structures (WAL, stray area, purge queue, root) should fence only that shard, keeping down:damaged and 'ceph mds repaired' for rank-level damage.
subset: Registry overflow is not fatal.
risk: A down:damaged rank takes all its shards offline until 'ceph mds repaired'.
question: How does an operator mark a single damaged shard repaired? 'ceph mds repaired' is per rank, so a per-shard tell command is needed.

group: Damage detection, DamageTable and its effects
name: damage ls and damage rm commands
why: With damage containment in P0 (D10), operators need the documented 'damage ls|rm' to find and clear entries; otherwise MDS_DAMAGE (HEALTH_ERR) blocks Rook reconciles until a restart (matches F-ADM-050).
subset: damage ls JSON array {damage_type, id, ino, path, plus frag/dname/snap_id per type, shard where known} and damage rm <id> on every rank for that rank's shards; the 'uninline' type is legacy (out).

group: Damage detection, DamageTable and its effects
name: EIO for requests that touch known damage
why: D10: requests whose path crosses known damage fail with EIO while the rest of the rank and shard keeps serving; clients pass EIO through unchanged.

group: Damage detection, DamageTable and its effects
name: readdir behaviour on damaged directories
why: C++ lists a damaged directory as complete and (normally) empty without error; under D10 a damaged listing should fail with EIO, while individually undecodable entries may be skipped.
risk: Presenting a damaged directory as empty invites rmdir or rm -rf to succeed and lose the remaining entries.
question: Confirm EIO for readdir of a damaged directory instead of the C++ silent partial listing.

name: QoS admission gate for client metadata requests
why: dmClock admission is superseded by the internal per-shard fair scheduler (D11); it has no wire contract (latency only, off by default).
risk: Any scheduler must never fail requests and must bound delay for session-critical ones: the kernel's mount-time GETATTR times out after mount_timeout (60 s).

name: QoS bucket classification from the session mount root
why: Buckets keyed by the client-asserted mount root are replaced by the shard an inode belongs to (D3, D11).
subset: client_metadata 'root' itself stays needed for evict filters and mgr/stats (owned elsewhere).

name: QoS per-op cost table
why: A compiled-in dmClock cost table (1 for 11 read ops, 3 otherwise); the per-shard scheduler defines its own cost model (D11).

name: dmClock tag-based scheduling per bucket
why: Tag scheduling per mount-root bucket is dmClock-specific behaviour (D11) and gives no capacity-aware SLA anyway (qos-dmclock-scheduler 8).

name: QoS scheduler threads and hand-off to request processing
why: Three scheduler threads per rank and a hand-off under mds_lock are C++ internals (D16).
risk: Requests waiting in the Rust scheduler should appear in ops in flight (operator essential, D13); C++ hides queued requests while counting their age.

name: Default QoS parameters (mds_dmclock_* options)
why: dmClock admin surface (D11); no mgr module, cephadm or Rook sets mds_dmclock_*, and only the MDS reads them (matches F-ADM-056).
question: The per-subvolume SLA use case needs its own admin surface: reuse the mds_dmclock_* and qos command names keyed by subvolume, or define new ones?

name: Per-bucket QoS overrides (qos set, qos rm)
why: Per-rank, in-memory overrides keyed by mount-root prefix are dmClock admin surface (D11) with no programmatic caller (matches F-ADM-056).
question: If per-subvolume limits get an admin surface, should they live in a persistent vxattr on the subvolume root that moves with the shard (C++ declares an unimplemented read_xattrs) rather than in tell commands?

name: QoS inspection commands and per-bucket statistics
why: dump qos / qos get inspect dmClock buckets (D11); no peer parses them (matches F-ADM-056).

name: QoS bucket state lifecycle tied to sessions
why: Per-rank in-memory buckets created and destroyed with sessions are dmClock integration internals; per-shard scheduling state belongs to the shard.

name: QoS enable, disable and drain on rank state and option changes
why: Enable, disable and drain of the dmClock queue on rank-state changes are integration internals (with a self-deadlock); a per-shard scheduler is always on and moves with its shard.

name: Client metrics negotiation (feature bit 14 and metric_spec)
why: Every OPEN to current clients carries supported_features and metric_spec (MClientSession v4+); bit 14 decides whether clients send metrics at all, and mgr/stats reads each client's own metric_spec from client ls without a default.
subset: Advertise bit 14 and a metric_spec of types 0-15 in every OPEN (add 16 with P1 subvolume metrics); store the client's metric_spec and dump it as client_metadata.metric_spec.metric_flags.feature_bits in session ls/client ls. Non-MIMIC (v1) OPEN is legacy (out).
risk: A session lacking metric_spec in client ls raises KeyError in mgr/stats and aborts the rest of that reply.

name: MClientMetrics ingestion of per-client metrics (types 0..9)
why: fs perf stats and cephfs-top show the latest per-client values of types 0-9; D13 lists mgr/stats among the P0 mgr modules (matches F-ADM-106).
subset: Types 0-9 in the v2 latency encoding; v1 latency decoding is legacy (out). Store the client's latest values, do not accumulate.
question: D11 only demands tolerance of client metrics; classified P0 by D13. If the team defers fs perf stats data, F-QOS-012/014/018/020/021/028/029/030 drop to P1, while F-QOS-011's client ls fields and F-QOS-013 stay P0.
override: mgr `stats` is not an always-on module (src/mon/MgrMonitor.cc:80-106 at the map commit); `fs perf stats` and cephfs-top are opt-in observability. P0 keeps the tolerance (F-QOS-013, F-PROTO-096) and the client ls fields (F-QOS-011).

name: Tolerant decoding of unknown metric types
why: D11: client metrics must never break a session; a decode exception faults the connection and resets the client's session socket (metrics 3.3).
subset: Accept CEPH_MSG_CLIENT_METRICS (type 29) on any rank, in any state, from any session; skip unknown or not-yet-implemented items (type 16 before P1) by struct_len; unlike C++, do not fault on a known type with a too-new struct_compat; never reply.
risk: libcephfs with client_collect_and_send_global_metrics=true sends every type, including 16, regardless of metric_spec once bit 14 is set.

name: Metrics accepted on any active rank (client send rules)
why: Kernel metrics can arrive at any rank (last OPEN with bit 14) and libcephfs metrics only at rank 0; with multi-rank P0 (D6) the aggregator must merge them per client without the C++ zero-flapping from ranks that hold a session but get no metrics.
risk: mgr/stats enriches only clients listed by rank 0's client ls; keep every client with a rank-0 session (e.g. root shard on rank 0) or they vanish from fs perf stats.
override: Same as F-QOS-012: per-client metric aggregation serves only the opt-in stats module.

name: Subvolume id in InodeStat and cap flush acks
why: subvolume_id in InodeStat v9 and cap flush acks only tags client I/O for subvolume metrics (P1, D11); with D3 it is the shard root ino.
subset: P0 may send 0 (the kernel then creates no subvolume records) or the real id; filling it from day one is free.
risk: A non-zero id must never change for an inode: the kernel WARN_ON_ONCEs on X->Y and ignores X->0.
question: Reconcile with F-SNAP-054 (P0, real id) and F-PROTO-025 (fill it with P1). If admins may mark arbitrary directories as shard roots (D3), keep subvolume_id = outermost ceph.dir.subvolume root (nested subvolumes refused), not the innermost shard.

name: Subvolume I/O metrics (type 16) ingestion and path resolution
why: Per-subvolume I/O metrics are P1 (D11); the owning rank knows its shard root paths, but kernel samples can land on any rank and need ino lookup or forwarding to the owner (D6).
subset: C++ silently drops samples whose subvolume root is not cached on the receiving rank.

name: Feature bit 22 enables kernel subvolume metrics
why: Bit 22 in the MDS bitmap only switches the kernel's subvolume metrics on (libcephfs never tests the MDS's bit 22), so it belongs with P1 subvolume metrics (D15).
subset: P0: do not advertise bit 22; the kernel then clears its subvolume tracker and still sends types 0-9. P1: advertise it once type-16 items are aggregated. The client's own bit 22 (CHARMAP for libcephfs, SUBVOLUME_METRICS for the kernel) is F-PROTO-025's concern.
risk: All ranks must advertise identical bits: the last OPEN from any rank flips the kernel's tracker, and while enabled it skips sessions without bit 22 as metrics targets.

name: Per-rank metrics forwarding to rank 0 (MMDSMetrics)
why: With multi-rank P0 (D6), every rank must forward its clients' latest metrics to the rank that answers the mgr (rank 0); MMDSMetrics is MDS-to-MDS and free to redesign.
subset: Subvolume aggregates and rank telemetry in the message come with P1 (F-QOS-016, F-QOS-022).
override: Same as F-QOS-012.

name: Rank-0 ping sequence and delayed-rank detection
why: The mgr shows ranks with stale metrics as delayed_ranks; the ping and sequence protocol behind it is free.
subset: P0 may report an empty rank_metrics_delayed set.

name: Client session lifecycle in metrics (REFRESH and REMOVE)
why: Per-client metric state must appear and disappear with sessions so closed clients leave fs perf stats (QA asserts counters vanish on disconnect); C++ can lose REMOVE updates.
override: Same as F-QOS-012.

name: Metrics state culling on mdsmap changes
why: With multi-rank P0 (D6), the aggregator must drop state of ranks that left and survive a rank-0 change, without the C++ labeled-counter leak.
override: Same as F-QOS-012.

name: Rank telemetry: CPU usage and open requests (mds_rank_perf)
why: ceph_mds_rank_perf_cpu_usage/open_requests feed panels of the shipped Grafana CephFS dashboard through ceph-exporter (config-perf-counters 3.8); cheap per rank (matches F-ADM-068).
question: Pull into P0 with the Grafana dashboard, as F-ADM-068 asks?

name: Subvolume quota_bytes and used_bytes reporting
why: quota_bytes/used_bytes per subvolume are part of P1 subvolume metrics (D11); the owning rank holds the shard root's exact quota and rbytes, removing C++'s last-broadcast-wins and stale-replica values.

name: Per-client labeled metric counters (mds_client_metrics)
why: mds_client_metrics labeled counters are documented (metrics.rst) and exported by ceph-exporter; no mgr module needs them (matches F-ADM-068).
subset: Keep set, label and counter names; fix the C++ value quirks (stuck latencies, opened_inodes = total_inodes).

name: Subvolume sliding-window metrics (mds_subvolume_metrics)
why: mds_subvolume_metrics (8 counters, labels fs_name/subvolume_path) feeds the shipped Grafana subvolume dashboard and is QA-asserted; per-subvolume metrics are P1 (D11).
subset: Window mechanics free; fix the n/(n-1) rate inflation.

name: Eviction of idle subvolume metrics
why: Subvolume counter sets must disappear after a window without samples (documented, QA-asserted); comes with subvolume metrics (P1, D11).

name: Labeled metric counter naming and export
why: ceph-exporter derives Prometheus series names from labeled set names and labels, so dashboards depend on them; comes with the labeled counters (P1).

name: MDS perf query configuration from ceph-mgr
why: mgr/stats registers its queries and the mgr pushes them in MMgrConfigure to every MDS; the daemon holding rank 0 must evaluate them (D13 stats, F-ADM-106).
subset: Decode and accept the perf-query part of MMgrConfigure on every rank (MgrClient obligation, F-PROTO-104); evaluating the queries and attaching results to MMgrReport is P1 (F-QOS-029/030).
risk: A MgrClient that rejects MMgrConfigure carrying an MDSConfigPayload could stall perf-counter reporting (status, dashboard, prometheus) as soon as someone runs fs perf stats.
override: Only the decode is needed by default flows; answers serve the opt-in stats module.

name: MDS perf query key construction and counter pairs
why: fs perf stats and cephfs-top need exact query echo, regex-capture keys and 16-byte counter pairs for the per-rank client and global client queries (D13, F-ADM-106).
subset: MDS_RANK and CLIENT_ID sub-keys (ECMAScript regex capture groups over the rank and 'client.<gid> <addr>') with counters 0-15 and the C++ pair semantics; SUBVOLUME_PATH keys and counters 16-23 come with P1 subvolume metrics.
override: Same as F-QOS-012.

name: MDS perf report to ceph-mgr (MMgrReport)
why: The rank-0 daemon attaches the query results to every MMgrReport (MDSMetricPayload) for fs perf stats (D13, F-ADM-106).
risk: Never send a metric report type other than 0 or 1 (the mgr aborts on UnknownMetricPayload); report all current keys every period because the mgr drains on read.
override: Same as F-QOS-012. Invariant kept for P1: never send a metric report type other than 0 or 1.

name: Quiesce DB leader and membership from the MDSMap
why: Quiesce is P2 (D12); mgr/volumes routes fs quiesce to the gid the monitor publishes as qdb_leader.
risk: Decoding the MDSMap fields qdb_cluster_leader/members (ev >= 19) is P0 regardless (CLU).

name: MDS compat incompat feature 12 (quiesce subvolumes)
why: The unmodified mon puts incompat 12 in the default compat of every new file system, and a daemon lacking any incompat bit of the fs compat is never assigned a rank, so bit 12 must be handled in the compat strategy (F-CLU-014, beacon-and-monitor 3.17).
subset: Follow F-CLU-014: under its recommended {7, N} set, do not advertise bit 12 and strip it from the fs compat with bits 1-6 and 8-12; only a zero-touch strategy that advertises the C++ default bits advertises 12, with no quiesce behaviour behind it.
risk: Mishandling it means no rank is ever assigned, or Rust standbys become eligible for C++ file systems; the compat set must also stay constant for the process lifetime (mon eviction).

name: Quiesce sets and request operations
why: Quiesce (D12): set and request semantics are user-visible API through ceph fs quiesce (fs-volumes.rst).

name: Quiesce set and member state machine
why: Set and member state names and their aggregation are user-visible in the quiesce db JSON (D12).

name: Quiesce timeout and expiration
why: Timeout and expiration semantics are documented fs quiesce API (D12).

name: Quiesce await semantics
why: Await outcomes and their error codes are documented fs quiesce API (D12).

name: Quiesce if_version optimistic concurrency
why: if_version (ESTALE; 0 means create-only) is documented fs quiesce API (D12).

name: Quiesce root URI sanitization
why: Root normalisation to file:/path is visible in quiesce replies (D12).
subset: inode: roots could work with per-shard ino lookup (C++ fails them).

name: Quiesce DB replication between ranks
why: Quiesce DB replication between ranks is MDS-to-MDS and free to redesign (D12).

name: Per-rank quiesce agent
why: The per-rank agent that turns sets into local quiesce actions is internal (D12).

name: Quiesce on degraded file systems and non-active ranks
why: C++ cancels every set while any rank recovers; per-shard recovery could keep unaffected shards quiesced (D12).

name: Tree quiesce request (quiesce_path)
why: With hierarchical S/X/IS/IX locks, quiescing a root is one subtree-level lock that conflicts with writers' intention locks, not an internal request walk per path (D12, D16).

name: Per-inode quiesce request (quiesce_inode)
why: Outcome: write and exclusive caps under the root are revoked and acked before QUIESCED; the per-inode request walk is C++ mechanism (D12).

name: quiescelock and parking of mutations
why: Outcome: mutations under a quiesced root park while reads, mksnap, flushes and file locks proceed; quiescelock itself is C++ internal (D12, D16).

name: Cap masking while quiesced
why: Clients see only p As Ls Xs Fs Fr Fc Fb while quiesced (keeping Fb avoids forced write-back), and QA asserts it (D12).

name: Quiescing inodes that appear during a quiesce
why: A subtree-level quiesce lock covers inodes loaded or imported later by construction, so no per-inode follow-up ops are needed.

name: Quiesce and directory fragmentation
why: There is no client-visible directory fragmentation to coordinate with (D5).

name: Quiesce and subtree migration
why: A shard migration (D6) must not let a subtree escape an active quiesce: refuse it or carry the quiesce state (D12).

name: Quiesce release and cancel cascade
why: Release drops the quiesce, wakes parked requests and re-issues caps; mechanism free (D12).

name: Quiesce dispatch throttle and heartbeat resets
why: Dispatch throttling and heartbeat resets exist because C++ quiesces inode by inode under mds_lock.

name: ceph.quiesce.block vxattr
why: Persistent ceph.quiesce.block flag exempting a subtree, set by clients through the ceph.* xattr passthrough (D12).

name: quiesce db command
why: quiesce db is what mgr/volumes fs quiesce sends to the qdb leader; its JSON layout and errnos are documented API (D12, F-ADM-054).
subset: Until built, answer with a plain error (e.g. EOPNOTSUPP), never -ENOTTY naming this daemon as leader: the mgr would retry 5 times.
question: ceph-csi's CephFS VolumeGroupSnapshot (outside the map) is believed to call fs quiesce; verify before keeping quiesce at P2.

name: Quiesce observability: counters and op events
why: Quiesce progress visibility (ops in flight, counters) for operators and QA; the C++ names follow its per-inode ops (D12).

name: quarantine enable and disable commands
why: Quarantine is P2 (D12); mgr/volumes fs subvolume quarantine sends these commands and returns the JSON verbatim (F-ADM-055).
subset: Reach the owning rank instead of answering -EXDEV: the mgr picks the first active MDS and its comment expects forwarding.

name: Persistent quarantine flag in inode optmetadata
why: The flag must persist with the subvolume root and survive failover; its on-disk encoding is free (D2, D12).

name: In-progress quarantine state and operation ordering
why: Enforcement from acceptance and its ordering with the journal commit are internal (D12).

name: Per-subvolume quarantine operation registry
why: One enable/disable per subvolume at a time with EBUSY (QA retries on EBUSY); mechanism free (D12).

name: Quarantine undo on failure
why: Undo of the in-progress state on failure is internal (D12).

name: Quarantine cap-revocation walk
why: Caps must drop to PIN (or come back) at once; with shard = subvolume all its caps are on the owning rank, removing the C++ coverage gap across subtree bounds (D12).

name: Quarantine propagation to replica ranks
why: Only the parent shard's boundary copy of the subvolume root needs the flag (D5); no general replica propagation (D12).

name: Subtree export refused inside a quarantined subvolume
why: Whole-shard migration (D6) carries the persistent flag; refusing exports would block max_mds reduction, which C++ QA has to work around.

name: Quarantine re-enforcement after restart
why: After failover, reconnected caps on a quarantined subvolume must again be limited to PIN (D12).

name: Quarantine enforcement predicate
why: With shard = subvolume, 'under quarantine' is a flag of the inode's shard (O(1), can fail closed) instead of a realm-chain walk on every request and cap issue (D12).

name: MDS auth cap flags q and Q (quarantine access)
why: Quarantine-specific use of the q/Q grant flags in access checks and cap issue (D12; matches F-ADM-015).
risk: The MDS cap parser must already accept q and Q in P0 (F-ADM-006/015): the mon accepts such grants and clients carrying them must still mount.

name: Quarantine client feature bit 24
why: The client's bit 24 selects EACCES (aware) or parking (unaware) once quarantine exists (D12).
subset: P0 does not advertise bit 24 (D15); libcephfs never tests the MDS's bit 24.

name: EACCES for quarantine-aware sessions
why: mgr/volumes infers quarantine from EACCES (subvolume info) and aware libcephfs clients expect it (D12).

name: Request parking for quarantine-unaware sessions
why: Quarantine-unaware clients (every kernel) block until the quarantine is lifted (D12).
subset: Park before taking locks: C++ parked requests keep path locks and can wedge enable and disable.

name: Snapshot operation parking under quarantine
why: Snapshot operations of unaware clients on a quarantined subvolume park, protecting recovery snapshots (D12; snapshots P1).

name: Cap restriction to PIN under quarantine
why: Clients without q/Q get only PIN on quarantined inodes (D12).

name: EQUARANTINED errno in MClientCaps
why: libcephfs marks an inode quarantined on a revoke carrying -EQUARANTINED (D12).
risk: Whenever MClientCaps v14 is sent before quarantine exists, oserrno must be 0.

name: QUARANTINE marker in InodeStat
why: libcephfs detects quarantined subtrees from optmetadata kind 2 on the subvolume root (D12).
risk: Never emit optmetadata kind 2 before quarantine exists.

name: MQuarantineDisable notification
why: Quarantine-aware clients clear their mark on MQuarantineDisable (D12).
risk: Send it uncounted (push_seq counts only CAPS, SNAP, LEASE, QUOTA): C++ counts it while libcephfs does not, so a later REQUEST_CLOSE is dropped. Never send it to the kernel.

name: MDS self-authentication, keyring and rotating service secrets
why: The MDS must authenticate as mds.<id> to mons, OSDs and mgr and verify client authorizers with the rotating mds secrets; cephadm puts the keyring in $mds_data, Rook passes --keyring.
subset: Keyring default /var/lib/ceph/mds/ceph-<id>/keyring or --keyring; rotating-secret renewal; aes256k keys and rotating secrets (Rook v1.21 sets auth_preferred_cipher/auth_service_cipher aes256k on supporting releases).
risk: Without aes256k support the MDS cannot authenticate on Rook clusters that prefer aes256k.

name: Peer authorizer verification and caps loading at connection accept
why: Every peer connection carries a cephx ticket whose mds caps become the session's auth caps; a missing or unparseable mds cap must refuse the connection (msgr2 AUTH_BAD_METHOD, kclient returns -EACCES).
subset: On kernel msgr1 connections a refused authorizer gets BADAUTHORIZER, and the cephx_require_signatures and cephx_service_require_version gates apply (decision 3).
risk: Caps are a snapshot per connection; mgr/nfs relies on caps never changing on an established connection.
override: Decision 3 (2026-10-11): a basic msgr1 listener for kernel clients is P0, so kernels mounted without ms_mode (Rook's default requireMsgr2=false for ceph-csi, the old device syntax, ms_mode=legacy) work unchanged.

name: Authentication method none (and Kerberos) means allow-all
why: With auth_service_required=none every client is treated as `allow *`; cephadm and Rook always deploy cephx, so MVP clusters do not need it.
subset: auth none => allow_all caps (including tell); Kerberos/gss not supported.
risk: If auth-none clusters are in scope for the MVP, every client is refused without it.

name: Peer-type message filtering and rank address check
why: Client-only messages must be accepted only from client peers and inter-rank messages only from authenticated MDS peers of the file system; this is part of the multi-tenant boundary, the C++ dispatch mechanism is internal.
risk: C++ does not bind the HELLO peer type and source to the authenticated entity; copying that keeps a spoofing gap.
question: Bind peer type and source to the authenticated cephx entity (stricter than C++, no current peer affected)?

name: Daemon key rotation commands (rotate-key, wipe-rotating-secrets)
why: cephadm's rotate-key path has no caller at this commit and Rook rotates with mon `auth rotate` plus a pod restart, so no default flow sends rotate-key or wipe-rotating-secrets.
risk: If cephadm activates daemon key rotation, a missing rotate-key forces its restart fallback.

group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
name: MDS cap string grammar, parser and canonical forms
why: The monitor validates and stores mds cap strings with the C++ parser, so the MDS must accept exactly that language (byte-exact `allow` = rwps, flags in order r w f p Q q s, fsname/path/root_squash/uid/gids/network qualifiers) or refuse the connection.
risk: A stricter parser refuses entities the mon accepted; a looser one can grant unintended access.

group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
name: Grant evaluation: union of grants in a fixed step order
why: Union-of-grants evaluation in the fixed step order is the server-side multi-tenant authorization for kclient, libcephfs, Ganesha and mgr; denial is -EACCES.

group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
name: path= restriction and the inode path used for checks
why: Subvolume isolation: mgr/volumes, mgr/nfs and fs authorize produce path grants checked against the inode's primary path from the fs root (stray_prior_path for unlinked-open inodes).
risk: With shards on different ranks the serving rank must know the shard root's current absolute path (ancestor renames such as the trash rename into /volumes/_deleting) and the prior path of unlinked-open inodes; a stale path is a cross-tenant leak or a false EACCES.

group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
name: fsname= restriction and file-system gating of session messages
why: Multi-fs isolation: grants are scoped by fsname and every MClientSession from an entity without a grant for the MDSMap fs gets CEPH_SESSION_REJECT with error_string (libcephfs mount fails EPERM).

group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
name: uid=/gids= restriction with simplified mode-bit check
why: The monitor accepts uid=/gids= grants; ignoring them would widen access, so the simplified owner/group/other mode-bit check (and the chown/chgrp rules) must be enforced as in C++.
risk: C++ intersects the caller gid list assuming it is sorted; sort it first.

group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
name: root_squash grants
why: fs authorize and the dashboard generate root_squash grants; the MDS skips them for writes by uid 0 or gid 0 (vxattr ops excluded) and clients enforce them locally from cap_auths.

group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
name: p flag: permission to set ceph.* vxattrs and non-default layouts
why: Tenant isolation: subvolume authorize grants `allow rw path=...` without p, so tenants cannot change quotas, layouts, pins or ceph.dir.subvolume; mgr (allow *) and mirror bootstrap (rwps) rely on holding p.
risk: Without the p check a tenant can raise its own quota or repin its subvolume.

group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
name: s flag and snapshot uid range
why: The s flag and the snap uid range only gate MKSNAP/RMSNAP/RENAMESNAP and SNAP_METADATA, which come with snapshots (D8: P0 refuses MKSNAP with EPERM); the flag is parsed in P0 (F-ADM-006).
risk: SNAP_METADATA must stay caps-unchecked (uid range only) because cephfs-mirror runs with `allow r`.

group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
name: f flag: metadata-pool-full bypass
why: When the metadata pool is full only grants with f (allow *: mgr, admin) may run growth ops, so operators can clean up; part of the full-pool policy (F-STORE-099).
subset: MAY_FULL check on the request's base inode for SETLAYOUT, SETDIRLAYOUT, SETXATTR, RMXATTR, CREATE, SYMLINK, MKSNAP, LINK, RENAME while the metadata pool is FULL; a single reply (no C++ duplicate reply).
question: Which errno for the denial: -EACCES (what clients see from C++ today) or -ENOSPC (documented in full.rst)?

group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
name: q/Q flags: access to quarantined subtrees
why: q/Q only matter for quarantined subtrees (D12: quarantine P2); the letters are parsed in P0 (F-ADM-006) and have no effect until then.
risk: C++ first-match pitfall: a matching grant lacking q denies before later grants are consulted.

group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
name: network restriction
why: The monitor accepts `network CIDR` qualifiers; ignoring them would grant access from any address, so the session address must be matched (same family, an unparseable network makes the grant unusable).

name: Mount root check at session open and auth_name check at reclaim
why: REQUEST_OPEN with a `root` outside every grant path gets REJECT ('non-allowable root'), and Ganesha's reclaim of another session requires the same cephx entity (-EPERM otherwise).
subset: REJECT without error_string to pre-MIMIC sessions is legacy and out.

name: Per-request access-check matrix
why: Defines which inode and mask each client op is checked against; this is the server-side enforcement behind path-restricted tenants (CSI, Manila, NFS exports).
subset: The -EIO for clients without FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2 and the undefined Server::_check_access are legacy and out.
risk: Do not share one access decision across sessions (C++ batched getattr/lookup sends the head's result to other sessions); LOOKUPINO answered on any rank needs the inode path for the mask-0 match (Ganesha handles).
question: Keep the C++ unchecked ops (RMXATTR of user xattrs, GETVXATTR, file locks, FILE_BLOCKDIFF) or close the RMXATTR gap? SNAP_METADATA must stay caps-unchecked for cephfs-mirror.

name: fscrypt attribute changes require allow *
why: fscrypt is P2 (D12); the allow_all gate on SETATTR with FSCRYPT_AUTH/FILE comes with it (mgr/volumes clones, P1, copy ceph.fscrypt.* attrs).
risk: Until then decide what a SETATTR carrying fscrypt flags returns.

name: cap_auths export in CEPH_SESSION_OPEN and client-side checks
why: The 7.3 kernel (bit 21) and libcephfs enforce read-only and root_squash locally from the cap_auths list carried in every CEPH_SESSION_OPEN; the kernel parses the v1 MDSCapAuth layout positionally and replaces its mount-wide list on each OPEN from any rank.
subset: OPEN header v1 without cap_auths for pre-MIMIC clients is legacy and out.
risk: Appending a field to MDSCapAuth/MDSCapMatch desynchronizes the kernel; an OPEN with an empty list (C++ force-opened import sessions) disables kernel checks, so sessions opened by shard migration (D6) must carry the real grants.

name: MDS_CLIENTS_BROKEN_ROOTSQUASH health check
why: Legacy: raised only for clients lacking feature bit 21 (kernels before 6.10, Ceph clients before 18.2.4/19.2.0); no baseline client triggers it.

group: Caps provisioning by the monitor and mgr
name: ceph fs authorize: cap generation and merge on the monitor
why: The unchanged monitor generates and merges mds caps (fsname=, path=, root_squash, r w p s q Q) for operators, the dashboard and mirror bootstrap; the MDS must accept and enforce every string it produces.
subset: No MDS code beyond parser and evaluator compatibility (F-ADM-006, F-ADM-007).

group: Caps provisioning by the monitor and mgr
name: mgr/volumes subvolume authorize, deauthorize and authorized_list
why: Default mgr/volumes flow for tenants: grants `allow r|rw path=<data path>` without fsname and serializes its /volumes/*.meta bookkeeping with blocking flock(LOCK_EX), O_CREAT opens and in-place rewrites.
risk: The bookkeeping files live in the root shard (D3), so blocking flock must work there.

group: Caps provisioning by the monitor and mgr
name: mgr/nfs export user caps
why: Each NFS export runs as a dedicated user with `allow rw path=<cmount_path>`; Ganesha's handle-based access (LOOKUPINO) is constrained only by the mask-0 path match.
risk: LOOKUPINO answered on any rank (D6) must still evaluate the path match.

name: Local admin socket transport
why: ceph-exporter (deployed by cephadm per host and Rook per node) and `ceph daemon` use the asok: NUL/newline-terminated JSON, 4-byte big-endian length reply, default path $run_dir/$cluster-$name.asok.
subset: Legacy binary request protocol (leading NUL, codes 0/1/2) is out.
risk: Under Rook the socket must resolve inside /run/ceph (default /var/run/ceph/ceph-mds.<id>.asok) or the exporter never scrapes it.

name: Remote tell transport (MCommand / MCommandReply)
why: `ceph tell mds.X`, mgr modules (volumes evict, dashboard, stats) and libcephfs mds_command use MCommand/MCommandReply (errno on the wire, tid echo, out-of-order async replies); rankless daemons answer daemon-level commands and -ENOSYS for rank commands.
subset: Legacy MMonCommand ('mds tell' via the monitor) is out.

name: Tell authorization: allow * required
why: mgr (allow *), client.admin and Rook's csi-cephfs-provisioner (client eviction) run tell commands; other callers must get -EACCES 'permission denied'.
question: C++ allow_all() ignores the grant's fsname= and network; keep that or require the fsname to match the daemon's fs (stricter, no current peer affected)?

name: Command self-description (get_command_descriptions, help)
why: The ceph CLI fetches get_command_descriptions before every tell or daemon command and splits arguments by descriptor type; without it no CLI command reaches the MDS.
subset: Descriptors (Ceph descriptor grammar) for every implemented command, plus help.

name: Argument validation, output formats, output-file and return-code conventions
why: Peers parse the JSON output (dashboard and stats expect `session ls` as a bare array, volumes checks rc) and send command maps with extra keys.
subset: json and json-pretty (default) with the C++ JSON shapes (no top-level section names), cmdmap validation (-EINVAL), unknown keys ignored, rc/return_code conventions of the implemented commands; xml/table/html formats and output-file are P2.

name: Client-side target resolution for tell (libcephfs mds_command)
why: The CLI, mgr modules and libcephfs resolve mds.<name>, gid, <fs>:<rank> and * against the FSMap; the MDS only needs correct FSMap entries (addrs, gid, name, rank, state, laggy_since).
subset: No dedicated MDS code; covered by beacons and the FSMap (category CLU).

group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
name: status command
why: Operator essential (D13); qa waits on status.state and docs read recovery progress from it.
subset: cluster_fsid, whoami, id, want_state, state, fs_name, rank_uptime, mdsmap_epoch, osdmap_epoch, osdmap_epoch_barrier, uptime, sysinfo; per-phase recovery status reports per-shard progress instead of C++ journal positions.

group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
name: Process control commands: exit, respawn, lockup
why: Used by qa and the libcephfs reclaim test, not by mgr, cephadm or Rook default flows; supervisors restart the process anyway.
subset: exit and respawn (new process identity); lockup (sleeps holding mds_lock) dropped.

group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
name: heap and cpu_profiler commands
why: Only opt-in telemetry (perf_memory_metrics) sends `heap stats` and it only logs failures; tcmalloc and gperftools are C++ process specifics.
subset: Return -EOPNOTSUPP ('not using tcmalloc'), as a C++ build without tcmalloc does.

group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
name: Op tracker dumps (ops, dump_ops_in_flight, blocked and historic ops)
why: dump_ops_in_flight is an operator essential (D13, documented); blocked and historic dumps back slow-request diagnosis and qa TestValidTell.
subset: dump_ops_in_flight, dump_blocked_ops(_count), dump_historic_ops(_by_duration) with ops[]{description, initiated_at, age, duration, type_data{flag_point, reqid, op_type, events[]}}; `ops --flags=locks` (C++ lock dump) dropped.

group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
name: op get and op kill
why: Only qa uses op get/op kill (also as the release of the lock path and quiesce path test ops); no peer sends them.

group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
name: session ls / client ls
why: The dashboard (session ls to <fscid>:0) and mgr/stats (client ls to rank 0) parse it, and operators use it to find clients to evict (D13).
subset: Bare JSON array; per client session: id, auth_name, entity, inst, state, num_caps, num_leases, request_load_avg, uptime, requests_in_flight, num_completed_requests, num_completed_flushes, reconnecting, client_metadata{client_features{feature_bits}, metric_spec{metric_flags{feature_bits}}, every metadata key verbatim}; same filters as session evict; C++ recall/decay internals, prealloc and delegated inos optional.
risk: mgr/stats indexes client_metadata.hostname, .root and metric_spec.metric_flags.feature_bits without defaults: one session lacking them aborts processing of the whole reply.

group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
name: session evict / client evict / session kill and the session filter grammar
why: Operator essential and peer-critical: mgr/volumes subvolume evict (auth_name= + client_metadata.root=), the dashboard (id=) and the ceph-csi provisioner; eviction blocklists the client, waits for the OSDMap and raises the epoch barrier before killing the session.
subset: Filters id=, bare id, auth_name=, client_metadata.<key>=, state=, reconnecting=; -EAGAIN while replaying; session kill (blocking variant) optional.
risk: A client can hold sessions on several ranks; each rank must evict its own.

group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
name: session config / client config timeout
why: Admin override of the per-session `timeout` metadata; Ganesha sets the key itself (F-PROTO-046), only qa and operators use the command.

group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
name: flush journal
why: Operator essential (D13: flush journal-equivalent), documented maintenance step and the most used qa command; reply {message, return_code} with rc = return_code.
subset: Semantics: make every shard's journal durable and checkpointed (F-STORE-020); no C++ segment format.

group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
name: flush_path
why: qa only (test_scrub_checks); writing back one inode and its dirfrag is a C++ cache concept.
subset: Flush the shard that owns the path; reply {message, return_code}.

group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
name: force_readonly
why: Operator and qa command; the read-only mode it triggers (FORCE_RO to clients, MDS_READ_ONLY) is P0 through the write-error policy (F-STORE-100), so the command is cheap once that exists.

group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
name: osdmap barrier
why: Only qa sets the OSD epoch barrier by hand; the barrier mechanism itself is P0 (F-STORE-098).

group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
name: cache drop
why: Documented operator action to shrink an MDS cache (recall caps from all clients, flush, trim); no peer default flow uses it.
risk: C++ asserts when the journal flush fails (read-only rank); report the error instead.

group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
name: cache status and dump cache
why: `cache status` lets operators compare cache memory with mds_cache_memory_limit; `dump cache` dumps C++ objects and stalls the rank.
subset: cache status {pool:{items, bytes}}; dump cache dropped.

group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
name: Cache and table dumps: dump tree, dump inode, dump dir, openfiles ls, dump snaps
why: Debug and qa dumps of C++ cache, open-file and snap tables (D13: C++-internal dumps OUT or P2); only a by-inode lookup helps operators diagnose damage.
subset: dump inode <ino> (path and attributes, new format); dump tree, dump dir, openfiles ls and dump snaps not implemented.
risk: qa test_volumes reads old_inodes from `dump inode` (C++ snapshot format) and will not run unchanged.

group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
name: dump stray
why: Documented troubleshooting for space that is not reclaimed; strays and purge are P0 but listing them is diagnosis only.
subset: Per-shard stray listing (ino, prior path, client caps) in a new format.

group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
name: Scrub control commands (scrub start, abort, pause, resume, status, purge_status)
why: Online scrub and repair are P1 (D10); docs and qa drive them with `ceph tell mds.<fs>:0 scrub start|status|abort|pause|resume`.
subset: scrub_path and scrub_start remnants are out.

group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
name: tag path and the scrub_tag xattr
why: D10: C++ scrub tags and the scrub_tag xattr are OUT; the only reader is cephfs-data-scan --filter-tag, a C++ offline tool (OUT by D2).

group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
name: damage ls and damage rm
why: Damage containment is P0 (D10) and MDS_DAMAGE (HEALTH_ERR) blocks Rook reconciles and fires alerts; operators need damage ls to find damaged metadata and damage rm to clear entries after repair.
subset: damage ls (array of id, damage_type, ino, path or shard where known) and damage rm <id>, per rank; entry format new.

group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
name: Multi-MDS inspection and control: get subtrees, dump loads, export dir, dump_export_states
why: No peer uses them (qa only); with whole-shard placement an equivalent shard-map dump and manual shard move help operators check pins and rebalance.
subset: get subtrees -> shard placement dump (shard root, owner rank, pins); export dir -> move one shard to a rank; dump loads and dump_export_states dropped (no balancer, D5).

group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
name: dirfrag split, merge and ls
why: D5: no client-visible fragmentation, every directory reports one frag; only qa uses dirfrag split/merge/ls.

group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
name: lock path and quiesce path test hooks
why: qa test hooks: lock path names C++ lock types (D16) and quiesce path belongs to quiesce (D12: P2).
subset: quiesce path (released by op kill) only if quiesce is built; lock path out.

group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
name: quiesce db command
why: Quiesce is P2 (D12); mgr/volumes `fs quiesce` sends quiesce db to mdsmap.qdb_leader and follows -ENOTTY {leader}.
risk: Until then `fs quiesce` fails; no default cephadm or Rook flow uses it.

group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
name: quarantine enable / disable command
why: Quarantine is P2 (D12); mgr/volumes sends `quarantine enable|disable path=` to the first active rank.
risk: The rank mgr/volumes picks (normally rank 0) must reach the shard owner instead of returning -EXDEV as C++ does.

group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
name: QoS commands (dump qos, qos set, qos rm, qos get)
why: dmClock admin surface (D11), superseded by per-shard fair scheduling; no mgr module or orchestrator consumes it.
question: Per-subvolume SLA and rate limiting (a motivating use case) needs its own admin surface: reuse the `dump qos`/`qos set|get|rm` names or define new ones?

group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
name: Generic process commands: perf, counter, config, log, injectargs
why: ceph-exporter needs counter dump/schema and config show (pid_file); operators need perf dump, config get/set/diff and injectargs (D13); qa uses perf dump heavily.
subset: perf dump [logger [counter]], perf schema, counter dump, counter schema, config show|get|set|unset|diff|help, injectargs; perf reset and log flush|reopen P2; legacy perfcounters_dump/schema, 1, 2 out; assert, abort, leak_some_memory, raise, messenger dump, objecter_requests, perf histogram dropped.

group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
name: dump_mempools
why: Only opt-in telemetry (perf_memory_metrics) reads dump_mempools and it only logs failures; mempools are a C++ allocator concept.
subset: Return {mempool:{by_pool:{}, total:{items, bytes}}} or -EOPNOTSUPP.

group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
name: Version and ping built-ins (0, version, git_version)
why: ceph-exporter pings every socket with {"prefix":"0"} and expects the 1-byte reply "2" (else ceph_daemon_socket_up 0); version and git_version are trivial and used by qa.

name: MDS option catalogue and option metadata
why: The unmodified monitor validates `ceph config set` against its compiled C++ option table, and operators, docs, cephadm and Rook use C++ option names, so options the Rust MDS honours must keep those names and types where the meaning carries over.
subset: Honour mds_cache_memory_limit, mds_join_fs, mds_session_blocklist_on_evict/_on_timeout, session and recall limits, mds_max_snaps_per_dir, mds_op_complaint_time, mds_health_* thresholds, journal trim limits; ignore C++-internal options.

name: Runtime config observer and per-subsystem fan-out
why: Runtime `ceph config set` and `tell config set` must reach the running MDS and apply runtime-updatable options; the C++ observer, tracked-key list and finisher are internal.
risk: Do not reproduce the C++ ignored-runtime-change bugs (F-ADM-063).

name: Config delivery from the monitor config DB and reporting to the mgr
why: Rook and cephadm write per-daemon options (mds_join_fs, mds_cache_memory_limit) to the mon config DB, delivered by MConfig; `ceph config show mds.<id>` is served from the config sent in MMgrOpen/MMgrReport.
subset: Ignore unknown option names in MConfig; the pre-Pacific blacklist renames (mon side) are out.

name: Option apply-class anomalies
why: C++ defects (misspelled tracked keys, values ignored at startup, unused options); nothing to replicate.

name: MDS option names read or written by peers
why: cephadm and Rook set mds_join_fs (Rook also mds_cache_memory_limit per pod) on every reconcile, cephadm memory autotune subtracts mds_cache_memory_limit, and snap_schedule reads mds_max_snaps_per_dir.
risk: If mds_cache_memory_limit is not the real memory bound, Rook pods (limit x 0.5) are OOM-killed.

name: Fault injection, killpoints and debug options
why: C++ dev options that crash or corrupt C++ internals for qa; the Rust MDS needs its own failpoint framework.
question: qa jobs that set these options will not run unchanged: port them to Rust failpoints?

name: Unlabeled MDS perf counter loggers
why: mgr/status, the dashboard, telemetry, ceph-exporter and the shipped Grafana dashboards read specific mds* counter names; the rest are C++ internals.
subset: Loggers mds, mds_mem, mds_server, mds_cache, mds_log, mds_sessions with the peer-read names (summary list) at priority >= 5 with correct type and unit; C++-internal counters (traverse_*, dir_split/merge, replication, scrub_*, oft.*) dropped or left at 0.
question: Map C++-specific names onto the new design (mds.subtrees = shards owned, mds_log.seg = journal segments) or leave them at 0?

name: Counter reporting to the mgr and the names mgr modules read
why: mgr/status and the dashboard read counters from MMgrReport (priority >= mgr_stats_threshold 5, every stats_period); declarations carry path, nick, type, priority and unit.
subset: mds.exported/imported (DEBUGONLY) and mds_log.replay (nonexistent) need not be sent.

name: Labeled perf counter families (client, subvolume and rank metrics)
why: Client and subvolume labeled families come with metrics aggregation (D11: subvolume metrics P1); mds_rank_perf (cpu_usage, open_requests) feeds the shipped Grafana CephFS dashboard.
question: Pull mds_rank_perf into P0 for the Grafana CephFS dashboard (cheap, per rank)?

name: Admin-socket counter dump and schema JSON format
why: ceph-exporter parses counter dump/schema (type bitmask, metric_type, value_type, priority, units; LONGRUNAVG as {avgcount, sum, avgtime}); operators and qa parse perf dump.

name: Prometheus export through ceph-exporter
why: ceph-exporter is deployed by default by cephadm and Rook: it pings, reads counter dump/schema (priority >= 5) and config show (pid_file), and labels series ceph_daemon=mds.<id>, which dashboards join with ceph_mds_metadata.

name: Memory gauges and gauge refresh cadence
why: mds_mem.{ino,dn,dir,cap} feed fs status and the dashboard; mds_mem.rss and heap feed the Grafana memory panel.
subset: rss (KiB) and heap (bytes) sampled periodically; ino/dn/dir/cap as counts of cached inodes, dentries, directories and caps refreshed at least every tick; `+`/`-` lifetime counters optional.

name: Grafana dashboards and Prometheus alerts shipped with Ceph
why: cephadm deploys Prometheus and Grafana with these dashboards and alerts by default; they query fixed ceph_mds_* names and health codes.
