risk: Missing names leave Grafana panels silently empty.

group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
name: Health metric pipeline (MDSHealth in beacons to monitor checks)
why: The unmodified monitor turns MDSHealth metrics carried in beacons into the health checks seen by operators, Rook's gate, cephadm and alerts.
subset: Only ids 1..17, never 0; per-client metrics summarised above mds_health_summarize_threshold; recomputed periodically from current state.
risk: A type-0 metric aborts the decoding monitor; each change of (type, sev, message) costs a mon proposal and an MDSMap epoch pushed to every client, so keep messages stable.

group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
name: MDS_TRIM: behind on trimming
why: Operator signal that the journal grows faster than it is trimmed (replay time); the mon refuses mds fail/fs fail on a daemon reporting it.
subset: Keep code MDS_TRIM, WARN, 'Behind on trimming (N/M)' and num_segments/max_segments; trigger on per-shard journal backlog.

group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
name: Client-behaviour warnings: late cap release, cache-pressure recall, oldest tid
why: Operators identify clients that do not release caps, ignore cache-pressure recall or do not advance their oldest tid, and evict them; essential when one tenant's client can block others.

group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
name: MDS_SLOW_REQUEST and slow-request detection
why: Main operator signal for stuck metadata operations, used together with dump_ops_in_flight; matching 'slow request' cluster-log lines.

group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
name: MDS_SLOW_METADATA_IO and slow RADOS IO detection
why: Tells operators the MDS is blocked on RADOS (OSD rather than MDS problem); threshold osd_op_complaint_time.

group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
name: MDS_DAMAGE and MDS_READ_ONLY state warnings
why: Damage containment (D10) and read-only mode on write errors must be visible; alerts key on MDS_DAMAGE and Rook stops reconciling while it is raised at HEALTH_ERR.
question: Shard-contained damage at HEALTH_ERR stops Rook reconciles of every CR in the cluster namespace: keep ERR (C++, alerts) or report per-shard damage at WARN?

group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
name: MDS_CACHE_OVERSIZED
why: Signals cache memory above mds_cache_memory_limit x mds_health_cache_threshold (Rook derives the limit from pod memory); the mon refuses mds fail/fs fail on a daemon reporting it.

group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
name: MDS_CLIENTS_LAGGY: evictions deferred because of laggy OSDs
why: Raised only with defer_client_eviction_on_laggy_osds (default false); follows the optional eviction deferral (F-PROTO-047).

group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
name: MDS_ESTIMATED_REPLAY_TIME
why: Progress of replays longer than 30 s; per-shard replay should be short, and qa parses the message text.
subset: Keep code and 'replay: P% complete - elapsed time: Es, estimated time remaining: Rs'; compute over the shards being replayed.

group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
name: Monitor-derived file-system health checks
why: Computed by the unchanged monitor from the FSMap (FS_DEGRADED, MDS_UP_LESS_THAN_MAX, MDS_ALL_DOWN, FS_WITH_FAILED_MDS, MDS_INSUFFICIENT_STANDBY, damaged-rank MDS_DAMAGE); alerts, Rook and cephadm key on them and they are right only if beacon states are right.
subset: No dedicated MDS code; MULTIMDS_WITH_OLDSNAPS, FS_INLINE_DATA_DEPRECATED and the dead legacy summaries are out.

group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
name: Health-gated monitor commands
why: The mon refuses unconfirmed `fs set max_mds` while any MDS reports any metric, and `mds fail`/`fs fail` while a target reports TRIM or CACHE_OVERSIZED; Rook sends all three unconfirmed and a refusal aborts its MDS upgrade.
subset: Report metrics only for real, current conditions; never a permanent informational metric.
risk: A spurious or sticky metric blocks Rook upgrades and scaling.

group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
name: Cluster log (clog) messages
why: Operators read evictions, session denials, slow requests, write and journal errors and damage in the cluster log; qa ignorelists match the wording.
subset: Evictions ('Evicting (and blocklisting) client session N (addr)'), session open denials, slow requests, late cap release and oldest-tid warnings, write/journal errors, damage, force read-only; flush the log before an abort; clog_to_monitors routing.

group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
name: Scrub task status in the mgr service map
why: Comes with online scrub (D10: P1); `ceph -s` shows 'scrub status' from the mgr service map and qa polls it.

group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
name: In-memory log dump on extraordinary events
why: Debug aid that dumps the C++ in-memory log ring after evictions or missed beacons; a Rust tracing ring can offer the same, no peer depends on it.

name: mgr libcephfs connection pool and mount identity
why: Every mgr module (volumes, nfs, snap_schedule, mirroring, dashboard) mounts as mgr.<id> with uid/gid 0: many concurrent sessions per entity, sessions abandoned with abort_conn, old-mgr addresses blocklisted on failover.
risk: Abandoned and blocklisted mgr sessions must be reaped (stale, autoclose) without blocking other tenants.

name: mgr/volumes: volume lifecycle (fs volume create, rm, rename, ls, info)
why: `fs volume create/rm/rename/ls/info` is the default way to create file systems; the MDS sees fs new/fail/rm/rename through the FSMap and serves statx(/volumes) (dir size = rbytes) and readdir of /volumes/_deleting.

name: mgr/volumes: in-filesystem layout, .meta files, versions, user metadata, open side effects
why: mgr/volumes keeps all state as files under /volumes in the root shard (D3): .meta rewritten via .tmp + fsync + rename over the old file, symlink indexes, auth .meta files; every subvolume open re-sets ceph.dir.subvolume=1 and stats paths.
subset: v1 to v2 .meta upgrade (old data) is out.
risk: setxattr ceph.dir.subvolume=1 on an existing shard root (every `fs subvolume info`) must be an idempotent cheap no-op, not a shard re-creation.

name: mgr/volumes: subvolume groups
why: Rook creates group csi and CephFilesystemSubVolumeGroup groups (create, resize --no-shrink, pin distributed, rm); groups are root-shard dirs needing mkdir, rmdir ENOTEMPTY, chown/chmod, quota, layout pool and pin vxattrs.
subset: Group charmap options are P2 (D12).
risk: Group create copies the nearest ancestor's ceph.dir.layout.pool, so / must expose a layout.

name: mgr/volumes: subvolume create
why: The core default flow (ceph-csi under Rook, Manila, dashboard): mkdirs, setxattr ceph.dir.subvolume=1 (shard root creation, D3/D4), quota, layout pool/namespace, chown, chmod, an earmark write, then .meta files.
subset: Charmap and enctag only when requested; fscrypt attrs only for clones (P1).
risk: Fails if a zero-length user xattr cannot be stored or / exposes no layout; verify in the mgr code that normalization/casesensitive are set only on request (charmap is P2).

name: mgr/volumes: removal, trash, snapshot retention and asynchronous purge
why: `fs subvolume rm` renames the subvolume base dir into /volumes/_deleting (a shard-root rename in the root shard, D4) and 4 purge threads delete its contents with client unlink/rmdir traffic.
subset: rm without snapshots, trash rename and rmtree purge; --retain-snapshots and .trash incarnations come with snapshots (P1).
risk: rmtree relies on rmdir of a directory with snapshots failing ENOTEMPTY (P1); path= grants of the old location stop matching after the trash rename.

name: mgr/volumes: subvolume resize via quota
why: `fs subvolume resize` sets ceph.quota.max_bytes (0 removes) and reports bytes_used from directory st_size (rstat rbytes through libcephfs); Rook resizes groups with --no-shrink.

name: mgr/volumes: subvolume and group pinning
why: D6: export and distributed pins on subvolumes and groups are shard placement hints; Rook pins every CephFilesystemSubVolumeGroup `distributed 1` by default.
subset: ceph.dir.pin (rank, negative unsets, >= 256 EDOM) and ceph.dir.pin.distributed honoured as placement hints with the C++ validation errors; ceph.dir.pin.random accepted and ignored (D12).

name: mgr/volumes: charmap (case sensitivity, normalization, encoding)
why: Charmap and case-insensitivity are P2 (D12); used only when an operator asks for them at create or with `fs subvolume charmap`.
question: What does P0 return for ceph.dir.casesensitive/normalization/encoding (EOPNOTSUPP or EINVAL)? Confirm mgr/volumes sets them only on request.

name: mgr/volumes and mgr/nfs: earmark and enctag xattrs
why: Subvolume create always writes user.ceph.subvolume.earmark (empty if none) and mgr/nfs checks or sets it at export creation, so zero-length user xattr values must be stored and returned.

name: mgr/volumes: subvolume snapshots
why: Snapshots are P1 (D8); in P0 MKSNAP returns EPERM (as with allow_new_snaps off), so `fs subvolume snapshot create` fails cleanly and ls is empty.

name: mgr/volumes: snapshot visibility
why: Controls .snap visibility per subvolume; only meaningful with snapshots (D8).
risk: In P0 accept ceph.dir.subvolume.snaps.visible on realm roots (store or C++-style no-op) so the command does not fail.

name: mgr/volumes: snapshot clone
why: Clones copy from snapshots (D8: P1) and need readable snapshot data, rstat of snapshot inodes, symlink st_size/ctime ordering and the _index/clone symlinks.

name: mgr/volumes: fs subvolume evict
why: mgr/volumes evicts a tenant's clients from every up rank with filters auth_name= and client_metadata.root= (exact match), retrying on -ETIMEDOUT; part of the deauthorize flow.
risk: client_metadata.root must be stored verbatim; each up rank must reach up:active or up:clientreplay within about 35 s.

name: mgr/volumes: fs quiesce
why: Quiesce is P2 (D12).

name: mgr/volumes: subvolume quarantine
why: Quarantine is P2 (D12).

name: mgr/snap_schedule: scheduled snapshots and retention
why: Scheduled snapshots are P1 (D8); the module stores its SQLite DB in the metadata pool and reads mds_max_snaps_per_dir.
subset: Legacy snap_db_v0 import is out.
risk: The MDS must never touch snap_db_v0.db* objects in the metadata pool (F-STORE-102).

name: mgr/mirroring: enable, peers, bootstrap and directory distribution
why: Snapshot mirroring is P1 (D8); needs ceph.mirror.info on the remote root (raw xattrs, XATTR_CREATE -> EEXIST) and coexistence with the cephfs_mirror objects in the metadata pool.

name: mgr/mirroring: checkpoints through snapshot metadata
why: Mirror checkpoints use SNAP_METADATA on snapshots (P1, D8), which must stay caps-unchecked except for the uid range.

name: mgr/stats: fs perf stats (and cephfs-top)
why: D13 lists stats: `fs perf stats` and cephfs-top need the client ls fields and rank 0 answering mgr perf queries for per-rank client keys and the global client counters 0-15.
subset: client ls schema; rank-0 answers to the per-rank and global client queries; the subvolume query (counters 16-21) is P1 (D11).
risk: Never send a metric report type other than 0/1 (the mgr aborts); clients without a session on rank 0 are missing from the output, so mounts should reach rank 0 (e.g. root shard on rank 0).
question: D11 says client metrics 'tolerate at least' while D13 makes the stats flow P0: confirm rank-0 aggregation of global client metrics (F-QOS-028..030) is P0.
override: Same as F-QOS-012: the stats module must be enabled explicitly.

name: mgr/status: fs status
why: `ceph fs status` (always-on status module) reads mds_mem.{dn,ino,dir,cap}, mds_sessions.session_count, the rates of mds_server.handle_client_request and mds_log.replayed, and ceph_version from mds metadata.

name: mgr/dashboard: CephFS pages
why: Dashboard CephFS pages read counters, list (session ls) and evict (client evict id=) clients on <fscid>:0, run fs authorize and browse files through libcephfs.
subset: Counters mds_server.handle_client_request, mds_log.ev, mds_cache.num_strays, mds.{inodes,caps,subtrees,exported_inodes,imported_inodes}, mds_mem.ino; client list/evict; file browser and quotas; snapshot pages need P1.

name: mgr/prometheus: MDS and file-system metadata metrics
why: Enabled with the default monitoring stack: ceph_mds_metadata (boot-beacon hostname, ceph_version, public_addr, rank, fs_id), ceph_fs_metadata and ceph_health_detail; perf counters are excluded by default.
subset: No dedicated MDS code beyond boot metadata (CLU) and health codes.

name: mgr/telemetry: MDS data collection
why: Opt-in reporting; the basic channel reads counters that are P0 anyway plus rank-0 root rstat gauges, and the perf channel only logs failures of heap stats and dump_mempools.
subset: mds.root_rfiles/root_rbytes/root_rsnaps on rank 0; heap and dump_mempools P2.

name: mgr/mds_autoscaler
why: Never talks to the MDS: sets the orchestrator daemon count to max_mds + standby_count_wanted from the FSMap, so it works if the FSMap is right and the MDS tolerates daemons added or removed on each max_mds change.
subset: No dedicated MDS code.

name: mgr/nfs: CephFS exports
why: Default NFS flow: validates the export path with statx, checks or sets the earmark, creates the per-export user (allow rw path=); Ganesha then mounts through libcephfs (delegations off, rados_cluster recovery).

name: cephadm MDS deployment
why: cephadm runs /usr/bin/ceph-mds -n mds.<id> -f --setuser ceph --setgroup ceph --default-log-* with the keyring in /var/lib/ceph/mds/ceph-<id>, /etc/ceph/ceph.conf, the run dir for the asok, and caps mon 'profile mds', osd 'allow rw tag cephfs *=*', mds 'allow'.
risk: All MDS RADOS objects must live in pools tagged cephfs (osd cap), and mon config-key access is limited to daemon-private/mds.<id>/.

name: cephadm MDS upgrade choreography
why: Upgrades clear allow_standby_replay, set max_mds 1 (ranks > 0 stop and hand off their shards, D6) or fs fail, wait on mds ok-to-stop, redeploy, check `ceph versions`, then restore max_mds or joinable.
risk: A ceph_version with fewer than three space-separated fields raises IndexError in the upgrade loop.

name: Rook operator: MDS pods, command line, keyring, config and probes
why: Rook starts ceph-mds via PATH with --fsid, --keyring, --default-log/err/mon-cluster-log flags, --mon-host (bracketed addrvecs), --mon-initial-members, --id=<fs>-<letter>, --setuser/--setgroup, --foreground and --public-addr, an empty mds_data, SIGTERM stop and SIGHUP log reopen; liveness = name present in fs dump.
risk: The FSMap name must equal --id; stopping must send a DNE beacon (Rook waits only on the FSMap); the image must ship bash, jq and the ceph CLI for the probe.

name: Rook operator: upgrade order, ok-to-stop gate and health gating
why: Rook compares each MDS ceph_version ('ceph version X.Y.Z-B (sha) ...') with the image's `ceph --version`: an older or different-commit string reruns the max_mds 1 upgrade on every reconcile, an unparsable one fails every reconcile; HEALTH_ERR checks other than MDS_ALL_DOWN/AUTH_* stop reconciles.
question: The Rust MDS must report the exact Ceph version string (same commit id) of the image it ships in: decide packaging and version reporting.

name: cephfs-mirror daemon
why: Snapshot mirroring is P1 (D8): snapdiff, blockdiff (feature bit 23), SNAP_METADATA under `allow r`, flock LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB on remote dir roots, the ceph.mirror.dirty_snap_id plain xattr and sync_fs.

name: Offline journal and table tools (cephfs-journal-tool, cephfs-table-tool)
why: D2: bound to the C++ journal and table encodings; cannot operate on the new on-disk format.
question: Provide Rust-native disaster-recovery tools (journal inspect/reset, table reset) as P1/P2?

name: Offline data and metadata repair tools (cephfs-data-scan, cephfs-meta-injection, first-damage.py)
why: D2: cephfs-data-scan, cephfs-meta-injection and first-damage.py parse C++ backtrace, dirfrag omap and snaptable encodings.
question: Recovery from lost metadata needs a Rust equivalent of data-scan (purpose P1/P2 redesign if the new format keeps data-object backtraces)?

name: Client-side tools: cephfs-tool bench and cephfs-shell
why: cephfs-tool bench and cephfs-shell use only libcephfs and work once the client protocol works; cephfs-shell du reads ceph.dir.rbytes, quotas work, snapshots fail with EPERM until P1.
subset: No dedicated MDS code.
